name: Donald J. Trump
education: Graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 1968 with a bachelor's degree in economics.
careerHistory: President of the United States (2017–2021; since 2025). President of his family's real estate business, renamed The Trump Organization, starting in 1971. Host of the reality television show The Apprentice from 2004 to 2015.
bio:
Donald John Trump (born June 14, 1946) is an American politician, media personality, and businessman who is the 47th president of the United States. A member of the Republican Party, he previously served as the 45th president from 2017 to 2021. Born into a wealthy New York City family, Trump graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 1968 with a bachelor's degree in economics. He became president of his family's real estate business in 1971, renamed it the Trump Organization, and expanded into skyscrapers, hotels, casinos, and golf courses. From 2004 to 2015, he hosted the reality television show The Apprentice. Presenting himself as a political outsider, Trump won the 2016 presidential election against Democratic nominee Hillary Clinton.

During his first term, Trump's domestic policies included imposing a travel ban on seven Muslim-majority countries, expanding the Mexico–United States border wall, enforcing a family separation policy on the border, rolling back environmental and business regulations, and signing the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. He appointed three Supreme Court justices. In foreign policy, he withdrew the U.S. from agreements on climate (Paris Agreement), trade, and Iran's nuclear program, and initiated a trade war with China. He signed the CARES Act in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, which he downplayed. After losing the 2020 presidential election to Joe Biden, Trump attempted to overturn the result, culminating in the January 6 Capitol attack. He was impeached in 2019 for abuse of power and obstruction of Congress, and in 2021 for incitement of insurrection; the Senate acquitted him both times.

In 2023, Trump was found liable in civil cases for sexual abuse and defamation and for business fraud. He was found guilty in 2024 on 34 counts of falsifying business records, becoming the first U.S. president convicted of a felony. After winning the 2024 presidential election against Kamala Harris, he was sentenced to a discharge, and two felony indictments for retention of classified documents and obstruction of the 2020 election were dismissed without prejudice.

Trump began his second presidency in 2025 by initiating mass layoffs of federal workers, imposing high tariffs, and signing the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. His administration's actions, including targeting political opponents and civil society, have drawn over 550 lawsuits. His leadership style and political agenda, often called Trumpism, have reshaped the Republican Party. Many of his comments and actions have been characterized as racist or misogynistic. He has made many false or misleading statements and promotes conspiracy theories. His actions, especially in his second term, have been described as authoritarian and contributing to democratic backsliding. Scholars and historians have ranked him as one of the worst presidents in American history.

name: J.D. Vance
education: Earned a Bachelor of Arts summa cum laude in political science and philosophy from Ohio State University in 2009 and a Juris Doctor from Yale Law School in 2013.
careerHistory: Enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps (2003-2007). Worked as a corporate lawyer at Sidley Austin after law school. Served as a venture capitalist and principal at Mithril Capital (2016-2017). Served as U.S. Senator from Ohio (2023-2025). Became the 50th Vice President of the United States in 2025.
bio:
James David Vance, known as J.D. Vance, is an American politician and author serving as the 50th vice president of the United States since 2025. A member of the Republican Party, he previously represented Ohio in the United States Senate from 2023 to 2025. Born James Donald Bowman on August 2, 1984, in Middletown, Ohio, he was raised in an Appalachian American culture. After graduating high school in 2003, he enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps, serving as a combat correspondent and deploying to Iraq in 2005. He left the military in 2007 and used the G.I. Bill to attend Ohio State University, graduating summa cum laude in 2009. He then earned a Juris Doctor from Yale Law School in 2013.

Vance gained national prominence with his 2016 memoir, *Hillbilly Elegy*, which was interpreted as an account of white working-class disaffection. After law school, he worked briefly in corporate law before becoming a venture capitalist, working for Peter Thiel's Mithril Capital and later co-founding Narya Capital. His political career began with his election to the U.S. Senate in 2022, winning a crowded Republican primary with Donald Trump's endorsement and defeating Democrat Tim Ryan in the general election.

Originally a critic of Trump's candidacy, Vance became a strong supporter during Trump's presidency. He was selected as Trump's running mate for the 2024 presidential election and resigned from the Senate before his inauguration as vice president. In his role as vice president, he also serves as finance chair of the Republican National Committee. Described as a national conservative and right-wing populist aligned with the "postliberal" New Right, his political platform is characterized by opposition to immigration, abortion, same-sex marriage, gun control, and U.S. support for Ukraine. He is an outspoken critic of childlessness and cites Catholic social teaching as an influence, though this stance has been criticized by Pope Francis and his successor. Key events during his vice presidency include the Munich Security Conference speech and the 2025 Trump-Zelenskyy Oval Office meeting.

name: Susie Wiles
currentRole: 白宫办公厅主任 (White House Chief of Staff)
education: Graduated from the University of Maryland, College Park in 1978. Also graduated from the Academy of the Holy Angels in Demarest, New Jersey in 1975.
careerHistory: 1978: Began working for Representative Jack Kemp as a receptionist/aide. Early 1980s: Worked for Ronald Reagan's 1980 campaign, in the White House Office of Scheduling and Advance, and as personal secretary for Labor Secretary Raymond J. Donovan. 1992: District director for Tillie Fowler's congressional campaign. 1995-2000: Served in Jacksonville Mayor John Delaney's administration, becoming his chief of staff in 1997. 2010: Campaign manager for Rick Scott's gubernatorial election. 2011: Briefly campaign manager for Jon Huntsman Jr.'s presidential campaign. 2015-2016: Florida campaign chairwoman and later campaign manager for Florida for Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign. 2018: Hired to lead Ron DeSantis's gubernatorial campaign. 2021: Appointed to lead Donald Trump's fundraising apparatus. 2022: Named campaign manager for Trump's 2024 presidential campaign. January 2025: Began serving as White House Chief of Staff.
bio:
Susan L. Wiles (née Summerall; born May 14, 1957) is an American political consultant and lobbyist who has served as the 32nd White House Chief of Staff since January 2025, the first woman to hold the position. Born in Lake City, Florida, she is the daughter of former professional football player and sportscaster Pat Summerall. She graduated from the University of Maryland, College Park in 1978.

Her political career began in 1978 when she started working for New York Representative Jack Kemp as a receptionist and later an aide. She worked for Ronald Reagan's 1980 presidential campaign in his scheduling office and subsequently in the White House Office of Scheduling and Advance. By 1982, she had become a personal secretary for Secretary of Labor Raymond J. Donovan.

After moving to Florida, Wiles served as district director for Tillie Fowler's 1992 congressional campaign. She entered Jacksonville city government in 1995, working for Mayor John Delaney first as director of communications and intergovernmental affairs, then as deputy chief of staff, and finally becoming the city's first female chief of staff from 1997 to 2000. She later served in Mayor John Peyton's administration as chief of special initiatives and communications.

In 2010, Wiles was campaign manager for Rick Scott's successful Florida gubernatorial election. In 2011, she briefly served as national campaign manager for Jon Huntsman Jr.'s presidential campaign. In October 2015, she was hired as a Florida campaign chairwoman for Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, later becoming his Florida campaign manager in September 2016. After Trump's victory, she moved to Washington, D.C., to lead Ballard Partners. In September 2018, she was hired to lead Ron DeSantis's campaign for the Florida gubernatorial election.

In 2021, Wiles was appointed to lead former President Donald Trump's fundraising apparatus, including Save America, assuming a dominant role in his political activities. After Trump announced his 2024 presidential campaign in November 2022, Wiles was named a campaign manager alongside Chris LaCivita. Following Trump's victory in the 2024 election, she was announced as his White House Chief of Staff.

name: Marco Rubio
education: Attended law school at the University of Miami.
careerHistory: City Commissioner for West Miami (1990s). Florida House of Representatives for the 111th district (2000-2008), serving as Speaker (2006-2008). U.S. Senator from Florida (2011-2025). U.S. Secretary of State (2025-present), also serving as Acting National Security Advisor and Acting Archivist of the United States from May 2025.
bio:
Marco Antonio Rubio (born May 28, 1971) is an American politician, attorney, and diplomat serving as the 72nd United States Secretary of State since January 21, 2025. A member of the Republican Party, he is the first Latino to hold the position. Rubio also concurrently serves as the Acting National Security Advisor and the Acting Archivist of the United States, a dual role last held by Henry Kissinger. He is considered the highest-ranking Hispanic American official in U.S. history.

Rubio began his political career after earning a Juris Doctor from the University of Miami School of Law. He was elected as a city commissioner for West Miami in 1998. In 2000, he was elected to the Florida House of Representatives, representing the 111th district. He rose through Republican ranks, becoming majority whip and later Speaker of the Florida House in November 2006, serving a two-year term until leaving the legislature in 2008 due to term limits.

In 2010, Rubio was elected to the U.S. Senate from Florida, taking office in 2011. During his Senate tenure, he was described as a "virtual secretary of state for Latin America" for his influence on U.S. policy toward the region and was known as one of Congress's most hawkish members regarding China and the Chinese Communist Party, resulting in Chinese government sanctions in 2020. He became Florida's senior senator in 2019 and was reelected to a third term in 2022.

Rubio launched a campaign for the Republican presidential nomination in 2015 but suspended it in March 2016 after losing the Florida primary to Donald Trump, whom he later endorsed. In November 2024, President-elect Trump announced his intention to nominate Rubio as Secretary of State. Following unanimous confirmation by the Senate, Rubio assumed the office on January 21, 2025. On May 1, 2025, he additionally assumed the role of Acting National Security Advisor. His tenure as Secretary of State has included foreign trips and summits such as the 2025 Saudi Arabia Summit, the 2025 Alaska Summit, and the 2025 Budapest Summit.

name: Pete Hegseth
education: Studied politics at Princeton University, graduating in 2003 with an Artium Baccalaureus degree. He attended Forest Lake Area High School, graduating as valedictorian in 1999.
careerHistory: 2003: Commissioned as an infantry officer in the Minnesota Army National Guard. 2006-2009: Executive Director and later President of Vets for Freedom. 2014-2024: Contributor and later co-host of Fox & Friends Weekend on Fox News. 2016: Served as an advisor to President Donald Trump after supporting his campaign. 2025: Confirmed as the 29th United States Secretary of Defense.
bio:
Peter Brian Hegseth (born June 6, 1980) is an American government official and former television personality who has served as the 29th United States Secretary of Defense since 2025. He was born in Minneapolis, Minnesota, and raised in Forest Lake, Minnesota, where he graduated as high school valedictorian in 1999. Hegseth studied politics at Princeton University, where he was the publisher and editor-in-chief of the conservative student newspaper, The Princeton Tory. He joined the Reserve Officers' Training Corps before graduating in 2003.

Hegseth was commissioned as a second lieutenant in the U.S. Army through Princeton's ROTC program. He served in the Minnesota Army National Guard, with assignments including an 11-month stint at the Guantanamo Bay detention camp, a deployment to Iraq as an infantry officer where he received a Bronze Star Medal, and a deployment to Afghanistan in 2010-2011 as a counterinsurgency instructor in Kabul. He was promoted to major in 2014 and served in the Individual Ready Reserve until January 2024.

Following his initial military service, Hegseth engaged in political activism. He served as executive director and later president of Vets for Freedom, an organization that supported the 2008 presidential campaign of John McCain. In 2012, he briefly entered the Republican primary for the U.S. Senate in Minnesota but withdrew after losing the party convention. He then served as president of Concerned Veterans for America, a group funded by the Koch brothers. Hegseth became a contributor to Fox News in 2014 and served as an advisor to President Donald Trump after supporting his 2016 campaign. From 2017 to 2024, he co-hosted Fox & Friends Weekend. He is the author of several books, including American Crusade (2020) and The War on Warriors (2024).

In November 2024, President-elect Trump nominated Hegseth for Secretary of Defense. His Senate confirmation hearing faced allegations of sexual misconduct, financial mismanagement, and excessive drinking. He was confirmed by the Senate that month, with Vice President JD Vance casting a tie-breaking vote, making it only the second time in U.S. history a Cabinet nominee's confirmation was decided by a vice president. Hegseth is the second-youngest Secretary of Defense in history. His tenure has drawn criticism related to a leaked government group chat and alleged war crimes concerning U.S. military strikes in the Caribbean Sea.

name: Tulsi Gabbard
currentRole: 国家情报总监 (Director of National Intelligence)
education: Dropped out of Leeward Community College in 2002. Graduated from Hawaii Pacific University in 2009 with a Bachelor of Science in business administration.
careerHistory: 2002-2004: Hawaii House of Representatives. 2003: Enlisted in Hawaii Army National Guard. 2004-2005: Deployed to Iraq as a specialist. 2007: Commissioned as second lieutenant after officer training. 2008-2009: Stationed in Kuwait as Army Military Police platoon leader. 2013-2021: U.S. Representative for Hawaii's 2nd congressional district. 2013-2016: Vice-chair of the Democratic National Committee. 2015: Promoted to major in Hawaii Army National Guard. 2020: Transferred to U.S. Army Reserve. 2021: Promoted to lieutenant colonel. 2025-present: Eighth Director of National Intelligence.
bio:
Tulsi Gabbard (born April 12, 1981) is an American politician and U.S. military officer serving as the eighth director of national intelligence (DNI) since 2025. She was born in Leloaloa, American Samoa, and moved to Hawaii as a child. Gabbard was mostly homeschooled and adopted the Hindu faith as a teenager. She briefly attended Leeward Community College before entering politics.

Gabbard's political career began in 2002 when, at age 21, she was elected to the Hawaii House of Representatives, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to a U.S. state legislature at the time. She served from 2002 to 2004 but did not seek reelection due to a military deployment. She later served on the Honolulu City Council from 2011 to 2012.

In 2012, Gabbard was elected as the U.S. Representative for Hawaii's 2nd congressional district, serving from 2013 to 2021. She was the first Samoan American and first Hindu American member of Congress. During her tenure, she served on the House Armed Services Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and in her fourth term, on the HASC Subcommittee on Intelligence. She supported military action against Islamic extremism but opposed U.S. intervention in the Syrian civil war. Gabbard was a member of the Democratic Party and served as vice-chair of the Democratic National Committee (DNC) from 2013 to 2016, resigning to endorse Bernie Sanders for the 2016 Democratic presidential nomination.

Gabbard launched a 2020 presidential campaign on an anti-interventionist and populist platform but dropped out and endorsed Joe Biden in March 2020. After leaving Congress in 2021, she took more conservative positions, spoke at the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) in 2022, and left the Democratic Party. In 2024, she endorsed Donald Trump for president and joined the Republican Party.

Her military service began in 2003 when she enlisted in the Hawaii Army National Guard. She was deployed to Iraq from 2004 to 2005 as a specialist with a medical unit, receiving the Combat Medical Badge. She completed officer training in 2007, was deployed to Kuwait as a Military Police officer from 2008 to 2009, and was promoted to major in 2015. She transferred to the U.S. Army Reserve in 2020 and was promoted to lieutenant colonel in 2021.

In 2025, Gabbard was confirmed by the Senate as the Director of National Intelligence, becoming the highest-ranking Pacific Islander American government official in U.S. history.

name: John Ratcliffe
currentRole: 中央情报局局长 (Director of the CIA)
education: Graduated from the University of Notre Dame in 1986 with a Bachelor of Arts in government and international studies, and from the Southern Methodist University School of Law in 1989 with a Juris Doctor.
careerHistory: Lawyer in private practice until 2004. Mayor of Heath, Texas (2004-2012). Acting U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Texas (May 2007-April 2008). U.S. Representative for Texas's 4th district (2015-2020). Director of National Intelligence (2020-2021). Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (since 2025).
bio:
John Lee Ratcliffe (born October 20, 1965) is an American politician and attorney who has served as the ninth director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) since 2025. A member of the Republican Party, his career includes service as the sixth director of national intelligence (2020–2021) and as a U.S. Representative for Texas's 4th congressional district from 2015 to 2020.

Ratcliffe was born in Mount Prospect, Illinois. He earned a Bachelor of Arts in government and international studies from the University of Notre Dame in 1986 and a Juris Doctor from the Southern Methodist University School of Law in 1989. After law school, he worked in private legal practice until 2004.

His political career began locally in Texas. He served as mayor of Heath, Texas from 2004 to 2012. Concurrently, he held federal prosecutorial roles. In 2004, President George W. Bush appointed him chief of anti-terrorism and national security for the Eastern District of Texas within the U.S. Department of Justice. He served as the interim U.S. attorney for that district from May 2007 to April 2008. During his 2014 congressional campaign, his website claimed he "personally managed dozens of international and domestic terrorism investigations" and "put terrorists in prison," though subsequent reports indicated no evidence he ever prosecuted a terrorism case. His official House biography also stated he "arrested 300 illegal aliens in a single day" while a prosecutor, though other accounts noted his role was supportive and the number arrested was significantly lower.

Ratcliffe was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2014 after defeating 17-term incumbent Ralph Hall in a Republican primary runoff. He was regarded as one of the most conservative members during his tenure. His committee assignments included the Judiciary, Homeland Security, Ethics, and Intelligence committees, where he held subcommittee leadership roles focusing on cybersecurity and infrastructure protection.

In July 2019, President Donald Trump announced his intent to nominate Ratcliffe to replace Dan Coats as director of national intelligence. Ratcliffe withdrew after Republican senators raised concerns and former intelligence officials warned he might politicize intelligence, alongside media reports about embellishments in his prosecutorial record. Trump renominated him in February 2020; he was confirmed, resigned from the House, and was sworn in on May 26, 2020, serving until 2021. On November 12, 2024, president-elect Trump announced he would nominate Ratcliffe to be director of the CIA. The Senate confirmed him on January 23, 2025, by a vote of 74–25, and he assumed office later that day.

name: Michael Waltz
currentRole: 美国驻联合国大使 (U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations)
education: Earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in international studies from the Virginia Military Institute in 1996, graduating with honors as a Distinguished Military Graduate.
careerHistory: 1996-2000: Active duty U.S. Army officer, later Special Forces officer. 2000-2023: Served in the Army National Guard. Served in the Bush administration as a defense policy director in the Pentagon and as counterterrorism advisor to Vice President Dick Cheney. 2019-2025: U.S. Representative for Florida's 6th congressional district. January to May 2025: 29th National Security Advisor. September 2025-present: 32nd United States Ambassador to the United Nations.
bio:
Michael George Glen Waltz (born January 31, 1974) is an American politician, diplomat, businessman, author, and former Army Special Forces officer. He has served as the 32nd United States Ambassador to the United Nations since September 2025, appointed during the second Trump Administration. A member of the Republican Party, his prior roles include serving as the 29th National Security Advisor from January to May 2025 and as the U.S. Representative for Florida's 6th congressional district from 2019 to 2025. Waltz was the first Army Special Forces soldier elected to Congress.

Waltz's military career began in 1996 when he was commissioned as an armor officer in the U.S. Army. He graduated from Ranger School and the Special Forces Qualification Course in 2000, subsequently serving on active duty with multiple combat tours in the Middle East and Africa. He was decorated with four Bronze Stars for his actions, including two for valor. He later served in the Army National Guard, retiring at the rank of colonel in 2025. Between his military service, Waltz worked in the Pentagon as a defense policy director for Secretaries of Defense Donald Rumsfeld and Robert Gates and served in the White House as Vice President Dick Cheney's counterterrorism advisor.

Elected to the House of Representatives in 2018, Waltz succeeded Ron DeSantis and was re-elected in 2020, 2022, and 2024, each time with over 60% of the vote. In the 118th Congress, he chaired the House Armed Services Subcommittee on Readiness. He was considered one of Congress's most hawkish members regarding China, believing the Chinese Communist Party is in a cold war with the U.S. and the West. In 2021, he was the first member of Congress to call for a full U.S. boycott of the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics over human rights concerns.

Following the 2024 election, President-elect Trump announced Waltz's appointment as National Security Advisor. He served for 101 days before resigning in May 2025 following reported group chat leaks. He was nominated as U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations the same day. After Senate confirmation in a 47–43 vote, he was sworn in on September 20, 2025, and presented his credentials to the UN the following day.

name: Scott Bessent
currentRole: 财政部长 (Secretary of the Treasury)
education: Graduated from Yale University in 1984 with a B.A. in political science.
careerHistory: After graduating from Yale in 1984, Bessent held financial positions at Brown Brothers Harriman, Olayan Group, and Kynikos Associates. He joined Soros Fund Management (SFM) in 1991, becoming head of its London office and a key figure in its Black Wednesday trade in 1992. He left SFM in 2000 to found Bessent Capital, then returned as chief investment officer from 2011 to 2015. In 2015, he left SFM to found the hedge fund Key Square Group. He served as an economic advisor to Donald Trump's 2024 campaign before being nominated and confirmed as the 79th U.S. Secretary of the Treasury, taking office on January 28, 2025.
bio:
Scott Kenneth Homer Bessent (born August 21, 1962) is an American businessman and government official serving as the 79th United States Secretary of the Treasury since January 28, 2025. Born in Conway, South Carolina, Bessent graduated from Yale University in 1984 with a Bachelor of Arts in political science. His early financial career included positions at Brown Brothers Harriman, the Olayan Group in Saudi Arabia, and the hedge fund Kynikos Associates under Jim Chanos.

Bessent's prominent investing career began in 1991 when he joined Soros Fund Management (SFM). He became head of its London office and was a leading member of the team that profited by approximately $1 billion during the 1992 Black Wednesday British pound sterling crisis. After a period away from SFM, during which he founded and closed his own hedge fund, Bessent Capital, he returned to SFM as chief investment officer from 2011 to 2015. In 2013, he made another major gain for the firm, earning over $1.2 billion by betting against the Japanese yen. In 2015, he left SFM to found the global macro investment firm Key Square Group, which received a $2 billion anchor investment from George Soros.

Bessent's involvement in politics evolved over time. He initially supported Democratic candidates, hosting a fundraiser for Al Gore in 2000 and donating to Barack Obama and Hillary Clinton. His political alignment shifted later, and he became a major donor and economic advisor to Donald Trump's 2024 presidential campaign, hosting fundraisers that raised millions of dollars.

On November 22, 2024, President-elect Trump announced his nomination of Bessent for Treasury Secretary. Following a Senate confirmation hearing on January 16, 2025, where he advocated for tax cut extensions and tougher economic policies on China and Russia, he was confirmed by the Senate on January 27, 2025, by a 68–29 vote. He was sworn in the next day by Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh, becoming the first openly gay person to lead the U.S. Treasury Department and the second openly gay Senate-confirmed Cabinet secretary.

Early in his tenure, on February 3, 2025, he was named acting director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and immediately ordered the agency to halt all work. In February 2025, he was tasked with helping implement a U.S. sovereign wealth fund. He has also been involved in personnel decisions within the Treasury, successfully lobbying for his preferred pick for Commissioner of Internal Revenue.

name: Pam Bondi
education: Received a BA in criminal justice from the University of Florida in 1987 and a JD from Stetson University College of Law in 1990.
careerHistory: Assistant State Attorney in Hillsborough County, Florida (1994–2009). Elected as the 37th Attorney General of Florida (2011–2019). Served as a defense lawyer for President Donald Trump during his first impeachment trial (2020). Led the legal arm of the America First Policy Institute (by 2024). Confirmed as the 87th United States Attorney General (2025–present).
bio:
Pamela Jo Bondi (born November 17, 1965) is an American attorney and politician who has served as the 87th United States Attorney General since 2025. A member of the Republican Party, she previously served as the 37th Attorney General of Florida from 2011 to 2019. Born and raised in the Tampa Bay area, Bondi graduated with a BA in criminal justice from the University of Florida in 1987 and earned a JD from Stetson University College of Law in 1990. She was admitted to the Florida Bar in 1991. Her early career was spent as an assistant state attorney and spokeswoman in Hillsborough County, Florida, from 1994 to 2009, where she prosecuted cases including those against former Major League Baseball player Dwight Gooden and defendants in the Martin Anderson death case.

In 2010, Bondi was elected Attorney General of Florida, becoming the first woman to hold the position. She was re-elected in 2014, becoming the first Republican to win a second term. During her tenure, she was the lead attorney general in an unsuccessful multi-state lawsuit seeking to overturn the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act. She also defended a state constitutional amendment banning same-sex marriage against legal challenges, stating her actions were out of respect for the constitution rather than a reflection of personal opinion. Her tenure included involvement in a 2018 lawsuit with other Republican-led states to overturn the ACA's bans on higher premiums for people with pre-existing conditions.

After being term-limited in 2018, Bondi entered private life, working as a registered foreign agent and lobbyist for Ballard Partners, representing clients including Qatar, the Kuwaiti company KGL KSCC, the GEO Group, Amazon, Uber, and General Motors. In 2020, she was hired by the Trump administration and served as one of President Donald Trump's defense lawyers during his first impeachment trial, where she made allegations concerning Joe Biden and his son Hunter Biden related to Ukraine. By 2024, she led the legal arm of the Trump-aligned America First Policy Institute. On November 21, 2024, President-elect Trump announced his intention to nominate Bondi for U.S. Attorney General. She was confirmed by the U.S. Senate in a 54–46 vote on February 4, 2025, and sworn in the next day.

name: Russell Vought
currentRole: 管理与预算办公室主任 (Director of OMB)
education: Earned a BA from Wheaton College in 1998 and a JD from the George Washington University Law School in 2004.
careerHistory: Legislative assistant for U.S. Senator Phil Gramm. Policy director for the Republican Conference of the U.S. House of Representatives and executive director/budget director of the Republican Study Committee. Vice president of Heritage Action. Deputy Director of the Office of Management and Budget (2018-2020). Director of the Office of Management and Budget (2020-2021). Founded the Center for Renewing America in 2021. Reappointed as Director of the Office of Management and Budget in February 2025, concurrently serving as acting director of the CFPB and acting director of USAID.
bio:
Russell Thurlow Vought (born March 26, 1976) is an American government official and conservative political analyst. He has served as the 44th director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) since February 2025, a role he previously held from 2020 to 2021 in the first Trump administration. Concurrently, he is the acting director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) and the acting director of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). He served as deputy director of the OMB from 2018 to 2020.

Vought earned a BA from Wheaton College in 1998 and a JD from George Washington University Law School in 2004. His early career included roles as vice president of Heritage Action, the lobbying arm of the Heritage Foundation; executive director and budget director of the Republican Study Committee; policy director for the Republican Conference of the U.S. House of Representatives; and a legislative assistant for U.S. Senator Phil Gramm. He became a Claremont Institute fellow in 2011.

Between the Trump administrations, in January 2021, Vought founded the Center for Renewing America (CRA), a conservative think tank focused on combating critical race theory and promoting an "America First" policy agenda. At CRA, he organized more than 350 executive orders and regulations in preparation for a potential Republican presidency. He played a major role in the creation of Project 2025, a Heritage Foundation initiative to reshape the federal government, and co-authored its policy playbook. In May 2024, he was named policy director of the Republican National Committee's platform committee.

In the second Trump administration, following his Senate confirmation in February 2025, Vought was sworn in as OMB director. In this role, he has guided efforts to dismantle the federal bureaucracy as part of the Department of Government Efficiency. He oversaw the dismantling of the CFPB in February 2025 and took charge of closing out USAID after it was folded into the U.S. Department of State in August 2025. His politics have been described as Christian nationalist, an ideology he has summed up as his core political belief.

name: Howard Lutnick
education: Graduated from Haverford College in 1983 with a degree in economics.
careerHistory: 1983: Hired at Cantor Fitzgerald. 1990: Became President and CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald. 1996: Appointed Chairman of Cantor Fitzgerald after B. Gerald Cantor's death. August 2024: Named co-chair of Donald Trump's presidential transition team. February 2025: Confirmed as the 41st United States Secretary of Commerce.
bio:
Howard William Lutnick (born July 14, 1961) is an American businessman and government official who has served as the 41st United States Secretary of Commerce since February 2025. Born on Long Island, New York, to a professor father and artist mother, Lutnick is of Jewish descent. He graduated with an economics degree from Haverford College in 1983, where he was captain of the tennis team.

Lutnick's business career is defined by his leadership of Cantor Fitzgerald. Hired in 1983 under founder B. Gerald Cantor, he rose to become president and chief executive by 1990. Following a contentious legal battle over succession after Cantor's declining health, Lutnick gained management control and was appointed chairman after Cantor's death in 1996. He significantly invested in technology, establishing the electronic trading platform eSpeed. The firm suffered devastating losses in the September 11, 2001 attacks, losing 658 employees, including Lutnick's brother, Gary. His handling of the aftermath, including the immediate cessation of salaries to deceased employees' families, drew both praise for rebuilding efforts and criticism from victims' families.

Politically, Lutnick was a Democrat until 2016, after which he became a Republican. He was a fundraiser for Donald Trump's 2020 and 2024 presidential campaigns and a vocal proponent of Trump's tariff proposals. In August 2024, he was named co-chair of Trump's presidential transition team. President-elect Trump nominated Lutnick for Secretary of Commerce in November 2024. Following a Senate Committee hearing in January 2025, he was confirmed by the Senate in February 2025. As Commerce Secretary, he has advocated for tariffs and made controversial statements regarding Social Security payments. Time magazine listed Lutnick as one of the world's 100 most influential people in 2025.

Lutnick is married to Allison Lambert (m. 1994).

name: Doug Burgum
currentRole: 内政部长 (Secretary of the Interior)
education: Graduated from North Dakota State University in 1978 with a bachelor's degree in university studies. Earned an MBA from Stanford University's Graduate School of Business in 1980.
careerHistory: 1983-2001: Co-founded and led Great Plains Software, serving as President from 1984 and taking the company public in 1997. 2001-2006: Senior Vice President of Microsoft Business Solutions Group after Microsoft acquired Great Plains Software. 2008 onward: Co-founded Arthur Ventures venture capital firm and founded Kilbourne Group real-estate development firm. 2016-2024: Served as the 33rd Governor of North Dakota. 2025-present: Serves as the 55th United States Secretary of the Interior.
bio: Douglas James Burgum (born August 1, 1956) is an American businessman and politician serving as the 55th United States Secretary of the Interior since 2025 under President Donald Trump. A member of the Republican Party, he previously served as the 33rd governor of North Dakota from 2016 to 2024. Burgum was born and raised in Arthur, North Dakota. He graduated from North Dakota State University in 1978 and earned an MBA from Stanford University in 1980. After working as a management consultant at McKinsey & Company, he mortgaged inherited farmland in 1983 to invest in Great Plains Software in Fargo, becoming its president in 1984. He took the company public in 1997 and sold it to Microsoft for $1.1 billion in 2001. He then served as senior vice president of Microsoft Business Solutions Group. Burgum is the founder of the Kilbourne Group, a real-estate development firm in Fargo, and co-founded Arthur Ventures, a software venture capital group. He has also served as board chairman for Atlassian and SuccessFactors. Burgum entered politics by winning the 2016 North Dakota gubernatorial election in a landslide and was reelected by a wide margin in 2020. As governor, he set a goal for North Dakota to become carbon-neutral by 2030, primarily through carbon capture and storage technology. He signed legislation providing tax relief and exempting National Guard members from state income tax. In June 2023, Burgum launched a campaign for the 2024 Republican presidential nomination, ending his candidacy in December 2023 and becoming an advisor on the Trump campaign's energy policy. Following the 2024 election, President-elect Trump announced his intention to nominate Burgum as Secretary of the Interior. He was confirmed by the U.S. Senate on January 30, 2025, and sworn in on February 1, 2025. As Secretary of the Interior, he has overseen policies promoting coal-fired power, expanded drilling on federal lands, and expanded metals extraction from federal lands and wildlife refuges, while implementing a crackdown on wind power.

name: Chris Wright
education: Earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering and a master's degree in electrical engineering at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Was a graduate student in electrical engineering at the University of California, Berkeley, and at MIT.
careerHistory: 1992: Founded Pinnacle Technologies and served as its CEO until 2006. Also served as chairman of Stroud Energy before selling it in 2006. 2011: Founded Liberty Energy (Liberty Oilfield Services) and served as its CEO. January 2020 - April 2024: Served on the board of directors for the Denver Branch of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City. February 3, 2025: Sworn in as the 17th United States Secretary of Energy.
bio:
Christopher Allen 'Chris' Wright (born January 15, 1965) is an American businessman and government official serving as the 17th United States Secretary of Energy since February 2025. Born in Colorado, Wright earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering and a master's degree in electrical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and was also a graduate student in electrical engineering at the University of California, Berkeley.

Prior to his government service, Wright had a lengthy career in the energy sector. In 1992, he founded Pinnacle Technologies, a company involved in commercial shale gas production through fracking, serving as its CEO until 2006. He was also chairman of Stroud Energy. In 2011, he founded Liberty Energy (originally Liberty Oilfield Services), North America's second-largest hydraulic fracturing company, and served as its CEO. As CEO of Liberty Energy, he earned $5.6 million in 2023. Wright also served on the boards of directors for Oklo Inc., a nuclear technology company designing small fast-neutron reactors, and EMX Royalty Corp., a Canadian mineral rights company. From January 2020 to April 2024, he served on the board of the Denver Branch of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City. He was publicly known for his skepticism of mainstream climate science, stating in 2023 that 'there is no climate crisis' and criticizing the term 'carbon pollution.'

Wright's nomination as Secretary of Energy was announced by President-elect Donald Trump on November 16, 2024. He had donated to Trump's joint fundraising committee and received endorsements from oil-industry figures, while facing criticism from scientists and environmental groups for his opposition to climate science. The United States Senate confirmed his nomination by a 59–38 vote on February 3, 2025, and he was sworn in the same day.

As Secretary of Energy, Wright has overseen actions by the Trump administration to undermine the United States' response to climate change, which have been widely criticized. He supported the rollback of climate change measures and oversaw a Department of Energy report questioning mainstream climate science. He has made controversial statements, including that 'too little' atmospheric carbon dioxide is a 'bigger risk' than rising levels, and falsely claimed climate change is not impacting extreme weather events. In September 2025, he made a widely criticized statement on social media about solar power's capacity. He has been critical of net-zero emissions targets, calling 'Net zero 2050' a 'colossal train wreck.' He has also criticized the European Green Deal and advocated for U.S. oil and gas exports to the EU, while urging EU states to stop buying Russian gas to strangle Russia's ability to fund its war in Ukraine. In October 2025, he directed the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on interconnection requests and appealed to the White House to accelerate reviews for connecting AI to power grids.

name: Brooke Rollins
education: Graduated from Texas A&M University with a B.S. in agricultural development in 1994. Later obtained a Juris Doctor from the University of Texas School of Law, graduating with honors.
careerHistory: 2003-2018: President and CEO of the Texas Public Policy Foundation. 2018-2020: Director of the Office of American Innovation and Assistant to the President for Strategic Initiatives. 2020: Acting Director of the United States Domestic Policy Council. 2021-March 2025: President and CEO of the America First Policy Institute. Since February 2025: 33rd U.S. Secretary of Agriculture.
bio:
Brooke Leslie Rollins (born April 10, 1972) is an American attorney and politician serving as the 33rd United States Secretary of Agriculture since February 2025. Born in Glen Rose, Texas, she grew up on a farm and was active in Future Farmers of America and 4-H. She earned a B.S. in agricultural development from Texas A&M University in 1994, where she was the first woman elected student body president. She later obtained a Juris Doctor from the University of Texas School of Law.

Rollins began her career as a commercial litigator and a clerk for U.S. District Judge Barbara M. Lynn. She entered public service as deputy general counsel, ethics advisor, and policy director for Texas Governor Rick Perry. From 2003 to 2018, she led the Texas Public Policy Foundation (TPPF), a conservative think tank, as its president and CEO, growing its staff significantly. During her tenure, TPPF advocated for ending agricultural subsidies and opposing ethanol fuel requirements.

In 2018, Rollins joined the Trump administration as Director of the Office of American Innovation and later became Assistant to the President for Strategic Initiatives. She was influential in encouraging the passage of the First Step Act in 2018. In May 2020, she was named acting director of the United States Domestic Policy Council, where she focused on bipartisan responses following the murder of George Floyd.

After the first Trump administration, Rollins co-founded the America First Policy Institute in 2021 with Larry Kudlow, serving as its president and CEO until March 2025. The institute aimed to promote Trump's policy agenda and plan for a potential second administration.

On November 23, 2024, President-elect Donald Trump nominated Rollins for U.S. Secretary of Agriculture. The Senate confirmed her on February 13, 2025, by a 72–28 vote, making her the second woman to hold the position. She was sworn in by Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas.

As Secretary, Rollins has opposed California's Proposition 12 farm animal welfare law, supporting federal efforts to preempt it. In June 2025, she announced an end to the Clinton-era "roadless rule" restricting road construction on millions of acres of national forest land. In January 2026, she announced the suspension of USDA financial awards to Minnesota and Minneapolis due to alleged fraud in federal benefit programs. Rollins is married to Mark Rollins and has four children.

name: Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
currentRole: 卫生与公众服务部部长 (Secretary of HHS)
careerHistory: Began career as an assistant district attorney in Manhattan. In the mid-1980s, joined environmental nonprofits Riverkeeper and the Natural Resources Defense Council. In 1986, became an adjunct professor of environmental law at Pace University School of Law, founding its Environmental Litigation Clinic in 1987. Founded the Waterkeeper Alliance in 1999. Served as the 26th U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services starting in 2025.

name: Tom Homan
currentRole: “边境沙皇” / 高级顾问 (Border Czar / Senior Advisor)
education: Received an associate degree in criminal justice from Jefferson Community College and a bachelor's degree in criminal justice from SUNY Polytechnic Institute.
careerHistory: 1983: Police officer in West Carthage. 1984: Joined U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service, serving as a Border Patrol agent, investigator, and supervisor for 30 years. 2013: Appointed by President Obama as ICE's executive associate director of enforcement and removal operations. January 2017 - June 2018: Served as acting director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). November 2024: Designated as 'border czar' for the second Trump administration.
bio:
Thomas Douglas Homan (born November 28, 1961) is an American law enforcement officer. In November 2024, Donald Trump designated Homan as "border czar" for Trump's second presidency. Homan also served during the Obama administration and the first Trump administration. He served as acting director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) from January 2017 to June 2018.

Homan began his federal law enforcement career in 1984 with the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service, serving as a Border Patrol agent, investigator, and supervisor for 30 years. In 2013, President Barack Obama appointed him as ICE's executive associate director of enforcement and removal operations. Under Obama, Homan began to argue that separating children from caregivers would be an effective deterrent to illegal border crossings, a policy he later helped implement under Trump. In 2015, Obama awarded him a Presidential Rank Award as a Distinguished Executive.

In January 2017, President Trump appointed Homan as acting ICE director. During his tenure, he announced increased arrest numbers of undocumented immigrants and advocated strongly against sanctuary city policies. In April 2018, he and Kevin McAleenan formally advised the implementation of the Trump administration's zero-tolerance policy, including family separation. He defended the policy publicly and participated in the press conference announcing its implementation. He retired as acting ICE director in June 2018.

After 2018, Homan became a commentator for Fox News. In 2022, he joined the Heritage Foundation and became a contributor to its Project 2025. He launched a border-focused project called "Defend the Border and Save Lives" and published a book of the same name in 2020. At the 2024 Republican National Convention, he criticized Biden's immigration policies and promised a large deportation force if Trump returned to office.

As the designated "border czar" in Trump's second administration starting in 2025, Homan was placed in charge of deportation operations. He has been involved in public disputes over immigration enforcement, including with Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and has overseen deportation flights, stating his intent to continue deportations regardless of court orders. The administration reported around 140,000 deportations by April 2025. Homan has advocated for the deportation of illegal immigrants throughout his career and opposes sanctuary city policies.

name: Kristi Noem
currentRole: 国土安全部部长 (Secretary of Homeland Security)
education: Attended Northern State University (1990-1994) but did not graduate. Later obtained a Bachelor of Arts in political science from South Dakota State University in 2012.
careerHistory: Served in the South Dakota House of Representatives from 2007 to 2011. Served as the U.S. Representative for South Dakota's at-large congressional district from 2011 to 2019. Served as the 33rd Governor of South Dakota from 2019 to 2025. Has served as the 8th United States Secretary of Homeland Security since 2025.
bio:
Kristi Lynn Arnold Noem (born November 30, 1971) is an American politician serving as the 8th United States Secretary of Homeland Security since 2025. A member of the Republican Party, she previously served as the 33rd governor of South Dakota from 2019 to 2025 and represented South Dakota's at-large congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives from 2011 to 2019.

Born in Watertown, South Dakota, Noem was raised on the family ranch and farm in Hazel. After her father's death in 1994, she left college to manage the family farm and businesses. She later obtained a Bachelor of Arts in political science from South Dakota State University in 2012 while serving in Congress.

Noem began her political career in the South Dakota House of Representatives, serving from 2007 to 2011, where she was an assistant majority leader and sponsored bills on property tax reform and gun rights. In 2010, she was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, defeating incumbent Democrat Stephanie Herseth Sandlin. She was reelected three times, serving until 2019. During her tenure, she was elected liaison to the House Republican leadership by the 2011 freshman class and served on the conference committee for the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017. Her committee assignments included the Committee on Ways and Means.

In 2018, with the endorsement of President Donald Trump, Noem was elected as the first female governor of South Dakota. She was reelected in 2022. As governor, she gained national attention during the COVID-19 pandemic for opposing statewide mask mandates. She has held conservative positions on issues such as gun rights, abortion, and immigration.

In November 2024, President-elect Donald Trump selected Noem to serve as Secretary of Homeland Security in his second term. She was confirmed by the Senate in January 2025 by a vote of 59–34. Noem is also a farmer, rancher, and member of the Civil Air Patrol, holding the rank of lieutenant colonel. She has published two autobiographies: *Not My First Rodeo: Lessons from the Heartland* (2022) and *No Going Back* (2024).

name: Elon Musk
currentRole: 政府效率部专员/顾问 (Commissioner, DOGE)
education: Received bachelor's degrees in 1997 from the University of Pennsylvania.
careerHistory: 1995: Co-founded the software company Zip2. 1999: Co-founded the online payment company X.com, which later became PayPal. 2002: Founded SpaceX, becoming its CEO and chief engineer. 2004: Joined Tesla as an early investor, later becoming CEO and product architect in 2008. 2015: Co-founded OpenAI. 2016: Co-founded Neuralink. 2017: Founded the Boring Company. 2022: Acquired Twitter (rebranded to X in 2023). 2025: Served as Senior Advisor to the President and de facto head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) before leaving the administration.
bio: Elon Reeve Musk (born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and entrepreneur. He was born into a wealthy family in Pretoria, South Africa, and holds South African and Canadian citizenship from birth. He emigrated to Canada in 1989. Musk received bachelor's degrees from the University of Pennsylvania in the United States in 1997. He became an American citizen in 2002. Musk is known for his leadership of several major companies. His business career began in 1995 when he co-founded the software company Zip2. After its sale in 1999, he co-founded the online payment company X.com, which later merged to form PayPal and was acquired by eBay in 2002. In 2002, he founded the space technology company SpaceX, where he serves as CEO and chief engineer. Musk joined the automaker Tesla as an early investor in 2004 and became its CEO and product architect in 2008. In 2015, he co-founded OpenAI but later left, subsequently establishing the artificial intelligence company xAI. In 2022, he acquired the social network Twitter, rebranding it as X in 2023. His other ventures include co-founding the neurotechnology company Neuralink in 2016 and founding the tunneling company the Boring Company in 2017. As of December 2025, Forbes estimates his net worth to be around US$717 billion, and he has been the wealthiest person in the world since 2021. In November 2025, a Tesla pay package worth $1 trillion for Musk was approved, to be received over 10 years if specific goals are met. Musk's political involvement became prominent when he served as the largest donor in the 2024 U.S. presidential election, supporting Donald Trump. Following Trump's inauguration in early 2025, Musk served as Senior Advisor to the President and as the de facto head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). However, after a public feud with Trump, Musk left the Trump administration and returned to managing his companies. Musk is a supporter of global far-right figures, causes, and political parties. His political activities, views, and statements have made him a polarizing figure. He has been criticized for promoting COVID-19 misinformation, conspiracy theories, and affirming antisemitic, racist, and transphobic comments. His acquisition of Twitter was controversial due to a subsequent increase in hate speech and misinformation following his pledge to decrease censorship. His role in the second Trump administration, particularly in the DOGE, attracted public backlash.

name: Vivek Ramaswamy
currentRole: 政府效率部专员/顾问 (Commissioner, DOGE)
education: Graduated from Harvard University with a Bachelor of Arts in biology in 2007. Earned a Juris Doctor degree from Yale University in 2013.
careerHistory: 2007-2014: Investment partner at hedge fund QVT Financial. 2014-2021: Founder and CEO of Roivant Sciences. 2022: Co-founded Strive Asset Management. 2024: Candidate in Republican presidential primaries. 2025: Launched campaign for Ohio gubernatorial election.
bio:
Vivek Ganapathy Ramaswamy (born August 9, 1985) is an American entrepreneur and politician. He was born in Cincinnati, Ohio, to Hindu Indian immigrant parents from Kerala. Ramaswamy graduated as valedictorian from St. Xavier High School in 2003. He earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in biology from Harvard University in 2007, where he was president of the Harvard Political Union and performed libertarian-themed rap music under the stage name "Da Vek." He received a Juris Doctor degree from Yale Law School in 2013, having attended on a Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans postgraduate fellowship. At Yale, he befriended future vice president JD Vance.

Ramaswamy's business career began in 2007 when he co-founded Campus Venture Network, later sold in 2009. He worked as an investment partner at the hedge fund QVT Financial from 2007 to 2014. In 2014, he founded the biotechnology firm Roivant Sciences, serving as its chief executive officer until 2021, when he became executive chairman. Roivant's strategy involved purchasing patents for undeveloped drugs from larger pharmaceutical companies. In 2015, he raised $360 million for its subsidiary Axovant Sciences to market an Alzheimer's drug, intepirdine, which ultimately failed in clinical trials in 2017. In 2022, he co-founded the investment firm Strive Asset Management. In January 2026, Forbes estimated his net worth at $2 billion.

Ramaswamy entered national politics as a candidate in the 2024 Republican presidential primaries, becoming the youngest candidate in the field. He withdrew his bid and endorsed Donald Trump for the 2024 presidential election. In 2025, he launched his campaign for the 2026 Ohio gubernatorial election, receiving endorsements from both former President Trump and the Ohio Republican Party. He describes himself as a conservative and an American nationalist. Politically, he was largely apolitical until 2020, when he supported Donald Trump's re-election. In 2021, he wrote the book *Woke Inc.* and began appearing on cable networks arguing against left-wing "woke" policies. He has been an active donor to the Republican Party and has criticized environmental, social, and corporate governance (ESG) and affirmative action. He has also promoted numerous conspiracy theories and false statements. He briefly considered running in the 2022 U.S. Senate election in Ohio. Ramaswamy is married to Apoorva Tewari (m. 2015).

name: John Thune
currentRole: 参议院多数党领袖 (Senate Majority Leader)
education: Graduated from Biola University in 1983 with a Bachelor of Arts in business. Received a Master of Business Administration from the University of South Dakota in 1984.
careerHistory: 1997-2003: U.S. Representative for South Dakota's at-large congressional district. 2005-present: United States Senator from South Dakota. Served as Republican chief deputy whip (2007-2009), chair of the Senate Republican Policy Committee (2009-2012), Senate Republican Conference chair (2012-2019), majority whip (2019-2021), and minority whip (2021-2025). Since January 2025: Senate Majority Leader and Senate Republican Leader.
bio: John Randolph Thune (born January 7, 1961) is an American politician serving as the senior United States senator from South Dakota, a seat he has held since 2005. A Republican, he has been the Senate majority leader and Senate Republican leader since January 2025. Thune was born in Pierre, South Dakota. He graduated from Biola University in 1983 with a Bachelor of Arts in business and received a Master of Business Administration from the University of South Dakota in 1984. His early political career included work as a legislative aide for U.S. Senator James Abdnor (1985–1987), executive director of the South Dakota Republican Party, South Dakota Railroad Director (1991–1993), and executive director of the South Dakota Municipal League (1993–1996). Thune was first elected to the U.S. House of Representatives for South Dakota's at-large district in 1996, defeating Democrat Rick Weiland. He was reelected in 1998 and 2000 by wide margins. In 2002, he made an unsuccessful bid for the U.S. Senate, narrowly losing to incumbent Tim Johnson. He ran again in 2004 and defeated Senate Democratic leader Tom Daschle, making Daschle the first incumbent Senate leader to lose an election since 1952. Throughout his Senate tenure, Thune has held several leadership positions: Republican chief deputy whip (2007–2009), chair of the Senate Republican Policy Committee (2009–2012), Senate Republican Conference chair (2012–2019), majority whip (2019–2021), and minority whip (2021–2025). In November 2024, he was elected Senate Republican leader, succeeding Mitch McConnell, and became majority leader when Republicans took control of the Senate in January 2025. He is the first Senate party leader to have first taken office as a senator in the 21st century. Thune serves on several Senate committees: Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry; Commerce, Science, and Transportation; Finance; and the Select Committee on Intelligence. He is married to Kimberley Weems, whom he wed in 1984.

name: Mike Crapo
currentRole: 参议院财政委员会主席 (Chairman, Senate Finance Committee)
education: Earned a Bachelor of Arts, summa cum laude, in political science from Brigham Young University in 1973 and a Juris Doctor, cum laude, from Harvard Law School in 1977.
careerHistory: Practiced law in Idaho Falls throughout the 1980s. Elected to the Idaho Senate in 1984, serving as Senate President Pro Tempore from 1988 to 1992. Served as U.S. Representative for Idaho's 2nd congressional district from 1993 to 1999. Elected as U.S. Senator from Idaho in 1998, a seat he has held since, serving as Chairman of the Senate Finance Committee.
bio:
Michael Dean Crapo (born May 20, 1951) is an American lawyer and politician serving as the senior United States senator from Idaho, a position he has held since 1999. A member of the Republican Party, Crapo is the current Chairman of the Senate Finance Committee. Born in Idaho Falls, Idaho, he earned a Bachelor of Arts, summa cum laude, in political science from Brigham Young University in 1973 and a Juris Doctor, cum laude, from Harvard Law School in 1977. After law school, he clerked for Judge James M. Carter of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit before returning to Idaho to practice law.

Crapo's political career began in the Idaho State Senate, to which he was elected in 1984. He served as Senate President Pro Tempore from 1988 to 1992. In 1992, he was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, representing Idaho's 2nd congressional district for three terms from 1993 to 1999. He was elected to the U.S. Senate in 1998, succeeding Dirk Kempthorne, and has been reelected in 2004, 2010, 2016, and 2022. He is the dean of Idaho's congressional delegation.

In the Senate, Crapo has held significant committee assignments. Beyond chairing the Finance Committee, he has served on the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs (where he was previously chairman during the 116th Congress), the Committee on the Budget, and the Joint Committee on Taxation. His caucus memberships include co-chairing the Senate Nuclear Cleanup Caucus, the Senate Renewables and Energy Efficiency Caucus, and the Sportsmen's Caucus.

Politically conservative, Crapo holds a lifetime conservative rating of 91.30 from the American Conservative Union. His key political positions include being anti-abortion, a proponent of nuclear energy (supporting projects at the Idaho National Laboratory), and a strong opponent of gun control regulations, having received 'A+' grades from the National Rifle Association. In fiscal policy, he has argued for extending Republican tax cuts without deficit offsets and supports ending the IRS Direct File program. In October 2023, he visited China as part of a bipartisan congressional delegation, where he met with Chinese leaders and stated he would raise market-access concerns for Micron Technology.

Crapo is married to Susan Diane Hasleton (since 1974), and they have five children. He is a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer in 1999, underwent treatment, and was declared cancer-free after a recurrence in 2005.

name: Tim Scott
currentRole: 参议院银行、住房和城市事务委员会主席 (Chairman, Senate Banking Committee)
education: Attended Presbyterian College from 1983 to 1984 on a partial football scholarship. Transferred to and graduated from Charleston Southern University in 1988 with a Bachelor of Science degree in political science.
careerHistory: Served on the Charleston County Council (1995–2009). Member of the South Carolina General Assembly (2009–2011). U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 1st congressional district (2011–2013). Appointed as U.S. Senator from South Carolina in 2013, winning subsequent elections. Currently chairs the Senate Committee on Banking and was elected chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee after the 2024 elections.
bio:
Timothy Eugene Scott (born September 19, 1965) is an American businessman and politician serving as the junior United States senator from South Carolina since 2013. A member of the Republican Party, he has achieved several historic firsts: he is the first African-American senator from the Southern United States to be directly elected, the longest-serving African-American senator in U.S. history, the first African-American to serve in both the House and Senate, and the first African-American senator to chair a full committee. He currently chairs the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

Born in North Charleston, South Carolina, Scott graduated from Charleston Southern University in 1988 with a Bachelor of Science in political science. He worked in financial services as an insurance agent and financial adviser before entering politics. His political career began on the Charleston County Council, where he served from 1995 to 2009. He then served as a member of the South Carolina General Assembly from 2009 to 2011.

Scott was elected to represent South Carolina's 1st congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives from 2011 to 2013. In December 2012, Governor Nikki Haley appointed him to the U.S. Senate to replace the retiring Jim DeMint, making Scott the first African American U.S. senator from South Carolina. He won a special election for the seat in 2014 and was elected to full terms in 2016 and 2022.

In the Senate, Scott has been active on issues of race and police reform. He led the drafting of the Justice Act, a bill that included measures such as increased federal reporting for use of force, grants for police body cameras, the creation of a database of police disciplinary records, and the creation of a federal crime for lynching. The bill was blocked by a Democratic filibuster in 2020.

In May 2023, Scott declared his candidacy for the 2024 Republican Party presidential nomination but suspended his campaign in November 2023 due to low polling numbers. After the 2024 elections, he was elected chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee. His committee assignments also include the Committee on Finance, the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, and the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.

name: Ted Cruz
currentRole: 参议院商业、科学和交通委员会主席 (Chairman, Senate Commerce Committee)
education: Graduated from Princeton University with a Bachelor of Arts and earned a Juris Doctor from Harvard Law School.
careerHistory: Policy advisor in the George W. Bush administration (dates unspecified). Solicitor General of Texas (2003-2008). U.S. Senator from Texas (2013-present). Chairman of the Senate Commerce Committee (2025-present).
bio:
Rafael Edward 'Ted' Cruz (born December 22, 1970) is an American politician and attorney serving as the junior United States senator from Texas since 2013. A member of the Republican Party, he has chaired the Senate Commerce Committee since 2025. Cruz was born in Calgary, Alberta, Canada, to an American mother of Irish and Italian descent and a Cuban-born father. His father, Rafael Cruz, left Cuba in 1957, later obtaining political asylum and U.S. citizenship. Ted Cruz renounced his Canadian citizenship in 2014. He is married to Heidi Nelson (m. 2001).

Cruz graduated from Princeton University with a Bachelor of Arts and earned a Juris Doctor from Harvard Law School. He began his political career as a policy advisor in the George W. Bush administration. From 2003 to 2008, he served as the Solicitor General of Texas, appointed by Attorney General Greg Abbott.

Cruz was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2012, becoming the first Hispanic American to serve as a U.S. senator from Texas. In the Senate, he has taken consistently conservative positions on economic and social policy. He played a leading role in the 2013 federal government shutdown, seeking to force Congress and President Barack Obama to defund the Affordable Care Act. Cruz was reelected in 2018 against Democratic nominee Beto O'Rourke and won a third term in 2024 against Congressman Colin Allred.

In 2016, Cruz sought the Republican presidential nomination, emerging as a serious competitor to Donald Trump. After initially withholding his endorsement, he became a strong supporter during Trump's first term. In 2021, Cruz objected to the certification of Joe Biden's victory in the 2020 presidential election.

As a senator, Cruz has stated his intention to be a leading defender of Israel. In 2025, he drafted and led the effort to pass the TAKE IT DOWN Act, signed into law by President Donald Trump, and introduced a bill to create what later became Trump Accounts.

name: Roger Wicker
currentRole: 参议院军事委员会主席 (Chairman, Senate Armed Services Committee)
education: Graduated from the University of Mississippi with a bachelor's degree in journalism and political science in 1973 and earned a J.D. degree from the University of Mississippi School of Law in 1975.
careerHistory: 1980: Served as House Rules Committee counsel to U.S. Representative Trent Lott. 1988-1995: Mississippi State Senator for the 6th district. 1995-2007: U.S. Representative for Mississippi's 1st congressional district. 2007-present: U.S. Senator from Mississippi, appointed in 2007, won special election in 2008, and reelected in 2012, 2018, and 2024. Currently chairs the Senate Armed Services Committee.
bio:
Roger Frederick Wicker (born July 5, 1951) is an American politician, attorney, and former Air Force officer serving as the senior United States senator from Mississippi, a position he has held since 2007. A member of the Republican Party, his political career began in the 1980s. After graduating from the University of Mississippi and its School of Law, he served as an officer in the United States Air Force from 1976 to 1980 and remained in the Air Force Reserve until 2003, retiring as a lieutenant colonel. He initially worked as a political counselor to Congressman Trent Lott on the House Rules Committee.

Wicker was first elected to public office in 1987, serving in the Mississippi State Senate from 1988 to 1994. In 1994, he was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, succeeding long-serving Democrat Jamie Whitten to represent Mississippi's 1st congressional district. He served in the House from 1995 to 2007, where he was a member of the House Appropriations Committee, served as deputy Republican whip, and was president of the large freshman Republican class elected in 1994.

In December 2007, Wicker was appointed to the U.S. Senate by Mississippi Governor Haley Barbour to fill the seat vacated by the resignation of Senator Trent Lott. He subsequently won a special election in 2008 to complete the term and has been reelected to full terms in 2012, 2018, and 2024. In the Senate, Wicker has held leadership roles including Chairman of the National Republican Senatorial Committee from 2015 to 2017 and serves as a deputy Republican whip. He became Mississippi's senior senator in 2018.

In the 119th Congress, Wicker serves on four committees: the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation; the Committee on Environment and Public Works; the Committee on Rules and Administration; and the Senate Armed Services Committee, which he chairs. His committee assignments include leadership of the Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe. He is also a member of several caucuses, including the Congressional Human Rights Caucus, the Senate Taiwan Caucus, and is a co-chair of the Rare Disease Caucus and the Interstate 69 Caucus.

name: Lindsey Graham
currentRole: 参议院预算委员会主席 (Chairman, Senate Budget Committee)
education: Earned a Bachelor of Arts and a Juris Doctor from the University of South Carolina.
careerHistory: Served in the South Carolina House of Representatives (1993-1995). Served in the U.S. House of Representatives for South Carolina's 3rd district (1995-2003). Elected as U.S. Senator from South Carolina (2003-present). Chaired the Senate Committee on the Judiciary (2019-2021). Currently serves as Chairman of the Senate Budget Committee.
bio: Lindsey Olin Graham (born July 9, 1955) is an American politician and attorney serving as the senior United States senator from South Carolina, a seat he has held since 2003. A member of the Republican Party, he currently serves as the Chairman of the Senate Budget Committee. He previously chaired the Senate Committee on the Judiciary from 2019 to 2021. Graham earned both a Bachelor of Arts and a Juris Doctor from the University of South Carolina. He served in the United States Air Force from 1982 to 1988 as a member of the Judge Advocate General's Corps, working as a defense attorney and chief prosecutor in Europe. He later served in the U.S. Air Force Reserve while in Congress, achieving the rank of colonel and receiving a Bronze Star Medal for meritorious service in 2014. Before his Senate career, Graham served in the South Carolina House of Representatives (1993–1995) and the U.S. House of Representatives (1995–2003), representing South Carolina's 3rd congressional district. He was elected to the Senate in 2002 and reelected in 2008, 2014, and 2020. Politically, Graham is a neoconservative known as a defense hawk and an advocate for an aggressive, interventionist foreign policy. He initially gained a reputation for working with Democrats on issues like campaign finance reform, a ban on waterboarding, cap and trade, immigration reform, and judicial nominees. He criticized the Tea Party movement, arguing for a more inclusive Republican Party. In 2015, he sought the Republican nomination for president but dropped out before the primaries began. He was an outspoken critic of Donald Trump's 2016 candidacy but, after a 2017 meeting, became a staunch ally. On foreign policy, he was a frequent critic of the Obama administration and, alongside senators John McCain and Joe Lieberman, was part of a group that pushed for American military intervention, supporting the 2002 Iraq Resolution and the invasion of Iraq. On domestic issues, Graham has a mixed record. He voted for the Defense of Marriage Act in 1996 and supported a constitutional amendment opposing same-sex marriage in 2006, though later stated a constitutional amendment was no longer viable. On climate change, he co-sponsored a framework for a climate bill in 2009 but later withdrew support, questioning the science. In 2020, he sponsored the Growing Climate Solutions Act. In 2023, he co-sponsored the Foreign Pollution Fee Act, a carbon tariff proposal. Regarding investigations into Russian interference in the 2016 election, Graham, along with Senator Chuck Grassley, recommended charges against Christopher Steele, author of the Steele dossier, in 2018. He also introduced legislation aimed at protecting Special Counsel Robert Mueller from being fired without cause.

name: Chuck Grassley
currentRole: 参议院司法委员会主席 (Chairman, Senate Judiciary Committee)
education: Graduated from New Hartford Community High School in 1951. Earned a BA in 1955 and an MA in political science in 1956 from Iowa State Teachers College (now University of Northern Iowa). Pursued a Ph.D. in political science at the University of Iowa but did not complete it.
careerHistory: Served in the Iowa House of Representatives (1959–1975). Served in the United States House of Representatives (1975–1981). U.S. Senator from Iowa since 1981. Served as president pro tempore of the U.S. Senate (2019–2021, and again since 2025). Became the 45th dean of the U.S. Senate in 2023.
bio:
Charles Ernest Grassley (born September 17, 1933) is an American politician serving as the senior United States senator from Iowa, a position he has held since 1981. A member of the Republican Party, he is the longest-serving Republican in congressional history and, as of the provided text, the oldest sitting United States senator. Grassley has held significant leadership roles, including serving as president pro tempore of the United States Senate from 2019 to 2021 and again since 2025. Upon Patrick Leahy's retirement in January 2023, he became the most senior member of the Senate, a role known as the Dean of the United States Senate.

His political career began in the Iowa House of Representatives, where he served from 1959 to 1975. He then served three terms in the United States House of Representatives from 1975 until his election to the Senate. During his extensive Senate tenure, Grassley has chaired several powerful committees, including the Finance Committee (during three separate stints), the Judiciary Committee, the Aging Committee, and the Narcotics Control Caucus. His committee assignments in the 118th Congress include the Committees on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry; Finance (where he is Ranking Member); the Budget (Ranking Member); and the Judiciary. He also co-chairs the United States Senate Caucus on International Narcotics Control.

Grassley is noted for his Senate voting record, having set a record for the longest period without a missed roll-call vote—a streak that lasted over 27 years and 8,927 votes until November 2020. He has cast over 12,000 votes in his Senate career.

On policy, the text highlights several of his positions. He identifies as pro-life, co-sponsored the Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act in 2019, and approved of the overturning of Roe v. Wade in 2022. In agriculture and energy, he has been a prominent advocate for federal ethanol subsidies and wind energy, authoring the federal wind energy tax credit in 1992. He has criticized the Environmental Protection Agency's handling of biofuel regulations. On antitrust, he co-introduced the American Innovation and Choice Online Act in 2021. He supports repealing the estate tax, arguing it is harmful to farmers and small business owners. Grassley filed for reelection for a ninth Senate term in 2028.

name: Jim Risch
currentRole: 参议院外交关系委员会主席 (Chairman, Senate Foreign Relations Committee)
education: Attended University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (1961-1963), transferred to University of Idaho, earning a B.S. in forestry in 1965 and a J.D. in 1968.
careerHistory: Elected Ada County Prosecuting Attorney in 1970. Served in the Idaho Senate from 1974 to 1988, and again from 1995 to 2002. Served as Lieutenant Governor of Idaho from 2003 to 2006, then as Governor from May 2006 to January 2007. Served again as Lieutenant Governor from 2007 to 2009. Elected as U.S. Senator from Idaho in 2008, and has been reelected since.
bio:
James Elroy Risch (born May 3, 1943) is an American lawyer and politician who has served as the junior United States senator from Idaho since 2009. A member of the Republican Party, his political career spans over five decades, beginning at the state level in Idaho. Born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, Risch moved to Idaho in the early 1960s. He earned a B.S. in forestry in 1965 and a J.D. in 1968 from the University of Idaho. He entered politics in 1970 at age 27, winning election as Ada County Prosecuting Attorney, a role in which he also taught criminal justice at Boise State College.

Risch was first elected to the Idaho Senate in 1974, where he served until 1988, holding leadership positions including majority leader and president pro tempore. After a brief period out of office, he was appointed to the state Senate again in 1995 and served until 2002. In 2002, he was elected Lieutenant Governor of Idaho.
