He ascended to the governorship in May 2006 upon the resignation of Governor Dirk Kempthorne, serving out the remainder of the term. During his brief tenure as the 31st governor, he called a special legislative session for property tax reform and issued an executive order on employee citizenship verification. He then returned to the role of Lieutenant Governor under Governor Butch Otter from 2007 to 2009.

Risch was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2008 and has been reelected in 2014 and 2020. In the Senate, he holds a seat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, where he currently serves as Chairman. His foreign policy actions include co-sponsoring the Israel Anti-Boycott Act in 2018, co-sponsoring a 2019 act to sanction Turkey, and advocating for sanctions related to conflicts in Ethiopia and Sudan. In 2024, he sponsored a report advocating for strengthening NATO. Politically conservative, Risch is anti-abortion and supported the overturning of Roe v. Wade. He is married to Vicki Risch since 1968.

name: Susan Collins
currentRole: 参议院拨款委员会主席 (Chair, Senate Appropriations Committee)
education: Graduated magna cum laude from St. Lawrence University with a bachelor's degree in government in 1975.
careerHistory: 1975-1987: Legislative assistant to U.S. Representative/Senator William Cohen. 1981-1987: Staff director of the Oversight of Government Management Subcommittee. 1987: Commissioner of the Maine Department of Professional and Financial Regulation. 1992: New England regional director for the Small Business Administration. 1993: Deputy State Treasurer of Massachusetts. 1994: Republican nominee for Governor of Maine. 1994-1996: Founding executive director of the Center for Family Business at Husson College. 1997-present: U.S. Senator from Maine. 2003-2007: Chair of the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. 2015-2021: Chair of the Senate Special Committee on Aging. 2025-present: Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee.
bio:
Susan Margaret Collins (born December 7, 1952) is an American politician serving as the senior United States senator from Maine, a seat she has held since 1997. A member of the Republican Party, she is Maine's longest-serving member of Congress and the longest-serving Republican woman senator. Since 2025, Collins has served as chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee.

Born in Caribou, Maine, Collins is a graduate of St. Lawrence University. Her political career began in 1975 as a staff assistant for Senator William Cohen. She later served as staff director of the Oversight of Government Management Subcommittee of the Committee on Governmental Affairs (1981-1987). Governor John R. McKernan Jr. appointed her commissioner of the Maine Department of Professional and Financial Regulation in 1987. In 1992, President George H. W. Bush appointed her director of the Small Business Administration's regional office in Boston. She served as a deputy state treasurer in Massachusetts in 1993.

Returning to Maine, Collins was the Republican nominee for governor in 1994, becoming the first female major-party nominee for the post, though she finished third. She then became the founding director of the Center for Family Business at Husson University.

Collins was first elected to the U.S. Senate in 1996 and has been reelected every six years since. She chaired the Senate Special Committee on Aging from 2015 to 2021 and the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs from 2003 to 2007. She is the dean of Maine's congressional delegation and, for several Congresses, has been the only New England Republican in the Senate.

Generally regarded as a moderate Republican, Collins is often a pivotal vote in the Senate. She was one of three Republicans to vote against a partial repeal of the Affordable Care Act, the sole Republican to vote against confirming Amy Coney Barrett to the Supreme Court, and one of three to vote to confirm Ketanji Brown Jackson. She voted to confirm Brett Kavanaugh. She opposed the Women's Health Protection Act and supports maintaining the 60-vote Senate threshold for legislation. Collins was a pivotal Republican vote for the Trump administration's Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.

During President Bill Clinton's impeachment trial, she voted to acquit on both charges. In the first impeachment trial of Donald Trump, she voted to acquit. In his second impeachment trial, she was one of seven Republicans to vote to convict Trump of incitement of insurrection.

name: Mike Johnson
currentRole: 众议院议长 (Speaker of the House)
education: Graduated from Captain Shreve High School. Earned a Bachelor of Science in business administration from Louisiana State University in 1995 and a Juris Doctor from Louisiana State's Paul M. Hebert Law Center in 1998.
careerHistory: Attorney for Alliance Defending Freedom (2002-2010). Served on the Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission of the Southern Baptist Convention (2004-2012). Elected to Louisiana House of Representatives (2015-2017). First elected to U.S. House of Representatives for Louisiana's 4th district (2017-present). Served as Chair of the Republican Study Committee (2019-2021) and Vice Chair of the House Republican Conference (2021-2023). Elected 56th Speaker of the House (2023-present).
bio: James Michael "Mike" Johnson (born January 30, 1972) is an American lawyer and politician serving as the 56th speaker of the United States House of Representatives since October 25, 2023. A member of the Republican Party, he is in his fifth term representing Louisiana's 4th congressional district, a position he has held since 2017. Johnson's political career began with his election to the Louisiana House of Representatives in 2015, where he served until 2017. He first won election to the U.S. House in 2016 and has been reelected consistently, running unopposed in 2022. Before entering politics, Johnson worked as a constitutional lawyer. He was an attorney for the Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF), a conservative Christian legal advocacy group, from 2002 to 2010. His legal career focused on defending religious freedom, the sanctity of human life, and traditional marriage. Notably, he defended Louisiana Amendment 1, which defined marriage as between one man and one woman, in 2004. He also represented the Ark Encounter theme park in a 2015 federal lawsuit against Kentucky officials. Johnson served on the Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission of the Southern Baptist Convention from 2004 to 2012. In Congress, Johnson has held several leadership roles. He chaired the Republican Study Committee, the largest caucus of conservatives in Congress, from 2019 to 2021. He served as vice chair of the House Republican Conference from 2021 to 2023. A social conservative, he has supported bills to ban abortion nationwide. Johnson was among the 147 Republicans who voted to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election. He was elected Speaker of the House in October 2023 after the ouster of Kevin McCarthy and was narrowly reelected to a full term as speaker in 2025. Johnson is a graduate of Captain Shreve High School in Shreveport, Louisiana. He earned a Bachelor of Science in business administration from Louisiana State University in 1995 and a Juris Doctor degree from LSU's Paul M. Hebert Law Center in 1998.

name: Steve Scalise
currentRole: 众议院多数党领袖 (House Majority Leader)
education: Graduated from Archbishop Rummel High School and earned a Bachelor of Science degree from Louisiana State University (LSU) with a major in computer science and a minor in political science.
careerHistory: 1995-2007: Served in the Louisiana House of Representatives. 2007: Elected to the Louisiana State Senate (served four months). 2008-present: U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 1st congressional district. 2013-2014: Chair of the House Republican Study Committee. 2014-2019: House Majority Whip. 2019-2023: House Minority Whip. 2023-present: House Majority Leader.
bio: Stephen Joseph Scalise (born October 6, 1965) is an American politician serving as the House Majority Leader since 2023 and as the U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 1st congressional district since 2008. A member of the Republican Party, his district includes most of New Orleans's suburbs and a portion of New Orleans itself. Before his election to Congress, Scalise served in the Louisiana State Senate for four months and three terms in the Louisiana House of Representatives. He was the chair of the House Republican Study Committee from 2013 to 2014. On June 19, 2014, Scalise was elected by his Republican colleagues as Majority Whip of the United States House of Representatives, assuming office on August 1. He served as Majority Whip from 2014 to 2019 and as House Minority Whip from 2019 to 2023. He is the first Louisianian to serve as majority whip since Hale Boggs. In 2017, Scalise became the dean of the Louisiana congressional delegation. On June 14, 2017, Scalise was shot and seriously wounded during a practice for the Congressional Baseball Game by a domestic terrorist targeting Republicans. He underwent months of treatment, returning to Congress on September 28. In October 2023, following the removal of Kevin McCarthy, Scalise defeated Jim Jordan to win the Republican nomination for Speaker of the House but withdrew a day later after failing to consolidate the necessary votes. Scalise was born in New Orleans and graduated from Archbishop Rummel High School. He earned a Bachelor of Science degree from Louisiana State University in Baton Rouge, majoring in computer science with a minor in political science. In Congress, his committee assignments have included the Committee on Energy and Commerce and its subcommittees, and he served as the Ranking Member on the Select Subcommittee on the Coronavirus Crisis. His caucus memberships include the Congressional Western Caucus, the Republican Study Committee, and the Congressional Caucus on Turkey and Turkish Americans. Key legislative actions include co-sponsoring the Stop Online Piracy Act in 2011, voting against reauthorizing the Violence Against Women Act in 2013, sponsoring the FCC Consolidated Reporting Act in 2013, and voting in favor of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act in 2017.

name: Tom Cole
currentRole: 众议院拨款委员会主席 (Chairman, House Appropriations Committee)
education: Graduated from Grinnell College in 1971 with a BA in history. Earned an MA from Yale University in 1974 and a PhD from the University of Oklahoma in 1984, both in British history.
careerHistory: Elected to the Oklahoma Senate (1988-1991). Served as Oklahoma's Secretary of State (1995-1999). Elected as U.S. Representative for Oklahoma's 4th congressional district (2003-present). Served as Chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC) following the 2006 election cycle. Served as chair of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on the Legislative Branch (as of 2015).
bio:
Thomas Jeffery Cole (born April 28, 1949) is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for Oklahoma's 4th congressional district since 2003. A member of the Republican Party, he currently chairs the House Committee on Appropriations, the first Native American and first Oklahoman to hold that position. Cole is a member of the Chickasaw Nation and, as of 2022, became the longest-serving Native American in the history of Congress. He is one of four Native Americans in Congress who are enrolled tribal members.

Cole's political career began in Oklahoma state government. Following his mother, Helen Cole, the first Native American elected to the Oklahoma Senate, he was elected to the Oklahoma Senate himself in 1988, serving until 1991. He chaired the Oklahoma Republican Party for much of the 1980s. He later served as the 26th secretary of state of Oklahoma from 1995 to 1999, appointed by Governor Frank Keating, and assisted with recovery efforts after the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing. Before his election to the U.S. House, he worked as a political consultant and was executive director of the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC).

Elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2002, Cole has established a solidly conservative voting record, consistently voting anti-abortion and for gun rights, while holding pro-business views and supporting free trade, the military, and veterans. Following the 2006 election cycle, he was elected by the House Republican Conference to serve as NRCC chairman. He has been a leading voice for strengthening protections for Native American women under the Violence Against Women Act and has prioritized educating members of Congress on American Indian issues. He has sponsored legislation on various topics, including prohibiting public funds for political party conventions and allowing tax credits for homeschool materials.

Cole holds a BA in history from Grinnell College, an MA from Yale University, and a PhD in British history from the University of Oklahoma. He was a Fulbright Fellow at the University of London. The Center for Effective Lawmaking ranked him as the third-most effective House Republican in the 119th Congress (2023–25). He is married to Ellen Cole and has one son.

name: Brett Guthrie
currentRole: 众议院能源和商业委员会主席 (Chairman, House Energy and Commerce Committee)
education: Earned a Bachelor of Science in mathematical economics from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1987 and a Master's of Public and Private Management from the Yale School of Management in 1997.
careerHistory: Field artillery officer in the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky (dates not specified). Vice president of Trace Die Cast, Inc. (dates not specified). Kentucky State Senator for the 32nd district (1999–2008). U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 2nd congressional district (2009–present). Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (119th Congress, present).
bio:
Steven Brett Guthrie (born February 18, 1964) is an American businessman and politician serving as the U.S. representative for Kentucky's 2nd congressional district since 2009. He is the Chairman of the House Energy and Commerce Committee in the 119th Congress. Guthrie was born in Florence, Alabama, and earned a Bachelor of Science in mathematical economics from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1987 and a Master's of Public and Private Management from the Yale School of Management in 1997. He served as a field artillery officer in the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, and was a vice president of Trace Die Cast, Inc., an automotive parts supplier.

Guthrie began his political career in the Kentucky Senate, representing the 32nd district from 1999 to 2008, where he served as vice chair of the Economic Development, Tourism and Labor Committee and chaired the Transportation Committee. He was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2008, succeeding retiring Representative Ron Lewis after defeating Democratic nominee David Boswell. He has been reelected multiple times, often by large margins.

During his tenure in Congress, Guthrie has served on the Committee on Energy and Commerce, which he now chairs. His legislative actions include voting for the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012, voting against defunding the NSA in 2013, and voting to end the 2013 federal government shutdown. He introduced the Missing Children's Assistance Reauthorization Act of 2013. In 2017, he co-introduced the PROSPER Act, which aimed to reform education funding, and voted for the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. In 2022, he criticized President Joe Biden's student loan forgiveness plan.

Guthrie's political positions include supporting the repeal and replacement of the Affordable Care Act and co-sponsoring a bill to reduce Medicare's power to negotiate drug prices. He is a member of several caucuses, including the Republican Study Committee, the Climate Solutions Caucus, the Congressional Arts Caucus, the U.S.–Japan Caucus, the Rare Disease Caucus, and the Congressional Caucus on Turkey and Turkish Americans. He is married to Beth Clemmons and has three children and three grandchildren.

name: Jim Jordan
currentRole: 众议院司法委员会主席 (Chairman, House Judiciary Committee)
education: Graduated from the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1986 with a bachelor's degree in economics. Later earned a master's degree in education from Ohio State University and a Juris Doctor from Capital University Law School in 2001.
careerHistory: Assistant wrestling coach at Ohio State University (1987-1995). Elected to Ohio House of Representatives (1995). Elected to Ohio Senate (2001). U.S. Representative for Ohio's 4th congressional district (2007-present). First Chair of the House Freedom Caucus (2015-2017). Ranking Member of the House Oversight Committee (2019-2020). Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee (2020-2023). Chairman of the House Judiciary Committee (2023-present).
bio:
James Daniel Jordan (born February 17, 1964) is an American politician who has served as the U.S. Representative for Ohio's 4th congressional district since 2007. A member of the Republican Party, he is currently in his tenth term. Jordan is the Chairman of the House Judiciary Committee, a role he assumed in 2023 after serving as its ranking member from 2020. He previously served as the ranking member of the House Oversight Committee from 2019 to 2020.

Before his political career, Jordan was a champion collegiate wrestler at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, winning two NCAA Division I national championships in 1985 and 1986. He later worked as an assistant wrestling coach at Ohio State University from 1987 to 1995, a period during which team physician Richard Strauss sexually abused numerous athletes. Several individuals have stated Jordan was aware of the abuse, which he has consistently denied.

Jordan entered politics in the Ohio General Assembly, serving in the Ohio House of Representatives from 1994 and later in the Ohio Senate from 2000 to 2006. Upon his election to the U.S. House in 2006, he became a prominent figure in conservative circles. He helped found the right-wing populist House Freedom Caucus and served as its first chair from 2015 to 2017, and as its vice chair since 2017. He was a prominent critic of Speaker John Boehner, who resigned under pressure from the caucus in 2015.

In Congress, Jordan has been a close ally of former President Donald Trump. During Trump's presidency, he sought to discredit investigations into Russian election interference and staged a sit-in to obstruct a Trump impeachment inquiry. After the 2020 presidential election, Jordan supported lawsuits challenging the results and voted against certifying the Electoral College results. He refused to cooperate with the House Select Committee on the January 6 Attack, which subpoenaed him in 2022.

Jordan has been involved in multiple Speaker of the House elections. He supported Kevin McCarthy during the January 2023 election, but after McCarthy's removal later that year, Jordan became the Republican nominee for Speaker in October 2023. He failed to win the speakership after three rounds of voting and withdrew his nomination.

name: James Comer
currentRole: 众议院监督与问责委员会主席 (Chairman, House Oversight Committee)
education: Received a BS in Agriculture from Western Kentucky University in 1993.
careerHistory: 2000-2012: Served in the Kentucky House of Representatives. 2012-2016: Served as Kentucky's Agriculture Commissioner. 2016-Present: U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 1st congressional district. 2023-Present: Chairman of the House Oversight Committee.
bio: James Richardson Comer Jr. (born August 19, 1972) is an American politician from Kentucky. A member of the Republican Party, he has represented Kentucky's 1st congressional district in the United States House of Representatives since 2016. He currently serves as the Chairman of the House Oversight Committee, a role he assumed in 2023. His political career began in Kentucky state government. He served in the Kentucky House of Representatives from 2000 to 2012, first elected at age 27. From 2012 to 2016, he served as Kentucky's Agriculture Commissioner. In that role, he chaired the Kentucky Industrial Hemp Commission and was instrumental in restarting the state's industrial hemp industry, including filing suit against the DEA to allow hemp seeds to be delivered to farmers. He also founded the Kentucky Proud Farm to Campus program and created mobile science centers for agricultural education. In 2015, Comer sought the Republican nomination for Governor of Kentucky but narrowly lost the primary to Matt Bevin. Elected to the U.S. House in 2016, Comer has focused on agricultural issues. He was an original cosponsor of the Hemp Farming Act, which was later included in the 2018 Farm Bill and legalized hemp nationwide. During the COVID-19 pandemic, he co-introduced the COVID-19 Child Nutrition Response Act to ensure student access to school meals during closures. He voted for the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017. As Chairman of the House Oversight Committee, Comer has led investigations into President Joe Biden and his family, and, following Biden's withdrawal from the 2024 presidential race, into Vice President Kamala Harris and Governor Tim Walz. The text notes that, as of August 2024, his investigation had not found evidence Biden was directly involved in or profited from his family's business activities. Comer is a social conservative, opposing same-sex marriage and abortion, and has supported lifting the trade embargo on Cuba. Prior to his political career, Comer graduated from Western Kentucky University with a BS in Agriculture, served as president of the Kentucky Future Farmers of America, operated a family farm, and was a bank director and local chamber of commerce president.

name: John Roberts
education: Attended Harvard University, graduating with a B.A. summa cum laude in 1976, then attended Harvard Law School.
careerHistory: Law clerk for Judge Henry Friendly (1979-1980). Law clerk for Justice William Rehnquist (1980-1981). Special assistant to the Attorney General (1981). Held positions in the Department of Justice (1989-1993). Appointed to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit (2003). Confirmed as the 17th Chief Justice of the United States (2005-present).
bio:
John Glover Roberts Jr. (born January 27, 1955) is an American jurist who has served since 2005 as the 17th chief justice of the United States. He is regarded as having a moderate conservative judicial philosophy and has been described as a swing vote in some cases. Roberts has presided over an ideological shift toward conservative jurisprudence on the Supreme Court, authoring key opinions.

Roberts was born in Buffalo, New York, and raised Catholic in Northwest Indiana. He attended Harvard University, graduating summa cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts in history in three years. He then attended Harvard Law School, where he was managing editor of the Harvard Law Review and graduated magna cum laude at the top of his class in 1979.

His early legal career included clerkships for Judge Henry Friendly on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit (1979–1980) and for Justice William Rehnquist at the U.S. Supreme Court (1980–1981). He served in the Department of Justice from 1989 to 1993 during the presidencies of Ronald Reagan and George H. W. Bush, first as Principal Deputy Solicitor General. Between government roles, he worked in private practice, building a leading appellate practice and arguing 39 cases before the Supreme Court.

In 2003, President George W. Bush appointed Roberts to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. In 2005, Bush nominated him to the Supreme Court—first as an associate justice to fill Sandra Day O'Connor's vacancy, then as chief justice following William Rehnquist's death. Roberts was confirmed by a Senate vote of 78–22, becoming, at age 50, the youngest chief justice since John Marshall.

As chief justice, Roberts has authored majority opinions in landmark cases including National Federation of Independent Business v. Sebelius (upholding most of the Affordable Care Act), Shelby County v. Holder (limiting the Voting Rights Act of 1965), Trump v. Hawaii (expanding presidential powers over immigration), Carpenter v. United States (expanding digital privacy), Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard (overruling race-based admission programs), and Trump v. United States (outlining presidential immunity from criminal prosecution). He also presided over President Donald Trump's first impeachment trial.

name: Clarence Thomas
education: Graduated with honors from the College of the Holy Cross in 1971 and earned his Juris Doctor from Yale Law School in 1974.
careerHistory: 1971: Graduated from College of the Holy Cross. 1974: Earned Juris Doctor from Yale Law School. After graduation, appointed as an assistant attorney general in Missouri, then entered private practice. 1979: Became a legislative assistant to U.S. Senator John Danforth. 1981: Made Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights at the U.S. Department of Education. 1982: Appointed Chairman of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). 1990: Nominated to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. 1991: Became an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
bio:
Clarence Thomas (born June 23, 1948) is an American lawyer and jurist who has served as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States since 1991. He is the second African American to serve on the Court and, following the retirements of Anthony Kennedy in 2018 and Stephen Breyer in 2022, he became its longest-serving and oldest member. President George H. W. Bush nominated Thomas to succeed Thurgood Marshall. His Senate confirmation hearings were intensely contentious, centering on an accusation of sexual harassment by Anita Hill, a former subordinate. He was confirmed by a narrow vote of 52–48.

Thomas was born in Pin Point, Georgia, into a poor Gullah community. After his father abandoned the family, he was raised by his maternal grandfather in Savannah. He initially intended to become a Catholic priest but left the seminary after encountering racism. He graduated with honors from the College of the Holy Cross in 1971 and earned a Juris Doctor from Yale Law School in 1974.

His legal career began as an assistant attorney general in Missouri. He later served as a legislative assistant to U.S. Senator John Danforth (1979), Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights at the U.S. Department of Education (1981), and Chairman of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), appointed by President Ronald Reagan in 1982. In 1990, President Bush nominated him to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, where he served for 19 months before his elevation to the Supreme Court.

On the Court, Thomas is known as a foremost originalist, emphasizing the original meaning of the U.S. Constitution in his interpretations. He is widely considered the Court's most conservative member. Notable majority opinions he has authored include Good News Club v. Milford Central School, concerning religious speech under the First Amendment, and New York State Rifle & Pistol Association, Inc. v. Bruen, affirming the right to bear arms outside the home. He is also known for his dissent in Gonzales v. Raich, arguing against Congress's power to criminalize private cultivation of medical cannabis. For many years, he was notable for his silence during oral arguments, though he has since begun asking more questions.

name: Samuel Alito
education: Princeton University (BA, graduated 1972) and Yale Law School (JD, graduated 1975).
careerHistory: 1976-1977: Law clerk for Third Circuit Judge Leonard I. Garth. 1977-1981: Assistant U.S. Attorney for the District of New Jersey. 1981-1985: Assistant to U.S. Solicitor General Rex E. Lee. 1985-1987: Deputy Assistant Attorney General in the Office of Legal Counsel. 1987-1990: U.S. Attorney for the District of New Jersey. 1990-2006: Judge on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit. 2006-present: Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
bio:
Samuel Anthony Alito Jr. (born April 1, 1950) is an American jurist serving as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States. He was nominated by President George W. Bush on October 31, 2005, and has served since January 31, 2006. He is the second Italian American justice to serve on the Court, after Antonin Scalia.

Alito was raised in Hamilton Township, New Jersey, and graduated summa cum laude from Princeton University's Woodrow Wilson School of Public and International Affairs in 1972. His senior thesis was on the Italian Constitutional Court. He then attended Yale Law School, where he served as an editor of the Yale Law Journal and earned a Juris Doctor in 1975. After law school, he clerked for Third Circuit Judge Leonard I. Garth.

His early legal career included serving as an Assistant United States Attorney for the District of New Jersey (1977–1981), where he prosecuted cases involving drug trafficking and organized crime. From 1981 to 1985, he was Assistant to the U.S. Solicitor General, arguing 12 cases before the Supreme Court. He later served as Deputy Assistant Attorney General in the Office of Legal Counsel (1985–1987) and as the United States Attorney for the District of New Jersey (1987–1990).

In 1990, President George H. W. Bush nominated Alito to the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, where he served until his elevation to the Supreme Court. As a judge, he described himself as a "practical originalist" and is considered a member of the Court's conservative bloc.

On the Supreme Court, Justice Alito has authored majority opinions in several landmark cases. These include McDonald v. Chicago (2010), which addressed firearm rights; Burwell v. Hobby Lobby (2014), concerning insurance coverage; Janus v. AFSCME (2018), on public-sector union security agreements; and Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization (2022), which overturned Roe v. Wade and returned the issue of abortion to the states.

name: Brett Kavanaugh
education: Graduated cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts in history from Yale University in 1987. Earned a Juris Doctor degree from Yale Law School in 1990.
careerHistory: 1990-1991: Law clerk for Judge Walter King Stapleton of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit. 1991-1992: Law clerk for Judge Alex Kozinski of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. 1993-1994: Law clerk for Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy. Mid-1990s to 1998: Associate Counsel in the Office of the Independent Counsel under Ken Starr, assisting with investigations concerning President Bill Clinton and co-authoring the Starr Report. Early 2000s: White House staff secretary in the Bush administration. 2006-2018: U.S. circuit judge of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. 2018-present: Associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
bio:
Brett Michael Kavanaugh (born February 12, 1965) is an American lawyer and jurist serving as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States. He was nominated by President Donald Trump on July 9, 2018, and has served since October 6, 2018. Kavanaugh was previously a U.S. circuit judge of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit from 2006 to 2018.

Kavanaugh studied history at Yale University, graduating cum laude in 1987, and then attended Yale Law School, where he was a member of the Yale Law Journal, earning a Juris Doctor in 1990. His legal career began with clerkships for Judge Walter King Stapleton of the Third Circuit and Judge Alex Kozinski of the Ninth Circuit. He later clerked for Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy from 1993 to 1994.

He worked as an associate counsel in the Office of the Independent Counsel under Ken Starr from 1994 to 1997 and again in 1998. In this role, Kavanaugh assisted with investigations concerning President Bill Clinton, was a principal author of the Starr Report recommending Clinton's impeachment, and argued the case Swidler & Berlin v. United States before the Supreme Court. He joined the George W. Bush administration in 2001, initially in the White House Counsel's office, and later served as Assistant to the President and White House Staff Secretary from 2003. In this capacity, he was a central figure in the administration's efforts to identify and confirm judicial nominees.

President Bush nominated Kavanaugh to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit in 2003. His confirmation hearings were contentious and stalled for three years over charges of partisanship before he was confirmed in May 2006.

His nomination to the Supreme Court in 2018 was highly controversial. During the confirmation process, Christine Blasey Ford and three other women accused him of sexual misconduct in the early 1980s; Kavanaugh denied all accusations, which were not corroborated by eyewitness testimony. The Senate Judiciary Committee held a supplemental hearing and voted along party lines to advance the nomination. The full Senate confirmed Kavanaugh by a vote of 50–48 on October 6, 2018. Since the death of Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg in 2020, Kavanaugh has come to be regarded as a swing vote on the Court. He was the target of an assassination plot in June 2022.

name: Amy Coney Barrett
education: Graduated magna cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts in English literature from Rhodes College in 1994. Earned a Juris Doctor summa cum laude, ranking first in her class, from Notre Dame Law School in 1997.
careerHistory: 1997-1998: Law clerk for Judge Laurence Silberman of the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals. 1998-1999: Law clerk for Justice Antonin Scalia of the U.S. Supreme Court. 1999-2002: Practiced law at Miller Cassidy Larroca & Lewin (later Baker Botts). 2002-2017: Faculty member at Notre Dame Law School, becoming a professor in 2010. 2017-2020: Judge on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit. 2020-present: Associate Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court.
bio:
Amy Vivian Coney Barrett (born January 28, 1972) is an American lawyer and jurist serving since 2020 as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States. She is the fifth woman to serve on the court. Barrett was nominated by President Donald Trump to succeed Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, and her nomination was confirmed by the U.S. Senate in a 52–48 vote the following month. Her nomination was controversial due to its proximity to the 2020 presidential election. Prior to her elevation, Barrett served as a U.S. circuit judge on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit from 2017 to 2020, becoming the first woman to occupy an Indiana seat on that court.

Barrett graduated from Rhodes College in 1994 with a Bachelor of Arts in English literature, magna cum laude. She then attended Notre Dame Law School, graduating summa cum laude in 1997 and ranking first in her class. After law school, she clerked for Judge Laurence Silberman of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit (1997–1998) and then for Justice Antonin Scalia of the U.S. Supreme Court (1998–1999). She practiced law in Washington, D.C., from 1999 to 2002, during which time she provided research and briefing assistance in the case of Bush v. Gore.

In 2002, Barrett joined the faculty of Notre Dame Law School, becoming a professor of law in 2010. Her scholarship focused on constitutional law, originalism, statutory interpretation, and stare decisis. She received the "Distinguished Professor of the Year" award three times. While a circuit judge, she continued to teach courses at Notre Dame. In 2010, Chief Justice John Roberts appointed her to the Advisory Committee for the Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure.

Described as a protégée of Justice Antonin Scalia, Barrett supports textualism in statutory interpretation and originalism in constitutional interpretation. While generally considered part of the Court's conservative bloc, she has demonstrated a growing pattern of independence and has acted as a swing vote in some controversial cases. Her 2017 confirmation hearing for the Seventh Circuit drew significant attention when her Catholic faith was discussed, a line of questioning that was both criticized and defended by various observers.

name: Neil Gorsuch
education: Columbia University (BA, 1988), Harvard Law School (JD, 1991), and Oxford University (DPhil, 2004).
careerHistory: Law clerk for Judge David B. Sentelle (1991-1992). Law clerk for Justices Byron White and Anthony Kennedy (1993-1994). Private practice attorney at Kellogg, Hansen, Todd, Figel & Frederick (1995-2005). Principal deputy associate attorney general at the U.S. Department of Justice (2005-2006). Judge on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit (2006-2017). Associate Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court (2017-present).
bio: Neil McGill Gorsuch (born August 29, 1967) is an American jurist serving as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States since April 10, 2017. He was nominated by President Donald Trump on January 31, 2017. Gorsuch was born in Denver, Colorado, into a family of attorneys. His mother, Anne Gorsuch Burford, served in the Colorado House of Representatives and was appointed by President Ronald Reagan as the first woman to lead the Environmental Protection Agency. Gorsuch attended Georgetown Preparatory School in Maryland, where he was a classmate of future Justice Brett Kavanaugh. He graduated cum laude from Columbia University in 1988 with a Bachelor of Arts in history and politics, where he co-founded the satirical publication The Fed. He then earned a Juris Doctor, cum laude, from Harvard Law School in 1991, having attended on a Harry S. Truman Scholarship. As a Marshall Scholar, he later received a Doctor of Philosophy in legal philosophy from the University of Oxford in 2004; his doctoral thesis concerned the morality of assisted suicide, supervised by legal philosopher John Finnis. Gorsuch's early legal career included clerkships for Judge David B. Sentelle of the D.C. Circuit (1991–1992) and for U.S. Supreme Court Justices Byron White and Anthony Kennedy (1993–1994). He then worked in private practice from 1995 to 2005 at the law firm Kellogg, Hansen, Todd, Figel & Frederick, becoming a partner in 1998. From 2005 to 2006, he served as Principal Deputy to the Associate Attorney General at the U.S. Department of Justice, where he assisted in managing civil litigation and worked on matters related to national security and detainee policy. On May 10, 2006, President George W. Bush nominated Gorsuch to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit, where he served until his elevation to the Supreme Court. As a jurist, Gorsuch is a proponent of textualism in statutory interpretation and originalism in constitutional interpretation. Along with Justice Clarence Thomas, he is an advocate of natural law jurisprudence. On the Supreme Court, he has authored majority opinions in several landmark cases, including Bostock v. Clayton County (on LGBT rights), McGirt v. Oklahoma (on Indian law), Kennedy v. Bremerton School District (on personal religious observance), and Ramos v. Louisiana (on jury verdicts). He is the first Supreme Court justice to serve alongside a justice for whom he once clerked (Anthony Kennedy). Gorsuch married Louise Burleston, an English equestrienne he met at Oxford, in 1996.

name: Jerome Powell
education: Graduated from Princeton University with a Bachelor of Arts in political science in 1975. Graduated from Georgetown University Law Center with a Juris Doctor in 1979.
careerHistory: 1990-1993: Served in multiple positions at the U.S. Treasury Department, becoming Under Secretary of the Treasury for Domestic Finance in 1992. 1993-1995: Managing director at Bankers Trust. 1997-2005: Partner at the Carlyle Group. 2005: Founded Severn Capital Partners. 2010-2012: Visiting scholar at the Bipartisan Policy Center. 2012-2018: Member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors. 2018–present: Chair of the Federal Reserve.
bio:
Jerome Hayden 'Jay' Powell (born February 4, 1953) is an American investment banker and lawyer who has served as the 16th chair of the Federal Reserve since 2018. A native of Washington, D.C., he earned a Bachelor of Arts in political science from Princeton University in 1975 and a Juris Doctor from Georgetown University Law Center in 1979, where he was editor-in-chief of the Georgetown Law Journal.

After law school, Powell clerked for a federal judge and worked in private legal practice. He began a career in investment banking in 1984 at Dillon, Read & Co., rising to vice president. His first public service role began in 1990 within the United States Department of the Treasury under President George H. W. Bush. In 1992, he was appointed Under Secretary of the Treasury for Domestic Finance. In this role, he oversaw the sanctioning of Salomon Brothers and was involved in negotiations that made Warren Buffett its chairman.

Following his Treasury service, Powell returned to finance, holding senior positions at Bankers Trust and again at Dillon, Read & Co. He was a partner at the Carlyle Group from 1997 to 2005, founding its Industrial Group. He later founded the private equity firm Severn Capital Partners. From 2010 to 2012, he served as a visiting scholar at the Bipartisan Policy Center, focusing on the debt ceiling.

Powell was nominated to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors by President Barack Obama in 2011 and took office in May 2012. He was reappointed to a full 14-year term in 2014. As a governor, he built a reputation as a consensus-builder. He was a skeptic of the third round of quantitative easing but voted for it, endorsed financial regulation to address 'too big to fail' institutions, and expressed concerns about the status of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

President Donald Trump nominated Powell to be Chair of the Federal Reserve in November 2017. He was confirmed by the Senate in January 2018 and assumed the role on February 5, 2018. President Joe Biden renominated him in 2021. His tenure as Chair has involved navigating the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021–2023 inflation surge, and global trade instability. His initial policy included raising interest rates and quantitative tightening, which drew public criticism from President Trump. Under Powell, the Federal Reserve's monetary policies have been associated with a broad uplift in financial markets, apart from declines in 2020 and 2022, leading to a mixed public reception.

name: Jamie Dimon
education: Graduated from Tufts University in 1978 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in economics and psychology, summa cum laude. Graduated from Harvard Business School in 1982 with an M.B.A. as a Baker Scholar.
careerHistory: 1978-1980: Management consultant at Management Analysis Center in Boston. 1982: Joined American Express as an assistant after graduating from Harvard Business School. 1986: Appointed Chief Financial Officer of Commercial Credit, later becoming its president. 1990-1998: Chief Operating Officer of Travelers and Smith Barney. 1998: President of Citigroup. 2000: Appointed CEO of Bank One. 2004: Became President and Chief Operating Officer of JPMorgan Chase after its merger with Bank One. 2006: Became Chairman and CEO of JPMorgan Chase.
bio:
Jamie Dimon (born March 13, 1956) is an American banker and businessman who has been the chairman and chief executive officer of JPMorgan Chase since 2006. Born in New York City and raised in Queens, Dimon is of Greek ancestry. He studied economics and psychology at Tufts University, graduating summa cum laude in 1978, and earned an M.B.A. from Harvard Business School in 1982.

Dimon began his career under the mentorship of Sandy Weill. After graduating, he joined American Express. In 1986, at age 30, he was appointed chief financial officer of Commercial Credit. He later served as chief operating officer of Travelers and Smith Barney from 1990 to 1998, becoming president of Citigroup in 1998 before departing later that year.

In March 2000, Dimon became CEO of Bank One. Following its merger with JPMorgan Chase in 2004, he became president and chief operating officer of the combined company. He was named CEO in 2005 and became chairman in 2006. Under his leadership, JPMorgan Chase became a leading U.S. bank in assets and market capitalization. He served on the board of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York in the late 2010s.

Dimon's tenure has included notable events. In 2012, JPMorgan Chase reported a trading loss of at least $2 billion from a flawed hedging strategy, an episode investigated by regulators and known as the "London Whale." In 2023, he testified in lawsuits accusing the bank of serving Jeffrey Epstein as a client. Professionally, he has served on the executive committee of The Business Council and as a board member and former chairman of the Business Roundtable.

Politically, Dimon donated primarily to the Democratic Party from 1989 to 2009 but later described himself as "barely a Democrat." He was speculated as a potential Treasury Secretary after Barack Obama's 2008 election. He had close ties to some Obama administration officials but often publicly disagreed with certain policies. In 2016, he and JPMorgan Chase supported the UK's Remain campaign against Brexit. In December 2016, he joined a business forum advising President-elect Donald Trump, which later dissolved. He supported the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act but criticized Trump's immigration and trade policies.

Dimon has been featured on Time magazine's list of the world's 100 most influential people multiple times. His compensation has been substantial, reaching $39 million in fiscal year 2024. As of December 2025, Forbes estimated his net worth at $3 billion.

name: David Solomon
education: Attended Hamilton College, earning a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science and government. The text notes he also stated he majored in economics.
careerHistory: After graduating, he worked for Irving Trust, then Drexel Burnham in 1986. He later worked at Bear Stearns, leading its junk bonds division. He joined Goldman Sachs in 1999 as a partner in leveraged finance. He was joint head of the investment banking division from July 2006 to December 2016. He became president and chief operating officer in January 2017, then CEO in October 2018, and chairman in January 2019.
bio:
David Michael Solomon (born January 17, 1962) is an American investment banker. He has been the chief executive officer (CEO) of Goldman Sachs since October 2018 and its chairman since January 2019. Solomon formally succeeded Lloyd Blankfein in these roles.

Before becoming CEO, Solomon served as president and chief operating officer (COO) of Goldman Sachs from January 2017 to September 2018. Prior to that, he was the joint head of the firm's investment banking division from July 2006 to December 2016. He joined Goldman Sachs in 1999 as a partner to work with the leveraged finance team, after previously working at Irving Trust, Drexel Burnham, and Bear Stearns, where he led the junk bonds division.

During his decade leading the investment banking division, Solomon is credited with professionalizing the division and doubling its profit margins from 11% to 22%, while sales rose by 70%. He secured the initial public offering for Lululemon Athletica in 2007. After Gary Cohn's resignation in December 2016, Solomon was elevated to president and co-COO alongside Harvey Schwartz. Following Schwartz's resignation in March 2018, Solomon became the sole heir apparent to Blankfein.

As a leader, Solomon has advocated for reforming company culture, including lowering maximum work hours. He has overseen changes such as increasing pay for programmers, loosening dress codes, modernizing computer systems, and instituting video interviews. His compensation has been reported at various levels, including an $11.85 million package in 2017 and 2018, and a $27.5 million package in 2019. In 2021, his pay was reduced by 39.6% to $17.5 million for 2020 due to the bank's role in the 1MDB scandal.

Solomon is also known for his recreational work as a disc jockey and producer of electronic dance music (EDM) under the name "DJ D-Sol." He performs at nightclubs and festivals and founded the charitable record label Payback Records in 2018. He is a member of The Business Council in Washington, D.C.

name: Ted Pick
education: Studied Russian history and politics at Middlebury College, followed by an MBA from Harvard Business School.
careerHistory: Joined Morgan Stanley as an analyst in 1990. Named managing director in 2002. Became a member of the management committee in 2008. Served as co-president from 2021 to 2023. Became CEO in January 2024 and chairman in January 2025.
bio:
Edward Noel "Ted" Pick (born October 31, 1968) is an American banker and business executive. He is the chief executive officer of Morgan Stanley, a position he assumed in January 2024, and became the company's chairman in January 2025. Prior to these roles, he served as the bank's Co-President, Co-Head of Firm Strategy, and Head of the Institutional Securities Group, where he oversaw Investment Banking, Equities, Fixed Income, Global Capital Markets, and Research.

Pick was born in New York City. His early childhood was spent in Caracas, Venezuela, before his family returned to the United States. He studied Russian history and politics at Middlebury College and later earned an MBA from Harvard Business School.

He began his career at Morgan Stanley as an analyst in 1990 after completing his undergraduate studies and returned to the firm after his MBA. His entry was facilitated through a connection related to former Morgan Stanley chair S. Parker Gilbert. Pick was named a managing director in 2002. By 2005, he was in charge of a division and was involved in capital-raising activities during the 2008 financial crisis. He became a member of the firm's management committee in 2008.

From 2009 to 2015, Pick was involved in global equities trading, a period during which Morgan Stanley surpassed Goldman Sachs as the leading equities business. He was credited as instrumental in this achievement. He subsequently took on the task of rejuvenating Morgan Stanley's fixed-income business, which involved reducing its workforce by 25% and addressing revenue concerns. He later held the position of global head of sales and trading and has held various other roles, including managing director and head of equity capital markets.

Pick served as co-president of Morgan Stanley from 2021 to 2023 before ascending to the roles of CEO and chairman. He is a member of The Business Council.

In his personal life, Pick married Betsey Kittenplan in 2000, and they have two daughters. He lives in New York's Upper East Side and maintains a vacation home in Martha's Vineyard. He is a Trustee at the Metropolitan Museum of Art and enjoys math problems.

name: Brian Moynihan
currentRole: 董事会主席兼首席执行官
education: Graduated from Brown University in 1981 with a history major. Earned a Juris Doctor from the University of Notre Dame Law School.
careerHistory: Joined Fleet Boston bank as deputy general counsel in April 1993. Served as executive vice president managing Fleet's brokerage and wealth management division from 1999 to April 2004. After Bank of America merged with FleetBoston in 2004, he joined BofA as president of global wealth and investment management. Became CEO of Merrill Lynch after its sale to BofA in September 2008. Was promoted to chairman, president, and CEO of Bank of America in 2010.
bio:
Brian Thomas Moynihan is an American lawyer and banker. He is the chairman, president, and chief executive officer of Bank of America, having been promoted to these positions in 2010. Moynihan was born in Marietta, Ohio, into a Catholic family of Irish descent. He graduated from Brown University in 1981 with a degree in history, where he co-captained the rugby team. He later earned a Juris Doctor from the University of Notre Dame Law School and began his career as a lawyer at the firm Edwards & Angell LLP in Providence, Rhode Island.

Moynihan's banking career began when he joined FleetBoston bank in 1993 as a deputy general counsel. He rose to become an executive vice president, managing Fleet's brokerage and wealth management division. Following Bank of America's merger with FleetBoston Financial in 2004, he joined Bank of America as president of global wealth and investment management. In January 2009, he became president of consumer and small business banking. After the sale of Merrill Lynch to Bank of America in 2008, he was named its CEO, and he succeeded Ken Lewis as CEO of Bank of America in 2010.

His tenure as CEO has included notable events. In 2011, he secured a $5 billion investment from Warren Buffett, a move that drew market scrutiny. That same year, he reversed a plan to charge a $5 monthly fee for debit card users after significant customer backlash. His leadership has also faced criticism. During the 2012 shareholder meeting, he addressed complaints about the bank's mortgage servicing operations and declining share price. That year, Senator Bernie Sanders criticized Bank of America in a report on corporate tax avoidance, noting the bank paid no federal income tax in 2010 and received a tax refund. In 2025, he was publicly rebuked by former President Donald Trump for the bank's client policies, to which Moynihan responded that the bank serves "everybody." He later spoke against the "over-regulation" of banks.

Moynihan holds several external board positions. He is a member of the Council on Competitiveness board and the Partnership for Rhode Island board. He is also a fellow at Brown University and became the Chancellor of the university in July 2024. Additionally, he is a member of The Business Council, the Business Roundtable, and sits on the steering committee of the Council for Inclusive Capitalism. In 2020, he received Chief Executive magazine's peer-selected "CEO Of The Year" award. In 2023, he was honored as a "Distinguished Bostonian" by the Greater Boston Chamber of Commerce.

In his personal life, Moynihan lives in Wellesley, Massachusetts, with his wife, Susan, and their three children. He commutes between Boston and Bank of America's headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, using company private jets, a practice he has defended as necessary for his role.

name: Jane Fraser
currentRole: 董事会主席兼首席执行官
education: Graduated with a BA (later MA) in economics from Girton College, Cambridge in 1988. Earned an MBA from Harvard Business School in 1994.
careerHistory: July 1988 - July 1990: Mergers and acquisitions analyst at Goldman Sachs, London. August 1990 - June 1992: Brokerage associate for Asesores Bursátiles, Madrid. 1994 - 2004: Worked at McKinsey & Company, rising to partner. July 2004: Joined Citigroup as Head of Client Strategy. October 2007 - May 2009: Global Head of Strategy and Mergers and Acquisitions at Citigroup. June 2009: Became CEO of Citi Private Bank. May 2013: Appointed CEO of CitiMortgage. March 2014: Promoted to CEO of US Consumer and Commercial Banking. April 2015: Named CEO of Citigroup Latin America. October 2019: Appointed President of Citigroup and Head of Global Consumer Banking. February 2021: Became CEO of Citigroup. October 2025: Elected Chair of the board of directors of Citigroup.
bio:
Jane Fraser (born 13 July 1967) is a British-American banking executive. She is the chief executive officer (CEO) and chair of Citigroup, positions she has held since March 2021 and October 2025, respectively. Educated at Girton College, Cambridge, where she earned a degree in economics, and Harvard Business School, where she earned an MBA, Fraser began her career as a mergers and acquisitions analyst at Goldman Sachs in London. She later worked for a securities broker in Madrid before joining McKinsey & Company in 1994. At McKinsey, she rose to partner, co-authored the book 'Race for the World: Strategies to Build a Great Global Firm', and her work there led to an invitation to join Citigroup in 2004.

Fraser joined Citigroup as Head of Client Strategy in its investment and global banking division. She was promoted to Global Head of Strategy and Mergers and Acquisitions in 2007, a role she held during the 2008 financial crisis, working on the bank's restructuring. In 2009, she became CEO of Citi Private Bank, returning it to profitability. Subsequent leadership roles included CEO of CitiMortgage (2013), CEO of US Consumer and Commercial Banking (2014), and CEO of Citigroup Latin America (2015), where she oversaw operations in 24 countries. In October 2019, she was appointed President of Citigroup and Head of Global Consumer Banking.

In September 2020, Citigroup announced Fraser would succeed Michael Corbat as CEO, making her the first woman to head a major U.S. bank upon her assumption of the role in February 2021. Her tenure has included instituting flexible work policies and leading strategic reviews, including discussions on a potential public listing for Banamex in Mexico. In October 2025, she was elected Chair of Citigroup's board of directors.

Fraser has been recognized on Fortune's 'Most Powerful Women in Business' list multiple times, named the 'Number 1 Woman to Watch' by American Banker in 2014 and 2015, and ranked by Forbes as the eighth most powerful woman in the world in 2025. She serves as a member of the President's Export Council and holds memberships in several organizations, including the Council on Foreign Relations and the Economic Club of New York. Fraser is married with two sons and became a U.S. citizen in 2001.

name: Charlie Scharf
education: Received a BA from Johns Hopkins University in 1987. Earned an Executive MBA from New York University Stern School of Business in 1991.
careerHistory: 1987: Hired for a back-office job at Commercial Credit. 1995-1999: CFO of Salomon Smith Barney. 1999-2000: CFO of Citigroup's global corporate and investment bank division. 2000-2002: CFO of Bank One. 2002-2004: CEO of Bank One's retail division. 2004-2011: CEO of JPMorgan Chase's retail financial services business. 2011-2012: Managing director of One Equity Partners. 2012-2016: CEO of Visa Inc. 2017-2019: CEO of Bank of New York Mellon (BNY). 2019-present: President and CEO of Wells Fargo (Chairman from October 2025).
bio:
Charles W. Scharf (born April 24, 1965) is an American business executive. He is the chairman and chief executive officer (CEO) of Wells Fargo, having become CEO in October 2019 and chairman in October 2025. Scharf was born in New York City and grew up in Westfield, New Jersey. He earned a BA from Johns Hopkins University in 1987 and an Executive MBA from New York University Stern School of Business in 1991.

Scharf's career in finance began in 1987 with an introduction to Jamie Dimon, who hired him at Commercial Credit. His career progressed through various roles at companies associated with Dimon and Sandy Weill, including Primerica, Smith Barney, Salomon Brothers, Travelers, Citigroup, Bank One, and JPMorgan Chase. He served as CFO of Salomon Smith Barney from 1995 to 1999 and later as CFO of Citigroup's global corporate and investment bank division from 1999 to 2000. At Bank One, he was CFO from 2000 to 2002 and CEO of its retail division from 2002 to 2004. Following Bank One's merger with JPMorgan Chase, he was chief executive of JPMorgan Chase's retail financial services business from 2004 to 2011, where he orchestrated the acquisition and integration of Washington Mutual in 2008. He was a managing director of One Equity Partners from 2011 to November 2012.

Scharf served as CEO of Visa Inc. from November 2012 until his resignation in December 2016. He was CEO of Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) from July 2017 to September 2019 and its chairman from January 2018 to September 2019.

As CEO of Wells Fargo, Scharf was tasked with leading the bank's cleanup and turnaround efforts. This included appointing new executives, committing to major cost cuts, exiting unprofitable businesses, and reworking risk management and controls. His efforts were credited by analysts as instrumental in the Federal Reserve's decision to lift a punitive asset cap on the bank in June 2025. In 2024, his total compensation from Wells Fargo was $31.2 million.

Beyond his corporate roles, Scharf served on the President’s Advisory Council on Financial Capability for Young Americans under President Barack Obama. He serves on the board of directors of Microsoft, is a member of The Business Council, vice chair of the Bank Policy Institute, and an emeritus trustee of Johns Hopkins University.

Scharf is married to Amy and they have two daughters. They live in New York.

name: Larry Fink
education: Earned a BA in political science from UCLA in 1974 and an MBA in real estate from the UCLA Anderson School of Management in 1976.
careerHistory: 1976: Started career at First Boston investment bank, eventually managing its bond department and co-heading the Taxable Fixed Income Division. 1988: Co-founded BlackRock under The Blackstone Group, becoming its Director and CEO. 1994: Retained Director and CEO positions after BlackRock split from Blackstone. 1998: Became Chairman of BlackRock after it became independent. 1999: Led BlackRock through its initial public offering.
bio:
Laurence Douglas "Larry" Fink (born November 2, 1952) is an American billionaire businessman, co-founder, chairman, and chief executive officer of BlackRock, the world's largest money-management firm with over US$10 trillion in assets under management. Born in Van Nuys, California, to a Jewish family, he earned a BA in political science in 1974 and an MBA in real estate in 1976, both from UCLA.

Fink began his career in 1976 at the investment bank First Boston, where he became a pioneering mortgage-backed securities trader and managed the bond department. A significant trading loss in 1986 influenced his focus on risk management. In 1988, under The Blackstone Group's umbrella, he co-founded BlackRock, serving as its director and CEO. He retained these roles when BlackRock split from Blackstone in 1994, becoming chairman in 1998 after the firm's independence. BlackRock went public in 1999.

In the 21st century, Fink oversaw BlackRock's expansion, including the 2006 merger with Merrill Lynch Investment Managers, which doubled its assets, and the 2009 acquisition of Barclays Global Investors, cementing its position as the global leader. The U.S. government contracted BlackRock to aid recovery after the 2008 financial crisis, leading to close relationships with officials. Fink has been a regular commentator on CNBC. In 2025, Time magazine listed him as one of the world's 100 most influential people, and he serves as Co-Chairman of the World Economic Forum.

Fink is noted for his annual open letters to CEOs, advocating for corporate social responsibility, environmental sustainability, and addressing climate change as a core investment consideration. He has called on companies to improve their environmental impact, community relations, and workforce diversity. However, his and BlackRock's actions have drawn scrutiny and criticism, including being named a top US "climate villain" in 2022 due to profiting from deforestation and investments in fossil fuel infrastructure.

His community involvement includes board positions at New York University (where he chairs the Financial Affairs Committee), the NYU Langone Medical Center, the Boys and Girls Club of New York, and the Robin Hood Foundation. He founded the Lori and Laurence Fink Center for Finance & Investments at UCLA Anderson. Fink joined a business forum for President-elect Donald Trump in 2016. Personally, he has been married to Lori Weider since 1974, has three children, and is a lifelong supporter of the Democratic Party. His net worth was estimated at US$1.2 billion in April 2024.

name: Elon Musk
education: Received bachelor's degrees in 1997 from the University of Pennsylvania.
careerHistory: 1995: Co-founded the software company Zip2. 1999: Co-founded the online payment company X.com, which later became PayPal. 2002: Founded SpaceX, becoming its CEO and chief engineer. 2004: Joined Tesla as an early investor, later becoming CEO and product architect in 2008. 2015: Co-founded OpenAI. 2016: Co-founded Neuralink. 2017: Founded the Boring Company. 2022: Acquired Twitter (rebranded to X in 2023). 2025: Served as Senior Advisor to the President and de facto head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) before leaving the administration.
bio: Elon Reeve Musk (born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and entrepreneur. He was born into a wealthy family in Pretoria, South Africa, and holds South African and Canadian citizenship from birth. He emigrated to Canada in 1989. Musk received bachelor's degrees from the University of Pennsylvania in the United States in 1997. He became an American citizen in 2002. Musk is known for his leadership of several major companies. His business career began in 1995 when he co-founded the software company Zip2. After its sale in 1999, he co-founded the online payment company X.com, which later merged to form PayPal and was acquired by eBay in 2002. In 2002, he founded the space technology company SpaceX, where he serves as CEO and chief engineer. Musk joined the automaker Tesla as an early investor in 2004 and became its CEO and product architect in 2008. In 2015, he co-founded OpenAI but later left, subsequently establishing the artificial intelligence company xAI. In 2022, he acquired the social network Twitter, rebranding it as X in 2023. His other ventures include co-founding the neurotechnology company Neuralink in 2016 and founding the tunneling company the Boring Company in 2017. As of December 2025, Forbes estimates his net worth to be around US$717 billion, and he has been the wealthiest person in the world since 2021. In November 2025, a Tesla pay package worth $1 trillion for Musk was approved, to be received over 10 years if specific goals are met. Musk's political involvement became prominent when he served as the largest donor in the 2024 U.S. presidential election, supporting Donald Trump. Following Trump's inauguration in early 2025, Musk served as Senior Advisor to the President and as the de facto head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). However, after a public feud with Trump, Musk left the Trump administration and returned to managing his companies. Musk is a supporter of global far-right figures, causes, and political parties. His political activities, views, and statements have made him a polarizing figure. He has been criticized for promoting COVID-19 misinformation, conspiracy theories, and affirming antisemitic, racist, and transphobic comments. His acquisition of Twitter was controversial due to a subsequent increase in hate speech and misinformation following his pledge to decrease censorship. His role in the second Trump administration, particularly in the DOGE, attracted public backlash.

name: Jensen Huang
education: Earned a Bachelor of Science (BS) from Oregon State University in 1984 and a Master of Science (MS) in electrical engineering from Stanford University in 1992.
careerHistory: After graduating college, he worked as a microchip designer at Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). He then left AMD to become a technical officer at LSI Logic, where he was later promoted to director of its CoreWare division. In 1993, he co-founded Nvidia and has served as its president and CEO since its founding.
bio:
Jen-Hsun Huang, commonly anglicized as Jensen Huang, is a Taiwanese and American business executive, electrical engineer, and philanthropist. He was born on February 17, 1963, in Taipei, Taiwan, and moved to Tainan as a child. His parents were Huang Hsing-tai, a chemical engineer, and Lo Tsai-hsiu, a schoolteacher. The family relocated to Thailand when he was five, where he attended Ruamrudee International School in Bangkok. At age nine, he and his older brother were sent to the United States, initially living with an uncle in Tacoma, Washington. They were mistakenly enrolled in the Oneida Baptist Institute, a religious reform academy in Kentucky, where Huang attended Oneida Elementary school. After two years, his parents moved to Beaverton, Oregon, and he attended Aloha High School in Aloha, Oregon, graduating at age 16. He worked at a Denny's restaurant from 1978 to 1983. Huang earned a Bachelor of Science in electrical engineering from Oregon State University in 1984 and later a Master of Science in electrical engineering from Stanford University in 1992 while working in Silicon Valley.

Huang began his career as a microchip designer at Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). He later moved to LSI Logic as a technical officer, working on a contract with Sun Microsystems. There, he collaborated with engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem on the GX graphics engine, a successful graphics accelerator card. Huang was promoted to director of LSI's CoreWare division.

In 1993, Huang co-founded Nvidia Corporation with Malachowsky and Priem. The company was conceived during meetings at a Denny's diner in East San Jose. Huang signed the articles of incorporation on April 5, 1993, and became the company's president and chief executive officer from its first day of operation, securing initial funding from venture capitalists including Don Valentine of Sequoia Capital. He has remained president and CEO since its founding, leading the company from near-bankruptcy in the 1990s into GPU production, high-performance computing, and artificial intelligence (AI). Under his leadership, Nvidia experienced rapid growth during the AI boom, becoming the world's largest company by market capitalization and the first to reach a market capitalization of over $5 trillion in October 2025. As of January 2026, Forbes estimated his net worth at US$164.1 billion.

Huang has received numerous accolades. Time magazine included him in their Time 100 list of the most influential people in 2021 and 2024, and in 2025 named him one of the "Architects of AI" for Time's Person of the Year. He is married to Lori Huang (since 1985).

name: Tim Cook
education: Received a Bachelor of Science in industrial engineering from Auburn University in 1982 and a Master of Business Administration from Duke University in 1988.
careerHistory: After graduating in 1982, Cook spent twelve years at IBM's personal computer business, ultimately as director of North American fulfillment. He later became COO of the computer reseller division of Intelligent Electronics, and in 1997 became vice president for corporate materials at Compaq. He joined Apple in March 1998 as a senior vice president for worldwide operations, later serving as vice president for worldwide sales and operations and then as COO. He was appointed CEO of Apple on August 24, 2011. Outside Apple, he has sat on the board of directors of Nike since 2005.

name: Satya Nadella
education: Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Manipal Institute of Technology (1988), MS in computer science from University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (1990), and MBA from University of Chicago Booth School of Business (1997).
careerHistory: Worked at Sun Microsystems as a member of its technology staff (before 1992). Joined Microsoft in 1992. Served as executive vice president of Microsoft's cloud and enterprise group. Succeeded Steve Ballmer as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Microsoft in 2014. Succeeded John W. Thompson as Chairman of Microsoft in 2021.
bio:
Satya Narayana Nadella (born 19 August 1967) is an Indian-American business executive. He is the chairman and chief executive officer (CEO) of Microsoft, having succeeded Steve Ballmer as CEO in 2014 and John W. Thompson as chairman in 2021. Prior to becoming CEO, he served as the executive vice president of Microsoft's cloud and enterprise group, responsible for the company's computing platforms.

Nadella was born in Hyderabad, India, into a Telugu Hindu family. His father, Bukkapuram Nadella Yugandhar, was an Indian Administrative Service officer, and his mother, Prabhavati, was a Sanskrit lecturer. He attended the Hyderabad Public School, Begumpet, before earning a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the Manipal Institute of Technology in 1988. He then moved to the United States, receiving a Master of Science in computer science from the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee in 1990. He later earned an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business in 1997.

His career began at Sun Microsystems as a member of its technology staff. He joined Microsoft in 1992. Beyond his role at Microsoft, Nadella has held several board positions, including on the Board of Directors of Starbucks (2017–2024), the Board of Trustees of the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, and the Board of Trustees of the University of Chicago. He served as Chairman of The Business Council from 2021 to 2022.

Nadella has received significant recognition. He was a Time 100 honoree in 2018 and 2024, named Financial Times Person of the Year and Fortune Magazine Businessperson of the Year in 2019. He received the CNN-News18 Indian of the Year award in 2014 and was recognized as a Global Indian Business Icon at the CNBC-TV18 India Business Leader Awards in 2020. The Government of India awarded him the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman in 2015 and the Padma Bhushan, its third-highest civilian award, in 2022. He also received an honorary PhD from the Georgia Institute of Technology in 2024.

In his personal life, Nadella married Anupama Priyadarshini in 1992. The couple has three children, a son (deceased) and two daughters, and resides in Clyde Hill and Bellevue, Washington. His son Zain, who had cerebral palsy, was a legally blind quadriplegic and died in February 2022 at age 26. Nadella is an avid reader of American and Indian poetry and enjoys cricket, having played on his school team. He and his wife are part of the ownership group of the Seattle Sounders FC, a Major League Soccer club. In 2017, he published a book titled *Hit Refresh: The Quest to Rediscover Microsoft's Soul and Imagine a Better Future for Everyone*.

name: Sundar Pichai
education: Earned a B.Tech in metallurgical engineering from IIT Kharagpur, an MS from Stanford University in materials science and engineering, and an MBA from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania.
careerHistory: Began career as a materials engineer. Worked in engineering and product management at Applied Materials and in management consulting at McKinsey & Company. Joined Google in 2004, leading product management for Chrome, ChromeOS, and Google Drive, later overseeing Gmail and Google Maps. Appointed CEO of Google on August 10, 2015, stepping into the position on October 24, 2015. Became CEO of Alphabet Inc. in December 2019.
bio:
Sundar Pichai, born Sundararajan Pichai on June 10, 1972, in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India, is an Indian-American business executive. He is the chief executive officer (CEO) of Alphabet Inc. and its subsidiary Google, a role he has held since 2015. Pichai completed his schooling in Chennai and earned a B.Tech in metallurgical engineering from IIT Kharagpur. He holds an MS from Stanford University in materials science and engineering and an MBA from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania.

Pichai began his career as a materials engineer and worked in product management at Applied Materials and in management consulting at McKinsey & Company. He joined Google in 2004, where he led product management and innovation for a suite of Google's client software products. He was largely responsible for Google Chrome, ChromeOS, and Google Drive, and later oversaw the development of applications such as Gmail and Google Maps. On March 13, 2013, Pichai added Android to the list of Google products he oversaw.

On August 10, 2015, Pichai was selected to become the next CEO of Google, after previously being appointed chief product officer by then-CEO Larry Page. He stepped into the position on October 24, 2015, following the formation of Alphabet Inc., the new holding company for Google. He was appointed to the Alphabet Board of Directors in 2017. In December 2019, Pichai became the CEO of Alphabet Inc. His compensation from the company topped $200 million in 2022.

Pichai's tenure has included several notable events. In August 2017, he drew publicity for firing a Google employee who wrote a manifesto criticizing the company's diversity policies. On December 11, 2018, he was questioned by the United States House Judiciary Committee on issues including possible political bias, plans for a search app in China, and privacy practices. In April 2024, after employees were fired for protesting against Project Nimbus, Pichai stated that the office is not a place to fight over disruptive issues or debate politics.

Pichai has received significant recognition. He was included in Time magazine's annual list of the 100 most influential people in 2016 and 2020, and the Time 100 AI list in 2024. He was awarded the 2021 Asia Game Changer Award by the Asia Society. In 2022, he received the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian award, from the Government of India in the category of Trade and Industry. As of May 2025, his net worth is estimated at $1.1 billion.

In his personal life, Pichai is married to Anjali Pichai (née Haryani), whom he met while studying at IIT Kharagpur. They have two children. His recreational interests include cricket and soccer, and he lives in Los Altos Hills, California.

name: Mark Zuckerberg
education: Briefly attended Harvard College, studying psychology and computer science, but dropped out in his second year. Previously attended Phillips Exeter Academy.
careerHistory: Co-founded Facebook (later Meta Platforms) in February 2004 while at Harvard. Dropped out of Harvard in his second year to focus on the company. Became the world's youngest self-made billionaire in 2008. Took Facebook public in May 2012. Serves as chairman and CEO of Meta Platforms and is co-founder and co-CEO of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.
bio: Mark Elliot Zuckerberg (born May 14, 1984) is an American businessman and programmer. He is the co-founder, chairman, and chief executive officer (CEO) of Meta Platforms, the parent company of the social media service Facebook, which he also co-founded. Zuckerberg co-founded and serves as co-CEO of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. He briefly attended Harvard College, where he launched Facebook in February 2004 with his roommates Eduardo Saverin, Andrew McCollum, Dustin Moskovitz, and Chris Hughes. He dropped out of Harvard in his second year to focus on the company. Zuckerberg took Facebook public in May 2012, retaining majority shares. In 2008, at age 23, he became the world's youngest self-made billionaire and has consistently ranked among the world's wealthiest individuals, with an estimated net worth of US$220 billion as of December 2025. His early career, legal troubles, and initial success were depicted in the 2010 film The Social Network, which won multiple Academy Awards. Zuckerberg's prominence has prompted significant political and legal attention. He has been the subject of multiple lawsuits regarding the creation and ownership of Facebook, as well as issues concerning user privacy. In 2012, he met with then-Russian Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev in Moscow to discuss stimulating social media innovation in Russia and boosting Facebook's position there.
