He has also hosted visiting Chinese politician Lu Wei. Zuckerberg has used his funds to organize large donations, including establishing the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. He was added to MIT Technology Review's TR35 list in 2007 as one of the top 35 innovators under 35. Vanity Fair named him number one on its 2010 list of the most influential people of the Information Age. At the 2013 TechCrunch Disrupt conference, he discussed the Internet.org project, aiming to increase global internet access. He was the keynote speaker at the 2014 Mobile World Congress, emphasizing mobile technology's importance for Facebook's future.

name: Andy Jassy
education: Graduated cum laude from Harvard College in government and earned an MBA from Harvard Business School.
careerHistory: Joined Amazon as a marketing manager in 1997. Became SVP and CEO of Amazon Web Services from 2003 to 2021. Promoted to President and Chief Executive Officer of Amazon in July 2021.
bio:
Andrew R. Jassy (born January 13, 1968) is an American business executive. He is the president and chief executive officer of Amazon, a role he assumed in July 2021, succeeding founder Jeff Bezos. Jassy was previously the senior vice president and chief executive officer of Amazon Web Services (AWS) from 2003 to 2021.

Jassy was born to Margery and Everett L. Jassy in Scarsdale, New York, and is of Jewish Hungarian ancestry. His father was a senior partner at the law firm Dewey Ballantine. Jassy attended Scarsdale High School, where he played varsity soccer and tennis. He graduated cum laude from Harvard College with a degree in government, serving as advertising manager for The Harvard Crimson, and later earned an MBA from Harvard Business School.

After graduation, Jassy worked as a project manager for the collectibles company MBI and co-founded a short-lived company before joining Amazon as a marketing manager in 1997. In 2003, he and Jeff Bezos conceived the idea for Amazon Web Services, the cloud computing platform that launched in 2006. Jassy led the initial AWS team of 57 people. He was promoted to CEO of AWS in 2016. In 2017, he was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. From 2018 to 2021, he served as a member of the National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence (NSCAI).

Upon becoming CEO of Amazon in 2021, Jassy received a long-term compensation package valued at $212.7 million, largely in stock. As of 2024, he has emphasized Amazon's strategic focus on artificial intelligence, with plans for significant capital expenditure directed towards AWS and generative AI. In 2025, Time magazine included him in its TIME100 AI list, and he was elected to the National Academy of Engineering. He has also been recognized as Person of the Year by the Financial Times in 2016.

Jassy married fashion designer Elana Rochelle Caplan in 1997. They have two children and reside in Seattle's Capitol Hill neighborhood. He is the chairman of Rainier Prep, a charter school in Seattle, and is a member of The Business Council.

name: Sam Altman
education: Attended Stanford University for two years studying computer science, but dropped out in 2005 without earning a degree.
careerHistory: 2005: Co-founded and served as CEO of Loopt. 2011: Became a partner at Y Combinator. 2014-2019: Served as President of Y Combinator (later YC Group). 2019-present: Serves as CEO of OpenAI (with a brief ouster and reinstatement in November 2023). Also served as Chairman of Helion Energy and Oklo (stepping down from Oklo in April 2025).
bio:
Samuel Harris Altman (born April 22, 1985) is an American businessman and entrepreneur. He has served as the chief executive officer (CEO) of the artificial intelligence research organization OpenAI since 2019. He is widely considered a leading figure of the AI boom, having overseen the successful launch of ChatGPT in 2022. In 2025, he was named among the "Architects of AI" for Time's Person of the Year.

Altman was born in Chicago, Illinois, to a Jewish family and grew up in Clayton, Missouri. He received his first computer at age eight and attended John Burroughs School. He studied computer science at Stanford University for two years before dropping out in 2005.

His business career began in 2005 when he co-founded Loopt, a location-based social networking app, serving as its CEO and raising over $30 million in venture capital. The company was acquired in 2012. In 2011, Altman joined the startup accelerator Y Combinator (YC), becoming its president in 2014 and later president of YC Group in 2016. He aimed to expand YC's funding scope, particularly for "hard technology" startups. His relationship with YC ended in early 2020.

As an investor, Altman co-founded Hydrazine Capital in 2012. His investment portfolio includes stakes in over 400 companies. He is also chairman of the board for the nuclear fusion company Helion Energy and was chairman of Oklo Inc., a clean energy company, until stepping down in April 2025 to avoid potential conflicts of interest with OpenAI.

His tenure at OpenAI has been marked by significant turmoil. In November 2023, OpenAI's board removed him as CEO, citing a lack of confidence and inconsistent candor. This triggered a strong backlash from employees and investors. After five days of negotiations and a threatened mass exodus of staff to Microsoft, Altman was reinstated as CEO with a new board.

Politically, Altman contemplated running for governor of California in 2018 but decided against it. In 2018, he announced "the United Slate," a political project focused on housing and healthcare policy. He has held fundraisers for Democratic candidates, including Andrew Yang, and donated to a super PAC supporting Joe Biden. Altman supports land value taxation and universal basic income.

name: Darren Woods
education: He earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Texas A&M University, followed by an MBA from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management.
careerHistory: Joined Exxon in 1992. Prior to becoming CEO, ran the refining and chemical divisions of ExxonMobil. Became CEO and chairman of ExxonMobil in January 2017.
bio:
Darren Wayne Woods (born December 16, 1965) is an American businessman who has been the chairman and chief executive officer (CEO) of ExxonMobil since January 2017. He was born in Wichita, Kansas, and spent much of his youth living near various U.S. military bases worldwide due to his father's work. Woods earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Texas A&M University and an MBA from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management.

Woods joined Exxon in 1992. He worked for the company for 24 years before being promoted to CEO following Rex Tillerson's nomination as U.S. Secretary of State. Prior to becoming CEO, Woods ran the company's refining and chemical divisions, which delivered the majority of ExxonMobil's net income in 2016. Unlike his predecessor, who focused on deal-making and exploration, Woods is a veteran of the refining side of the oil business.

Upon becoming CEO, Woods outlined a growth plan focusing on drilling in the Permian Basin and the Bakken shale formation. He has publicly endorsed the Paris Agreement and, in 2017, urged President Trump to keep the U.S. in the accord, arguing it would allow the U.S. to ensure a level playing field. Woods has stated that technologies like horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing have "shattered the Peak Oil myth."

His tenure has involved significant focus on climate and emissions. In 2020, reports indicated Exxon, under an investment plan signed by Woods, was set to significantly increase its annual carbon emissions, though the company stated internal projections had changed. In 2021, he was named a top "climate villain" by The Guardian after lobbyists revealed efforts to obstruct climate legislation. That same year, he denied that Exxon covered up its own climate research and declined to stop lobbying against climate initiatives.

Woods has presented a long-term strategy involving investment in carbon capture and storage (CCS) and direct air capture (DAC) technology, while also calling for a higher carbon price. In 2024, he noted DAC technology remained costly and needed to become cheaper to scale. He has stated that company investments in CCS and DAC could change if related tax credits are repealed. In 2023, his compensation was $31 million, rising to $44.1 million in 2024. Woods is a member of The Business Council.

name: Mike Wirth
education: Attended the University of Colorado, earning a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering in 1982.
careerHistory: 1982: Joined Chevron as a design engineer. 2001: Became president of marketing for Chevron's Asia, Africa and Middle East region. Later served as vice chairman of Chevron. 2018: Became chairman and CEO of Chevron.
bio: Michael K. Wirth (born October 15, 1960) is an American businessman. He has been the chairman and chief executive officer of Chevron Corporation since 2018, having previously served as the company's vice chairman. Wirth earned a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from the University of Colorado in 1982, where he also played football and basketball. He joined Chevron as a design engineer in 1982 and worked in multiple sectors including engineering, construction, and operations. In 2001, he became president of marketing for Chevron's Asia, Africa, and Middle East region. He has served on the board of directors for Caltex Australia and GS Caltex. Wirth succeeded John S. Watson as CEO of Chevron in 2018. He is a member of the board of the American Petroleum Institute, an oil industry trade group. Under his leadership, Chevron has been cited as responsible for one of the highest total carbon sequestration efforts of any private company worldwide. However, the company has also been involved in several greenwashing tactics and was found by the Federal Trade Commission to have misled customers about its efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. In response to questions about investing in alternative energy, Wirth stated Chevron would rather return money to shareholders for them to invest elsewhere. In November 2025, he attended a White House dinner for Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Personally, Wirth and his wife have four adult children. He relocated to Houston, Texas, in 2024 as part of Chevron's corporate headquarters move from California. He maintains a routine of sleeping by 10:00 PM and waking at 3:45 AM for a 90-minute gym session.

name: John Furner
education: Graduated from the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville's Sam M. Walton College of Business in 1996, where he studied marketing management.
careerHistory: 1993: Began career as an hourly store associate at Walmart. Later became store manager, district manager, and buyer. Served as EVP of merchandising and marketing for Walmart China for nearly three years. February 1, 2017: Became CEO of Sam's Club. November 2019: Became President and CEO of Walmart U.S.
bio:
John Furner (born 1974) is an American business executive. He was born in Jacksonville, Arkansas. Furner attended the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville, where he studied marketing management and graduated from the Sam M. Walton College of Business in 1996.

Furner began his career at Walmart in 1993 as an hourly store associate. He advanced through the company, holding positions including store manager, district manager, and buyer. His career later expanded into Walmart's international operations, where he spent nearly three years as Executive Vice President of merchandising and marketing for Walmart China. Upon returning to the United States, he served as the chief merchandising officer for Sam's Club before being appointed its President and Chief Executive Officer on February 1, 2017.

During his tenure as CEO of Sam's Club, Furner implemented strategic changes to enhance the division's competitiveness. This included closing 63 stores to better compete with rival Costco, a move reported by The Wall Street Journal alongside increased sales. Leveraging his experience in China, he focused on integrating more technology into Sam's Club warehouses and refining the membership warehouse club's target customer base. He also emphasized growing the private brand business of Sam's Club.

In November 2019, Furner was appointed president and chief executive officer of Walmart U.S., the company's largest operating segment. It has been announced that he will succeed Doug McMillon as the CEO of Walmart Inc. in early 2026.

Outside of his corporate roles, Furner holds leadership positions in industry and philanthropic organizations. He serves as the board chairman of the National Retail Federation. In 2020, he was a board member of the Medal of Honor Foundation. In his personal life, Furner is married and has four children.

name: David Joyner
education: Graduated with a Bachelor of Science degree in Electronic engineering technology from the ITT Technical Institute in Indianapolis, Indiana.
careerHistory: Software analyst at Texas Instruments (six years). Physical performer of Barney on Barney & the Backyard Gang and Barney & Friends (1991-2001, with occasional appearances until 2005 and a brief return in 2008). Performer of the title character on Hip Hop Harry. Works as a tantric massage therapist.
bio:
David Eugene Joyner is an American actor and therapist. He is best known for physically portraying the character of Barney the dinosaur on the children's television series 'Barney & Friends' and its predecessor 'Barney & the Backyard Gang' from 1991 to 2001. The character's voice during this period was provided by Bob West, Duncan Brannan, and Tim Dever. Joyner later played the title character of 'Hip Hop Harry'.

Joyner attended MacArthur High School and graduated with a Bachelor of Science degree in Electronic engineering technology from the ITT Technical Institute in Indianapolis, Indiana. Prior to his acting career, he worked as a software analyst for Texas Instruments for six years.

Joyner originally auditioned for the role of Barney in 1991, replacing the original costume actor, David Voss. He was initially cast as the back-up performer but assumed the primary role after the originally chosen actress had difficulty staying in the costume for extended periods. He was first cast to play Barney in two 'Barney & the Backyard Gang' home videos and continued in the subsequent television series 'Barney & Friends' for its first six seasons, as well as in live performances. After the fourth season, he left to film 'Barney's Great Adventure' and was temporarily replaced by Josh Martin and Maurice Scott. Joyner returned to perform as Barney in 'Barney in Outer Space' in 1997. Although he left the series, he continued to make occasional appearances as the character until 2005, with a brief return in 2008. He was eventually replaced by Carey Stinson.

Outside of his acting career, David Joyner also works as a tantric massage therapist.

name: Stephen Hemsley
education: Graduated from Fordham University in 1974.
careerHistory: Began career at Arthur Andersen as Managing Partner and Chief Financial Officer. Joined UnitedHealth Group in 1997, serving in senior financial roles. Became President and Chief Operating Officer in 1999. Appointed CEO in 2006. Stepped down as CEO in 2017, becoming Executive Chairman. Reappointed as CEO in May 2025.
bio: Stephen J. Hemsley (born June 4, 1952) is an American businessman. He graduated from Fordham University in 1974. Hemsley began his professional career at the accounting firm Arthur Andersen, where he served as Managing Partner and Chief Financial Officer. In 1997, he joined UnitedHealth Group Inc., initially serving in senior financial roles. He rose to become President and Chief Operating Officer in 1999. In 2006, Hemsley was appointed Chief Executive Officer of UnitedHealth Group, succeeding William W. McGuire. Under his leadership, the company consistently ranked among the top U.S. companies by revenue. In August 2017, UnitedHealth announced that Hemsley would be stepping down as CEO after more than a decade and transitioning to the newly created role of Executive Chairman of the board. In May 2025, Hemsley returned to his prior post, being reappointed as CEO of UnitedHealth Group. In May 2024, a lawsuit was filed against Hemsley, then-UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, and two other senior executives. The lawsuit alleged fraud and insider trading for failing to disclose a United States Department of Justice antitrust investigation into the company and for selling stock options before the probe was made public. Regarding compensation, Hemsley's annual salary was reported as $14,518,164 by Business Week. For 2016, his compensation was estimated at $31.3 million. Forbes magazine ranked him 269th in its 2009 Special Report on CEO Compensation. According to bizjournals.com, he was the country's highest-paid CEO in 2010, making $101.96 million. In 2011, Forbes named him the highest-paid CEO following a large gain in the value of his stock ownership. In 2025, following his return as CEO, Hemsley was awarded a compensation package that included $60 million in stock options vesting over three years and a base annual salary of $1 million. Outside his corporate role, Hemsley holds several other positions. He is a trustee of the University of St. Thomas, Minnesota, and of Minnesota Public Radio. He is also a member of the National Executive Board of the Boy Scouts of America, the organization's governing body.

name: Suzanne Scott
education: Graduated from American University in 1988.
careerHistory: 1996: Began at Fox News as a programming assistant. 2002-2005: Associate producer, producer, and senior producer of On the Record with Greta Van Susteren. 2005: Network executive producer. 2007: Vice president of programming. 2009: Senior vice president of programming and development. 2016: Executive vice president of programming. 2018: Named CEO of Fox News and Fox Business Network.
bio:
Suzanne Scott is the Chief Executive Officer of Fox News and Fox Business Network, the second CEO in the network's history and its first female CEO. She was ranked 61st on Forbes's 2021 list of the World's 100 Most Powerful Women. Scott was raised in Parsippany, New Jersey, where her father ran a trucking company from the family home and her mother worked as a real estate agent. She is a 1988 graduate of American University.

Scott began her media career as an executive assistant to Chet Collier at CNBC before moving with him to Fox News at its inception in 1996. She started at Fox News as a programming assistant. Throughout her tenure, she rose through the ranks in numerous programming, production, and creative positions. These roles included executive vice president of programming (2016), senior vice president of programming and development (2009), vice president of programming (2007), and network executive producer (2005). She also served as associate producer, producer, and senior producer for the program 'On the Record with Greta Van Susteren' from 2002 to 2005. Scott was responsible for launching several on-air and digital initiatives, including the 2002 primetime debut of 'On the Record.'

Following the departure of founder and former CEO Roger Ailes in 2016, Scott, along with Jay Wallace and Jack Abernethy, is credited with 'turning Fox News around' after the scandal involving Ailes. During this period, she served as president of programming, overseeing Fox News Channel's opinion shows such as 'Fox & Friends,' 'The Five,' and 'Hannity.'

On May 17, 2018, Scott was named CEO of both Fox News and Fox Business Network. Lachlan Murdoch noted that she had made history as the network's first female CEO. She remained the only woman in charge of a major TV news organization until Rashida Jones was installed as head of MSNBC. Her promotion was not universally praised due to allegations of complicity in several sexual harassment suits within the company; while Scott was not a defendant, she was cited within them and involved in several internal complaints, accusations she denies. In March 2023, The Guardian reported she was furious when a network reporter fact-checked Donald Trump's false claims about the 2020 election, stating it was 'bad for business.'

name: Joseph Kahn
education: Attended New York University's Tisch School of the Arts but dropped out after a year.
careerHistory: Mid-1990s: Began directing music videos for artists like Aaliyah and Ice Cube. 2004: Directed his first feature film, 'Torque'. 2011: Directed the horror comedy film 'Detention'. 2017: Directed the film 'Bodied', which premiered at TIFF. 2024: Premiered his fourth feature film, 'Ick', at TIFF.
bio:
Joseph Kahn (born Ahn Jun-hee on October 12, 1972) is a South Korean-born American director renowned for his work in music videos and film. He was born in Busan, South Korea, and spent part of his childhood there and in Livorno, Italy, before his family moved to Jersey Village, Texas, when he was seven. After graduating from Jersey Village High School in 1990, he briefly attended New York University's Tisch School of the Arts before dropping out and returning to Houston to begin directing hip hop music videos.

Kahn's music video career spans over thirty years, during which he has worked with a wide array of prominent artists including Britney Spears, Taylor Swift, Eminem, Backstreet Boys, Lady Gaga, and Destiny's Child, among others. His early work in the mid-1990s included videos for Aaliyah, Ice Cube, and Snoop Dogg. Kahn achieved significant acclaim in 2003 when he won his first Grammy Award for Eminem's "Without Me" video, which also earned the MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year and Best Direction. He received further recognition with Katy Perry's "Waking Up in Vegas" winning the MVPA 2009 Best Video of the Year. In 2014, he was honored with The Icon Award by the UK Music Video Awards.

A notable collaborator with Taylor Swift, Kahn directed multiple videos from her albums *1989* and *Reputation*, including "Blank Space," "Bad Blood," and "Look What You Made Me Do." For "Bad Blood" featuring Kendrick Lamar, he won the Grammy Award for Best Music Video in 2015. Other career highlights include directing the 2017 American Country Music Awards Video of the Year, "Forever Country," a 2019 video for Ava Max's "Torn," a new video for Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You," and a 2022 video for Chris Brown's "Iffy." His video for Janet Jackson's "Doesn't Really Matter" is noted for its use of Japanese pop culture and was among the most expensive ever made, costing over $2.5 million.

In film, Kahn directed the 2004 action movie *Torque* starring Ice Cube. He later directed the self-financed horror comedy *Detention* (2011), which was picked up for theatrical distribution by Sony. He produced test footage for a *Swamp Thing* film in 2016. His satirical black comedy *Bodied* (2017), produced by Eminem, premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival, winning the People's Choice Award in the Midnight Madness section, and later collected audience awards at AFI Fest and Fantastic Fest. His fourth feature film, *Ick*, premiered at the 2024 Toronto International Film Festival and received a theatrical release in July 2025.

name: Matt Murray
careerHistory: 2012: Began career with guest roles in TV series. 2014-2015: Played recurring role of Officer Duncan Moore in Rookie Blue. 2015: Played Brian in Kevin from Work. 2016: Starred in recurring role of Tony in Eyewitness. 2017: Played a supporting role in 9JKL and was featured in the web series Teenagers. Later played Officer Gene Clemens in In the Dark and appeared in Snowpiercer.
bio:
Matt Murray (born September 18, 1989) is an American actor. He was born in Detroit, Michigan, and is the youngest of eight siblings. After graduating from high school, Murray moved first to Toronto and then to Los Angeles to pursue an acting career.

Murray began his professional acting career in 2012 with guest appearances on television series such as *The Firm* and *Suits*. He gained his first recurring role in 2014, playing Officer Duncan Moore on the police drama series *Rookie Blue*, a role he held through 2015. In 2015, he played the character Brian in the television series *Kevin from Work*.

In 2016, Murray starred in a recurring role as Tony in the USA Network series *Eyewitness*; the series was canceled after one season in March 2017. That same year, he played a supporting role in the CBS sitcom *9JKL*, which was also canceled after one season in May 2018. Also in 2017, Murray was featured prominently in the third season of the web series *Teenagers*. As part of an ensemble cast that included Emmanuel Kabongo, Chloe Rose, and Raymond Ablack, he won the award for Best Ensemble at the 2018 HollyWeb Festival. This ensemble also received a nomination for Best Ensemble at the 9th annual Indie Series Awards.

Further television roles include playing Officer Gene Clemens on the series *In the Dark* and appearing in four episodes of *Snowpiercer*.

name: Emma Tucker
education: Attended the Armand Hammer United World College of the American West (UWC-USA) from 1983 to 1985. Read PPE at University College, Oxford.
careerHistory: 1990: Graduate trainee at the Financial Times. 1994-2000: Foreign correspondent in Brussels for the FT. 2000-2003: Foreign correspondent in Berlin for the FT. Later became editor of Financial Times Weekend. 2007: Joined The Times as associate features editor, later editor of Times2. 2012: Became The Times' editorial director. 2013: Appointed deputy editor of The Times. 2020: Became editor of The Sunday Times. 2023: Appointed editor-in-chief of The Wall Street Journal.
bio:
Emma Jane Tucker (born 24 October 1966) is an English journalist. She is the editor-in-chief of The Wall Street Journal, a position she assumed on 1 February 2023, becoming the first woman to lead the publication in its 133-year history. Prior to this role, she served as the editor of The Sunday Times, the first woman to hold that position since 1901, and was previously a deputy editor of The Times.

Tucker was born in London, England, to Nicholas Tucker and Jacqueline Anthony. She was educated at Wallands School and Priory School in Lewes, East Sussex. At age 16, she won a scholarship to attend the Armand Hammer United World College of the American West in New Mexico, USA, from 1983 to 1985. She later read Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE) at University College, Oxford.

Her journalism career began in 1990 as a graduate trainee at the Financial Times (FT). She initially worked in the House of Commons press gallery and wrote the money markets column, later working in the newspaper's economics room during the ERM crisis. From 1994 to 2000, Tucker was posted to Brussels as a foreign correspondent covering the European Union. She then moved to Berlin in January 2000, serving as a foreign correspondent in Germany for three years. Upon returning, she became the property editor and later moved into features, eventually rising to become the editor of Financial Times Weekend.

Tucker joined The Times in 2007 as associate features editor. A year later, she became editor of Times2, and in 2012, she was appointed The Times's editorial director. In October 2013, she was promoted to deputy editor of The Times. At the end of January 2020, she became editor of The Sunday Times. During her tenure there, the newspaper reported on controversies regarding COVID-19 contracts.

In her personal life, Tucker has three sons. She was previously married and divorced before marrying her second husband, Peter Andreas Howarth, in 2008. She formerly lived in Lewes, East Sussex, and now resides in the Upper West Side neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City.

name: John Micklethwait
education: Educated at Ampleforth College and Magdalen College, Oxford, where he studied history.
careerHistory: Worked for Chase Manhattan Bank for two years (starting date unspecified). Joined The Economist in 1987, later setting up and working from its Los Angeles office (1990-1993). Edited the Business Section for four years, then ran the New York Bureau for two years as U.S. editor. Served as editor-in-chief of The Economist from March/April 2006 to 2015. Appointed editor-in-chief of Bloomberg News in February 2015, a position he holds as of the text.
bio:
Richard John Micklethwait CBE (born 11 August 1962) is an English journalist. He is the editor-in-chief of Bloomberg News, a position he has held since February 2015. Prior to this, he served as the editor-in-chief of The Economist from 2006 to 2015.

Micklethwait was born in London and educated at Ampleforth College, an independent school, and Magdalen College, Oxford, where he studied history. He began his career working for Chase Manhattan Bank for two years before joining The Economist in 1987. His early roles at the publication included setting up an office in Los Angeles, where he worked from 1990 to 1993. He later edited the Business Section for four years and served as U.S. editor, running the New York Bureau for two years before his appointment as editor-in-chief. His journalistic work has covered business and politics from the United States, Latin America, Continental Europe, Southern Africa, and Asia.

Appointed editor-in-chief of The Economist in March 2006, the first issue under his editorship was released on 7 April 2006. In 2010, he was named Editors' Editor by the British Society of Magazine Editors. He has frequently appeared as a commentator on media outlets including CNN, ABC News, BBC, C-SPAN, PBS, and NPR. In 2015, he was appointed as a Trustee of the British Museum. He was also a delegate at the 2010 Bilderberg Conference in Spain.

Micklethwait was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in the 2016 Birthday Honours for services to journalism and economics. In his role at Bloomberg News, he ordered his staff in November 2019 not to investigate their boss, Michael Bloomberg, nor any other Democratic candidates during Bloomberg's presidential campaign. In October 2024, as Bloomberg's top editor, he interviewed President-elect Donald Trump at the Economic Club of Chicago.

In his personal life, Micklethwait married actress Kristin Scott Thomas in September 2024 after a five-year romance.

name: Joe Rogan
education: Attended the University of Massachusetts Boston but dropped out early. Graduated from Newton South High School in 1985.
careerHistory: Began stand-up comedy career in Boston in 1988. Moved to Los Angeles in 1994, signing a deal with Disney and landing a role on the sitcom 'Hardball'. Starred on the NBC sitcom 'NewsRadio' from 1995 to 1999. Started working for the UFC as an interviewer and color commentator in 1997. Hosted the game show 'Fear Factor' from 2001 to 2006. Launched his podcast, The Joe Rogan Experience, in 2009.
bio: Joseph James Rogan Jr., known as Joe Rogan, is an American podcaster, comedian, and UFC color commentator, born on August 11, 1967, in Newark, New Jersey. He is the host of The Joe Rogan Experience, one of the world's most popular podcasts and the most streamed podcast on Spotify since 2020. Rogan began his career in comedy in 1988 in the Boston area. After moving to Los Angeles in 1994, he secured a developmental deal with Disney and landed acting roles, most notably as Joe Garrelli on the NBC sitcom NewsRadio from 1995 to 1999. In 1997, he started working for the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) as an interviewer and later, in 2002, became a color commentator, a role he continues in. From 2001 to 2006, he hosted the game show Fear Factor. Rogan launched his podcast, The Joe Rogan Experience, in 2009. Its success led to an exclusive distribution deal with Spotify in 2020 for $200 million, which he renewed in 2024 for an estimated $250 million, though the podcast is no longer exclusive to the platform. In his early life, Rogan developed an interest in martial arts as a teenager, winning the US Open Championship taekwondo tournament at 19 and working as a taekwondo instructor. He attended the University of Massachusetts Boston but dropped out. Rogan has publicly voiced support for various political and social positions, including same-sex marriage, recreational drug legalization, universal health care, universal basic income, gun rights, and free speech, while opposing cancel culture and military adventurism. He has endorsed political candidates across the spectrum, supporting Ron Paul in 2012, Bernie Sanders in 2020, and Donald Trump in 2024, though he later criticized some of Trump's policies. Rogan has also faced criticism for promoting conspiracy theories, COVID-19 misinformation, and hosting guests accused of spreading misinformation and pseudoscience.

name: Tucker Carlson
careerHistory: Began media career in the 1990s writing for The Weekly Standard and other publications. CNN commentator (2000–2005) and co-host of Crossfire (2001–2005). Hosted Tucker on MSNBC (2005–2008). Became a political analyst for Fox News in 2009, later hosting Tucker Carlson Tonight (2016–2023). Co-founded and served as editor-in-chief of The Daily Caller (2010–2020). After Fox News, launched The Tucker Carlson Show and Tucker on X.
bio: Tucker Swanson McNear Carlson (born May 16, 1969) is an American conservative political commentator, television journalist, columnist, and writer. He began his media career in the 1990s, writing for publications including The Weekly Standard. His television career started at CNN in 2000, where he co-hosted the prime-time debate program Crossfire from 2001 to 2005. After leaving CNN, he hosted the nightly program Tucker on MSNBC from 2005 to 2008. In 2009, he joined Fox News as a political analyst. From 2016 until April 2023, he hosted the nightly political talk show Tucker Carlson Tonight on Fox News. Following the cancellation of that show and the termination of his Fox News contract, he launched his own program, The Tucker Carlson Show, and hosts Tucker on X. In 2010, he co-founded the right-wing news website The Daily Caller, serving as its initial editor-in-chief until leaving in 2020. Carlson is an advocate of former President Donald Trump and has been described as a high-profile proponent of Trumpism and an influential voice in right-wing media. He is known as a critic of immigration and U.S. foreign interventions, having renounced his initial support for the Iraq War. His commentary has been noted for introducing far-right ideas into mainstream discourse and for promoting conspiracy theories on various topics, including demographic replacement, COVID-19, the United States Capitol attack, and Ukrainian bioweapons. Some of his remarks on race, immigration, and women have been described as racist and sexist. He has defended Russian president Vladimir Putin and, in February 2024, became the first Western journalist to interview Putin since the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Carlson was among the Fox News hosts named in the 2021 Dominion Voting Systems defamation lawsuit for broadcasting false statements. He is the author of three books: Politicians, Partisans, and Parasites (2003), Ship of Fools (2018), and The Long Slide (2021).

name: Lex Fridman
education: Obtained B.S. and M.S. degrees in computer science from Drexel University in 2010, and a Ph.D. in electrical and computer engineering from Drexel University in 2014.
careerHistory: 2014: Spent six months at Google working on AI for identity authentication. 2015: Moved to MIT's AgeLab as a research scientist, working on driver behavior. 2019: Transitioned to an unpaid role in MIT's Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics. 2018-present: Host of the Lex Fridman Podcast. 2022-present: Research scientist at the MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS).
bio:
Lex Fridman, born Alexei Fridman on August 15, 1983, is an American computer scientist, research scientist, and podcast host. He was born in Chkalovsk, Tajik Soviet Socialist Republic, and grew up in Moscow before his family moved to the Chicago area when he was about 11. Fridman is Jewish. He earned B.S. and M.S. degrees in computer science from Drexel University in 2010 and a Ph.D. in electrical and computer engineering from the same institution in 2014. His doctoral dissertation focused on learning identity from behavioral biometrics for active authentication.

Fridman's career is primarily associated with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). After a six-month stint at Google in 2014, he joined MIT's AgeLab as a research scientist in 2015, working on understanding driver behavior through psychology and big-data analytics. There, he led a team developing learning algorithms for semi-autonomous vehicles in collaboration with Toyota. In 2019, he published a non-peer-reviewed study on Tesla's Autopilot system, which concluded drivers remained focused. This study drew criticism from AI experts for its methodology and small sample size but gained prominence after praise from Elon Musk. Following this, Fridman transitioned to an unpaid role in MIT's Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics. As of 2022, he has been a research scientist at the MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS) and also conducts research for the Center for Complex Engineering Systems, a collaboration between MIT and King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology. As of February 2024, he lives in Texas and remains employed at MIT.

Fridman is best known as the host of the Lex Fridman Podcast, which he began in 2018 under the name The Artificial Intelligence Podcast, renaming it in 2020. The podcast interviews notable figures from science, technology, sports, arts, and politics, and by 2024 had attracted 3.6 million subscribers. His interview style has received mixed reception. Some colleagues, like Nobel laureate Frank Wilczek, have praised him as an effective science communicator. Critics, however, note he often does not challenge false claims made by guests, maintains personal friendships with some interviewees like Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner, and has been described as a 'softball interviewer' for tech elites. Observers have also commented that his posture of neutrality and empathetic interviewing approach can fail to adequately challenge misinformation, despite featuring guests from across the political spectrum.

name: Kevin Roberts
education: Earned a bachelor's degree in history magna cum laude from the University of Louisiana at Lafayette in 1996, a Master of Arts in history from Virginia Tech in 1999, and a Ph.D. in American history from University of Texas at Austin in 2003.
careerHistory: Assistant professor of history at New Mexico State University (2003-2005). President of Wyoming Catholic College (2013-2016). Executive Vice President and later CEO of the Texas Public Policy Foundation (from 2016). President of the Heritage Foundation and its lobbying arm, Heritage Action (from December 2021).
bio:
Kevin David Roberts (born June 24, 1974) is an American political strategist and former historian. He is the president of the Heritage Foundation, a conservative political think tank, and its lobbying arm, Heritage Action, serving both organizations in a joint role. He was appointed to this position in October 2021. Prior to this, Roberts was the CEO of the Texas Public Policy Foundation and served as the president of Wyoming Catholic College from 2013 to 2016.

Roberts holds a Ph.D. in American history from the University of Texas at Austin (2003), a Master of Arts in history from Virginia Tech (1999), and a bachelor's degree in history from the University of Louisiana at Lafayette (1996). He worked as an assistant professor of history at New Mexico State University from 2003 to 2005. In 2006, he founded John Paul the Great Academy, a private Catholic K-12 school in Lafayette, Louisiana.

Soon after Roberts joined the Heritage Foundation in December 2021, the organization established Project 2025, a comprehensive plan to overhaul the federal government under a new Republican administration. Roberts has been frequently described as the "mastermind" or "architect" of this controversial initiative. He has stated that Heritage's role is "institutionalizing Trumpism" and ensuring a faster start for a future conservative administration. Roberts has made statements questioning the legitimacy of the 2020 presidential election and, in a July 2024 interview, spoke of being "in the process of the second American Revolution."

In 2024, Roberts wrote a book titled "Dawn's Early Light: Taking Back Washington to Save America," with a foreword by Vice President JD Vance. The book's release was postponed until after the November 2024 election. In July 2024, he was appointed by Oklahoma State Superintendent Ryan Walters to a committee tasked with revising K-12 social studies standards. Roberts's career and public statements are centrally defined by his leadership of the Heritage Foundation and his prominent role in advancing the policy agenda of Project 2025.

name: Robert Doar
education: Graduated from Princeton University with an A.B. in history in 1983.
careerHistory: After graduating in 1983, he worked at the New York City Office of Business Development, then became deputy to the editor-in-chief of The Washington Monthly. He later served as editor of the Harlem Valley Times and as assistant vice president of the First National Bank of Hudson Valley. In May 1995, he became Deputy Commissioner of the NY State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance's Division of Child Support Enforcement, and was appointed Commissioner of that office in 2003. In January 2007, he was appointed commissioner of the New York City Human Resources Administration. He is now the president of the American Enterprise Institute.
bio:
Robert Larkin Doar is an American businessman, writer, and former public administrator. He currently serves as the president of the American Enterprise Institute (AEI), a public policy think tank. His research at AEI focuses on federal and state antipoverty policies and safety net programs.

Doar was born in Washington, D.C., the son of former Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights John Doar. He attended St. Ann's School, Phillips Academy, and Princeton University, graduating in 1983 with an A.B. in history. His early career included work at the New York City Office of Business Development, a role as deputy to the editor-in-chief of The Washington Monthly, and positions as editor of the Harlem Valley Times and assistant vice president of the First National Bank of Hudson Valley.

His career in public administration began in May 1995 when he became the Deputy Commissioner of the New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance's Division of Child Support Enforcement. In 2003, Governor George Pataki appointed him as Commissioner of the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance. He is also a member of the board of directors of the research organization Child Trends.

Before joining the American Enterprise Institute, Doar was appointed by Mayor Michael Bloomberg on January 8, 2007, to serve as commissioner of the New York City Human Resources Administration. In this role, he oversaw the city's welfare and public assistance programs.

At AEI, Doar has been involved in significant policy work. He served as co-chair of the bipartisan National Commission on Hunger and was a lead member of the AEI-Brookings Institution working group on poverty and opportunity. This group published the report "Opportunity, Responsibility, and Security: A Consensus Plan for Reducing Poverty and Restoring the American Dream." He is the editor of "A Safety Net That Works: Improving Federal Programs for Low-Income Americans," an AEI publication featuring expert discussions on federal assistance programs and reform proposals. In 2018, he helped convene a bipartisan working group with Brookings and Opportunity America that published the report "Work, Skills, Community: Restoring Opportunity for the Working Class."

Doar has testified before the United States Congress and has written for publications including The Wall Street Journal, USA Today, The Hill, and National Review.

name: Doug Hamlin
currentRole: 执行副总裁兼首席执行官
education: Undergraduate at the University of Michigan.
careerHistory: Served in the United States Marine Corps for six years. Worked for Petersen Publishing Company for 14 years, serving as vice president and group publisher for Motor Trend and publisher of Guns & Ammo from 1991 to 1995. Founded autoMedia Solutions in the 1990s. Joined the NRA as executive director of publications in 2014. Appointed CEO and Executive Vice President of the NRA in May 2024.
bio:
Douglas (Doug) Hamlin is an American publisher and businessman who has served as the chief executive officer (CEO) and executive vice president (EVP) of the National Rifle Association (NRA) since May 2024. He was raised in Michigan. Prior to his career in publishing, Hamlin served for six years in the United States Marine Corps as an infantry weapons officer and recruiter. He then worked for the Petersen Publishing Company for 14 years, where he was vice president and group publisher for Motor Trend and publisher of Guns & Ammo from 1991 to 1995. In the 1990s, he founded autoMedia Solutions, an automotive news company.

Hamlin joined the NRA in 2014, serving as executive director of NRA Publications. The organization credited him with saving approximately $30 million by increasing production efficiency and moving the production of America's First Freedom in-house. In 2021, then-CEO Wayne LaPierre named Hamlin as a potential successor. Following LaPierre's resignation amid corruption allegations, the NRA board of directors elected Hamlin as CEO and EVP in May 2024, a move marketed as a reformist choice against LaPierre loyalists. Upon his election, Hamlin stated his focus was on protecting Second Amendment rights and executing the NRA's programs. He subsequently appointed Randy Kozuch as executive director of the NRA Institute for Legislative Action and Joseph P. De Bergalis Jr. as executive director of NRA general operations. As CEO, Hamlin vowed to rebuild the organization, aiming to regain lost members, grow training programs, and support women and minority gun owners. He set a membership goal of 10 million. After his selection, he reportedly fought with NRA president Bob Barr, a LaPierre loyalist.

Hamlin's appointment was accompanied by the resurfacing of a 1979 animal cruelty incident from his time as an undergraduate and chapter president of the Alpha Delta Phi fraternity at the University of Michigan. In December 1979, Hamlin and four other fraternity members were implicated in the death of the fraternity cat. A judge later held Hamlin responsible for not using his authority as president to prevent the killing. The five were charged with misdemeanor animal cruelty, pleaded no contest in March 1980, were fined, given deferred sentences, and sentenced to 200 hours of animal-related community service. Their records were later expunged. Following the report's resurgence, anonymous NRA employees sent a letter to the board asking for Hamlin's suspension. In response to the incident, Hamlin stated he did not condone the actions, took responsibility as chapter president, and highlighted his subsequent life of service, business, and charity work. An earlier 2018 lawsuit between New York state and the NRA also included allegations from whistleblowers that Hamlin had received around $25,000 in inappropriate reimbursements for living expenses from LaPierre.

name: Clint Pressley
education: Graduated from Wofford College with a Bachelor of Arts and later received a Master of Divinity from New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary, having first attended Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary.
careerHistory: Pastored two churches in Mississippi (dates unspecified). Returned to Hickory Grove Baptist Church in 1999 as senior associate pastor of preaching. Served as senior pastor of Dauphin Way Baptist Church in Mobile, Alabama from 2004. Returned to Hickory Grove Baptist Church as co-pastor in 2010 and became senior pastor in 2011. Served as first vice president of the Southern Baptist Convention from 2014 to 2015. Served on the board of trustees of the Southern Baptist Theological Seminary since 2015, including as chairman from 2020 to 2022. Elected President of the Southern Baptist Convention in June 2024 and reelected in June 2025.
bio:
Clint Pressley (born February 26, 1969) is an American evangelical pastor who has served as the president of the Southern Baptist Convention since his election in June 2024. He was reelected to a second one-year term in June 2025. Pressley has also been the senior pastor of Hickory Grove Baptist Church in Charlotte, North Carolina, since 2011.

Born in Charlotte, North Carolina, Pressley attended a Presbyterian Church (USA) congregation with his parents in his youth and later attended Hickory Grove Baptist Church as a teenager. He earned a Bachelor of Arts degree from Wofford College and a Master of Divinity from New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary, having first attended Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary.

Pressley began his pastoral career leading two churches in Mississippi. He returned to Hickory Grove Baptist Church in 1999, serving as senior associate pastor of preaching. In 2004, he became senior pastor of Dauphin Way Baptist Church in Mobile, Alabama. He returned to Hickory Grove Baptist Church in 2010 as co-pastor and was installed as its senior pastor in 2011.

Within the Southern Baptist Convention, Pressley served as first vice president from 2014 to 2015. He has been a member of the board of trustees of the Southern Baptist Theological Seminary since 2015, chairing the board from 2020 to 2022. His election as President of the Southern Baptist Convention occurred at the denomination's annual meeting in Indianapolis, Indiana, in June 2024.

Pressley is married to Connie LaBelle Smith Pressley. The couple has two adopted sons, one of whom died in 2023 at the age of 24.

name: Cecilia Rouse
education: Bachelor of Arts in economics from Harvard University in 1986 and PhD in economics from Harvard University in 1992.
careerHistory: Joined the faculty at Princeton University in 1992. Served in the National Economic Council under President Bill Clinton from 1998 to 1999. Served on President Barack Obama's Council of Economic Advisers from 2009 to 2011. Served as dean of the Princeton School of Public and International Affairs. Served as the 30th Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers from 2021 to 2023. Became the 9th President of the Brookings Institution in January 2024.
bio:
Cecilia Elena Rouse (born December 18, 1963) is an American economist who currently serves as the President of the Brookings Institution, a position she assumed in January 2024. She previously served as the 30th Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA) from 2021 to 2023, becoming the first Black American to hold this position. President Joe Biden nominated her for the CEA role in November 2020, and she was confirmed by the U.S. Senate by a vote of 95–4 on March 2, 2021. She resigned from the CEA on March 31, 2023, to return to teaching.

Rouse's career in public service spans multiple administrations. She served on President Barack Obama's Council of Economic Advisers from 2009 to 2011 and worked in the National Economic Council under President Bill Clinton from 1998 to 1999. Her academic career is centered at Princeton University, where she joined the faculty in 1992 after earning her doctorate. She served as the dean of the Princeton School of Public and International Affairs and holds the title of Lawrence and Shirley Katzman and Lewis and Anna Ernst Professor in the Economics of Education. She is also the founding director of the Princeton University Education Research Section.

Her primary research expertise lies in labor economics, with a specific focus on the economics of education. She is a member of the National Academy of Education and a research associate of the National Bureau of Economic Research. Rouse has held editorial roles at the Journal of Labor Economics and The Future of Children and has served on the board of directors for MDRC and the T. Rowe Price Equity Mutual Funds.

Rouse graduated from Harvard University with a Bachelor of Arts in economics in 1986 and a PhD in economics in 1992. She grew up in Del Mar, California, and is the sibling of physicist Forest Rouse and anthropologist Carolyn Rouse. Her father, Carl A. Rouse, was a research physicist, and her mother, Lorraine, worked as a school psychologist.

name: Neera Tanden
education: Graduated from Bedford High School in 1988. Received a Bachelor of Arts from the University of California, Los Angeles in 1992 and a Juris Doctor from Yale Law School in 1996.
careerHistory: 1988: Worked on Michael Dukakis's presidential campaign. 1992: Worked on Bill Clinton's presidential campaign. 1996-2000: Held various domestic policy roles in the Clinton White House and First Lady's Office. 1999-2000: Deputy campaign manager and policy director for Hillary Clinton's Senate campaign. 2003-2005: Legislative director for Senator Hillary Clinton. 2003-2021 & 2025-present: Various roles, including President and CEO, at the Center for American Progress. 2008: Domestic policy director for Barack Obama's general election campaign. Served as senior adviser at HHS in the Obama administration, helping draft the Affordable Care Act. 2021-2023: Senior advisor and later White House Staff Secretary to President Joe Biden. 2023-2025: Director of the United States Domestic Policy Council.
bio:
Neera Tanden (born September 10, 1970) is an American political consultant and former government official. She is the president and CEO of the Center for American Progress (CAP), a Democratic think tank, a role she has held in two separate tenures. Tanden's career has been significantly defined by her work on domestic policy, in think tanks, and for various Democratic campaigns and administrations. She played a central role in the founding of CAP in 2003 and first served as its president and CEO from 2011 to 2021, succeeding John Podesta. She returned to this leadership position in February 2025.

Tanden has a long history of involvement in Democratic presidential campaigns, beginning with volunteering for Michael Dukakis in 1988. She worked on Bill Clinton's 1992 campaign and served in his administration as associate director for domestic policy and as a domestic policy advisor in the First Lady's Office. She is regarded as a loyalist and personal friend of Hillary Clinton, having served as deputy campaign manager and policy director for Clinton's successful 2000 Senate campaign in New York, and later as her legislative director from 2003 to 2005. Tanden was Hillary Clinton's policy director during her 2008 Democratic primary bid and was an unpaid adviser during her 2016 presidential campaign.

After Barack Obama secured the 2008 Democratic nomination, Tanden joined his team as domestic policy director for the general election. In the Obama administration, she served as a senior adviser to the Secretary of Health and Human Services, helping to draft the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and negotiate its provisions, earning a description as one of its "key architects."

In the Biden administration, Tanden served as a senior advisor and staff secretary to President Joe Biden from 2021 to 2023. She was then appointed Director of the United States Domestic Policy Council, serving from 2023 to 2025, where she succeeded Susan Rice.

Tanden's nomination by President-elect Biden to be Director of the Office of Management and Budget in 2020 was withdrawn following opposition in the Senate. She holds a Bachelor of Arts from the University of California, Los Angeles (1992) and a Juris Doctor from Yale Law School (1996).

name: Michael Froman
education: Received a B.A. from Princeton University in 1985, a D.Phil. from St Antony's College, Oxford in 1988, and a J.D. from Harvard Law School.
careerHistory: 1992-1993: White House Fellow. 1993-1995: Deputy National Security Advisor for International Economic Affairs. 1997-1999: Chief of Staff at the U.S. Department of the Treasury. 2001-2009: Held executive roles at Citigroup, including President and CEO of CitiInsurance. 2009-2013: Deputy Assistant to the President and Deputy National Security Advisor for International Economic Affairs. 2013-2017: U.S. Trade Representative. 2017: Distinguished Fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations. 2018: Vice Chairman and President for Strategic Growth at Mastercard Inc and Director at The Walt Disney Company. 2023-present: President of the Council on Foreign Relations.
bio:
Michael Braverman Goodman Froman (born August 20, 1962) is an American lawyer and the current president of the Council on Foreign Relations. He served as the United States Trade Representative from 2013 to 2017. His career in government spans several high-level economic policy roles. During the Clinton administration, he served as Deputy Assistant Secretary for Eurasia and the Middle East, focusing on economic policy towards the former Soviet Union and Central and Eastern Europe, and worked on the economic components of the Dayton Accords. He later became Chief of Staff to Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin from 1997 to 1999.

Froman rejoined government service in 2009 under President Barack Obama, a former Harvard Law School classmate with whom he served on the Harvard Law Review. He was appointed Assistant to the President and Deputy National Security Advisor for International Economic Affairs, a position held jointly at the National Security Council and the National Economic Council. In this capacity, he acted as the U.S. sherpa to the G7, G8, and G20 summits.

Nominated by President Obama in May 2013, Froman was confirmed as U.S. Trade Representative by the Senate in June 2013. During his tenure, he was the lead U.S. negotiator for a bilateral investment treaty with China and served as the chief negotiator for the Trans-Pacific Partnership trade agreement. His role in classified trade negotiations drew scrutiny from some politicians and lawyers. Following his government service, he joined the Council on Foreign Relations as a distinguished fellow in 2017. He later served as Vice Chairman and President for Strategic Growth at Mastercard Inc (2018) and became a director of The Walt Disney Company (2018). In March 2023, he was chosen as president of the Council on Foreign Relations.

Froman's education includes a B.A. in Public and International Affairs from Princeton University (1985), a D.Phil. in International Relations from St Antony's College, Oxford (1988), and a J.D. from Harvard Law School. Early in his career, he worked for the American Bar Association's legal assistance program in Albania and for the European Commission's Forward Studies Unit in Brussels. He was also a White House Fellow (1992-93) and, between government posts, held executive positions at Citigroup, including President and CEO of CitiInsurance.

name: Anthony D. Romero
education: Received his B.A. from Princeton University's Woodrow Wilson School of Public and International Affairs in 1987 and a J.D. from Stanford Law School in 1990.
careerHistory: Started career at the Rockefeller Foundation. In 1992, began working for the Ford Foundation as a program officer in the Civil Rights and Social Justice Program. After less than four years, was promoted to director, later serving as director of Human Rights and International Cooperation. Became executive director of the American Civil Liberties Union in September 2001.
bio:
Anthony D. Romero (born July 9, 1965) is an American lawyer and activist serving as the executive director of the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), a position he assumed in September 2001. He is the first Latino and openly gay man to hold this role. Born in the Bronx, New York to Puerto Rican parents, Romero was the first in his family to graduate high school. He earned a B.A. from Princeton University's Woodrow Wilson School of Public and International Affairs in 1987 and a J.D. from Stanford Law School in 1990.

Romero began his career at the Rockefeller Foundation before joining the Ford Foundation in 1992. There, he served as a program officer and later became a director, managing approximately $90 million in grants for civil rights, human rights, and peace projects. He launched initiatives in areas including affirmative action, voting rights, immigrants' rights, women's rights, reproductive freedom, and LGBT rights.

His tenure at the ACLU began just before the September 11, 2001 attacks. In response, he launched the "Keep America Safe and Free" campaign, which targeted the Patriot Act, uncovered documents on detainee abuse, and successfully challenged the Bush administration's NSA spying program in court. Under his leadership, ACLU membership and donations increased significantly, staff numbers grew, and the organization expanded its work on racial justice, religious freedom, privacy rights, reproductive freedom, and LGBT rights. It also established new programs focused on human rights and surveillance technology privacy issues.

Romero has been a vocal advocate on various issues, denouncing Pentagon surveillance of antiwar protests, speaking at the 2008 March for Women's Lives, praising whistleblower Edward Snowden in 2013, and co-signing a 2016 letter to the UN advocating for more humane drug policies. His time at the ACLU has also included criticisms from within the organization regarding management decisions and a 2011 DWI charge.

He is the author of "In Defense of Our America: The Fight for Civil Liberties in the Age of Terror" (2007). His recognitions include being named one of Time magazine's 25 Most Influential Hispanics in 2005, receiving the Golden Plate Award from the American Academy of Achievement in 2009, the "Maggie" Award from Planned Parenthood in 2011, and the Woodrow Wilson Award from Princeton University in 2020.

name: Alexis McGill Johnson
ChineseName: 亚历克西斯·麦吉尔·约翰逊
education: Graduated from Princeton University with a bachelor's degree in political science in 1993. Received a Master of Arts in political science from Yale University in 1995.
careerHistory: Taught political science and African-American studies at Yale and Wesleyan University. Served as political director for the Hip-Hop Summit Action Network and executive director of Citizen Change (2004). Co-founded and was executive director of the Perception Institute (2009). Served as board chair of Planned Parenthood (2013-2015). Appointed acting president of Planned Parenthood (July 2019), then permanent president and CEO (June 2020).
bio:
Lori Alexis McGill Johnson (born August 5, 1972) is an American businesswoman and abortion rights advocate who serves as the president and CEO of Planned Parenthood. She was born and raised in New York City. Her childhood was strongly influenced by her parents' Black Nationalism and pride in Black culture. Her mother rose from a secretary to an executive-level position at AT&T. McGill Johnson graduated from Princeton University in 1993 with a bachelor's degree in political science, focusing on Latin-American social movements. She earned a Master of Arts in political science from Yale University in 1995.

Her early career was in academia, teaching political science and African-American studies at Yale and Wesleyan University. She transitioned to political advocacy, serving as political director for Russell Simmons's "Hip-Hop Summit Action Network" and as executive director of Citizen Change during the 2004 election season, where she helped launch the "Vote or Die!" campaign. In 2009, she co-founded the Perception Institute, a research group studying bias reduction and discrimination, and served as its executive director. In this role, she co-created the curriculum for Starbucks' racial bias training in May 2018.

McGill Johnson has a long association with Planned Parenthood, having served on its board and as board chair from 2013 to 2015. On July 16, 2019, she was announced as the organization's acting president following the termination of Leana Wen. She was elevated to permanent president and CEO on June 26, 2020. In this role, she has been a prominent public advocate, speaking at rallies such as one against abortion restrictions in North Carolina in 2023.

Her board service extends to other organizations, including the New York Civil Liberties Union, the Center for Social Inclusion, and Citizen Engagement Lab. Her work has been recognized with several honors. In 2023, she appeared in Politico's Playbook Power List for her work following the repeal of Roe v. Wade and was selected for STAT's Status List for helping patients. In 2024, CNN As Equals recognized her as a social justice leader.

She is married to Robert Johnson, president of the Institute for New Economic Thinking, and they have two daughters. The family lives in New York City.

name: Loren Blackford
bio: Loren Blackford is the executive director of the Sierra Club, a prominent American environmental organization. The Sierra Club, founded in 1892 in San Francisco by preservationist John Muir, is one of the first large-scale environmental preservation organizations in the world. It is a nonprofit membership association with chapters in all 50 U.S. states, Washington D.C., and Puerto Rico, and is headquartered in Oakland, California. The organization's mission is to explore, enjoy, and protect the wild places of the earth, practice and promote responsible resource use, and educate humanity to protect the environment. It engages in political advocacy for sustainable energy and against coal, hydropower, and nuclear power, and organizes outdoor recreation activities, historically playing a notable role in U.S. mountaineering and rock climbing. The Sierra Club is governed by a 15-member board of directors, and the executive director runs its day-to-day operations. Blackford's appointment came in September 2025, following a period of significant internal strife under the previous executive director, Ben Jealous. Jealous's tenure, which began in January 2023, was marked by repeated restructures, layoffs, allegations of unfair labor practices, and multiple votes of no confidence from staff and chapters. The organization's turmoil was further highlighted in April 2025 when environmental justice pioneer Robert D. Bullard publicly requested the removal of his name from a Sierra Club award, citing unmet promises. After Jealous took a leave of absence in July 2025, the Sierra Club board unanimously voted to terminate his employment for cause in August 2025. Loren Blackford was subsequently named to the executive director role the following month, tasked with leading the organization's ongoing advocacy and operational activities.

name: Derrick Johnson
education: Enrolled in The University of Texas at Austin and played college football for the Texas Longhorns from 2001 to 2004.
careerHistory: 2005-2017: Linebacker for the Kansas City Chiefs (selected 15th overall in the 2005 NFL Draft). 2018: Played six games for the Oakland Raiders. Retired in 2019 after signing a ceremonial contract with the Chiefs.
bio:
Derrick O'Hara Johnson (born November 22, 1982) is an American former professional football player who was a linebacker in the National Football League (NFL). He was born in Waco, Texas, and attended Waco High School, where he was a three-sport star in football, track, and basketball. In football, he played as a linebacker, earning Parade magazine high school All-America and first-team All-Texas Class 5A honors following both his junior and senior seasons. He also played in the first-ever U.S. Army All-American Bowl in 2000. As a track and field athlete, Johnson was a state-qualifier in the 100-meters and the triple jump.

Johnson played college football for the Texas Longhorns at the University of Texas at Austin from 2001 to 2004. He became one of the most dominant linebackers in Longhorns history, earning first-team All-Big 12 selection in 2002, 2003, and 2004. He was a consensus first-team All-American in 2003 and a unanimous first-team All-American in 2004. Following his senior season, Johnson was recognized as the Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year and received the Dick Butkus Award and the Bronko Nagurski Trophy.

Johnson was selected by the Kansas City Chiefs in the first round of the 2005 NFL draft with the 15th overall pick. He played 13 seasons with the Chiefs, during which he made four Pro Bowl selections (2011–2013, 2015). He was also a First-team All-Pro selection in 2011 and a Second-team All-Pro selection in 2015, and he won the Pro Bowl Defensive MVP award in 2013. Johnson is the Kansas City Chiefs' all-time leading tackler with 1,151 tackles. He finished his career by playing six games for the Oakland Raiders in 2018 before retiring on May 8, 2019, after signing a one-day ceremonial contract with the Chiefs.

His career awards and honors in the NFL include four Pro Bowl selections, First-team All-Pro, Second-team All-Pro, Pro Bowl Defensive MVP, and PFWA All-AFC selection. His college honors include the Dick Butkus Award, Bronko Nagurski Trophy, Jack Lambert Trophy, Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year, two-time Consensus All-American, three-time First-team All-Big 12, and Big 12 Co-Defensive Freshman of the Year. His older brother, Dwight Johnson, and his cousins, Bert Emanuel and Ben Emanuel, also played in the NFL.

name: Liz Shuler
education: Bachelor of Arts degree in journalism from the University of Oregon in 1992.
careerHistory: After college, she became a union organizer for IBEW Local 125 (1990s). In 1997, she became a lobbyist for the IBEW. In June 2004, she was appointed executive assistant to IBEW President Edwin Hill. On September 16, 2009, she was elected AFL–CIO Secretary-Treasurer. On August 20, 2021, she was elected AFL–CIO President to fill the remainder of Richard Trumka's term, and on June 12, 2022, she was elected to a full term as AFL–CIO President.
bio:
Elizabeth "Liz" H. Shuler (born 1970) is an American labor activist and the president of the AFL–CIO, the first woman to be elected president of the federation. She is the highest-ranking woman in the labor federation's history. Shuler previously served as the federation's secretary-treasurer, a role where she was also the first woman and, as of 2009, the youngest person to hold that position. The period from her election until 2013 marked the first time women held two of the three officer positions in the AFL–CIO.

Shuler was born in 1970 to Lance and Joyce Shuler. Her father was a union electrical lineman for Portland General Electric (PGE), while her mother worked there as a non-union secretary. Raised in Gladstone, Oregon, Shuler attended public schools and earned a Bachelor of Arts in journalism from the University of Oregon in 1992. While in college, she worked summers at PGE and was active in the state Democratic Party.

Her union career began after college as an organizer for the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (IBEW) Local 125, focusing on a campaign to organize clerical workers at PGE. In 1997, she became a lobbyist for the IBEW before the Oregon Legislature, successfully working to defeat a bill to deregulate Oregon's electricity market. She also taught in the union's COMET and MEMO organizing programs and served on state labor committees. In 1998, she led the AFL–CIO's successful effort to defeat California Proposition 226.

After the California campaign, Shuler was appointed an IBEW international representative, moving to Washington, D.C., to work in the IBEW's Political and Legislative Affairs Department. In June 2004, she was appointed executive assistant to IBEW President Edwin Hill, becoming the highest-ranking woman in the union's history at that time. In this role, she supervised and coordinated 11 of the IBEW's departments.

On July 7, 2009, AFL–CIO Secretary-Treasurer Richard Trumka chose Shuler as his running mate for secretary-treasurer. She was elected on September 16, 2009. In her term, she stated intentions to reach out to workers under 35, use new media for outreach, and work to balance the federation's budget. Trumka also appointed her to head the AFL–CIO's youth outreach efforts.

Upon Trumka's death on August 5, 2021, Shuler became acting AFL–CIO president. She was elected to fill the remainder of his term on August 20, 2021. On June 12, 2022, she was unanimously elected to a full four-year term as president, solidifying her place as the first woman elected to lead the AFL–CIO. Shuler spoke at the 2024 Democratic National Convention.

Outside her AFL–CIO roles, Shuler is active in the Women's Campaign Fund and is a supporter of the International Women's Democracy Center. She has also been active in Oregon and Washington chapters of Women in the Trades, organizations that promote opportunities for women in the skilled trades.

name: Ronald Hicks
currentRole: 纽约总主教 (Archbishop of New York)
education: Earned a Bachelor of Arts in philosophy from Loyola University Chicago in 1989 and a Master of Divinity from the University of Saint Mary of the Lake/Mundelein Seminary in 1994. Also received a Doctor of Ministry degree from the University of St. Mary of the Lake in 2003.
careerHistory: Associate Pastor at Our Lady of Mercy Parish (1994-1996). Associate Pastor at St. Elizabeth Seton Parish (1996-1999). Dean of Formation at St. Joseph College Seminary (1999-2005). Director for Nuestros Pequeños Hermanos in El Salvador (2005-2010). Dean of Formation at Mundelein Seminary (2010-2015). Vicar General of the Archdiocese of Chicago (2015-2018). Auxiliary Bishop of Chicago (2018-2020). Bishop of Joliet (2020-2026). Archbishop-designate of New York (appointed December 18, 2025).
bio:
Ronald Aldon Hicks (born August 4, 1967) is an American Catholic prelate who has been the archbishop-designate of New York since December 18, 2025. Born in Harvey, Illinois, and raised in South Holland, Illinois, Hicks is of Irish, German, and Polish descent. His early consideration of the priesthood led him to attend Quigley Preparatory Seminary South, graduating in 1985. Before entering university, he spent a year volunteering at an orphanage in Mexico run by Nuestros Pequeños Hermanos. Hicks earned a Bachelor of Arts in philosophy from Loyola University Chicago in 1989 and a Master of Divinity from the University of Saint Mary of the Lake/Mundelein Seminary in 1994.

Hicks was ordained a priest for the Archdiocese of Chicago by Cardinal Joseph Bernardin on May 21, 1994. His early pastoral assignments included serving as an associate pastor at Our Lady of Mercy Parish in Chicago and at St. Elizabeth Seton Parish in Orland Hills, Illinois. In 1999, he was appointed dean of formation at St. Joseph College Seminary in Chicago. He later earned a Doctor of Ministry degree in 2003 from the University of St. Mary of the Lake. From 2005 to 2010, Hicks lived in El Salvador, serving as a director for Nuestros Pequeños Hermanos. Upon returning to Illinois, Cardinal Francis George appointed him dean of formation at Mundelein Seminary in 2010. On January 1, 2015, Archbishop Blase J. Cupich selected him as vicar general for the Archdiocese of Chicago.

Pope Francis appointed Hicks titular bishop of Munatiana and auxiliary bishop of Chicago on July 3, 2018. He was consecrated on September 17, 2018. On July 17, 2020, Francis named him bishop of Joliet. He was installed at the Cathedral of St. Raymond Nonnatus on September 29, 2020. Pope Leo XIV named Hicks metropolitan archbishop of New York on December 18, 2025, with his installation scheduled for February 6, 2026.

Within the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops, Hicks serves as chairman of the Committee on Clergy, Consecrated Life and Vocations. He is also a board member of the Catholic Extension Society and the Mundelein Seminary Advisory Board. A noted fan of the Chicago Cubs, Hicks has described personal similarities with Pope Leo XIV, having grown up in the same neighborhood and frequented the same local establishments.

name: Gavin Newsom
education: Graduated from Santa Clara University in 1989 with a Bachelor of Science in political science. Also attended École Notre Dame des Victoires and Redwood High School, graduating in 1985.
careerHistory: Appointed to San Francisco's Parking and Traffic Commission in 1996. Appointed to the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in 1997 and first elected to the board in 1998. Served as Mayor of San Francisco from 2004 to 2011 (elected 2003, reelected 2007). Served as Lieutenant Governor of California from 2011 to 2019 (elected 2010, reelected 2014). Has served as Governor of California since 2019 (elected 2018, reelected 2022).
bio: Gavin Christopher Newsom (born October 10, 1967) is an American politician and businessman serving as the 40th governor of California since 2019. A member of the Democratic Party, he previously served as the 49th lieutenant governor of California from 2011 to 2019 and as the 42nd mayor of San Francisco from 2004 to 2011. Born in San Francisco, Newsom graduated from Santa Clara University in 1989 with a Bachelor of Science in political science. Before entering politics, he founded the PlumpJack Group, a boutique winery and hospitality business, with investor Gordon Getty. The company grew to manage 23 businesses, including wineries, restaurants, and hotels. Newsom began his political career in 1996 when San Francisco mayor Willie Brown appointed him to the city's Parking and Traffic Commission. Brown appointed him to the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in 1997 to fill a vacancy, and Newsom was first elected to the board in 1998. He was elected mayor of San Francisco in 2003 and reelected in 2007. During his tenure as mayor, he oversaw the 2004 same-sex weddings in San Francisco and dealt with the aftermath of California Proposition 8 in 2008. Newsom was elected lieutenant governor in 2010 and reelected in 2014. In that role, he hosted The Gavin Newsom Show from 2012 to 2013 and wrote the book Citizenville in 2013, focusing on using digital tools for democratic change. He was elected governor of California in 2018 and reelected in 2022. His tenure as governor has included navigating the COVID-19 pandemic, which contributed to an unsuccessful recall effort in 2021. In 2025, he began hosting a podcast, This Is Gavin Newsom, and oversaw the passage of California Proposition 50, the Election Rigging Response Act, a referendum to amend the State Constitution. His political career has also been marked by events such as the 2025 Los Angeles protests and the Newsom v. Trump legal case.

name: Kathy Hochul
education: Graduated from Syracuse University in 1980 with a Bachelor of Arts in political science. Received a Juris Doctor from the Catholic University of America Columbus School of Law in 1984.
careerHistory: Appointed to Hamburg Town Board (1994), later elected and served until 2007. Appointed Deputy Erie County Clerk (2003), then appointed Erie County Clerk (2007), elected to full term (2007) and reelected (2010). U.S. Representative for New York's 26th congressional district (2011-2013). Lieutenant Governor of New York (2015-2021). Governor of New York (2021-present).
bio: Kathleen Courtney Hochul (born August 27, 1958) is an American politician and lawyer who has served as the 57th governor of New York since 2021. A member of the Democratic Party, she is New York's first female governor.
