Born in Buffalo, New York, Hochul graduated from Syracuse University in 1980 and received a Juris Doctor from the Catholic University of America Columbus School of Law in 1984. Her early career included work as legal counsel and legislative assistant to U.S. Representative John LaFalce and U.S. Senator Daniel Moynihan, and for the New York State Assembly. She entered local elected office in 1994 when she was appointed to the Hamburg Town Board, where she served until 2007. In 2003, she was appointed deputy Erie County clerk, and in 2007, she was appointed Erie County clerk by Governor Eliot Spitzer. She was elected to a full term as clerk in 2007 and reelected in 2010. In May 2011, Hochul won a special election for New York's 26th congressional district, becoming the first Democrat to represent the district in 40 years. She served as a U.S. representative from 2011 to 2013. During her tenure, she co-sponsored bills to streamline passport acquisition, met with President Barack Obama on economic issues, and was one of 17 Democrats to join Republicans in a contempt of Congress resolution against Attorney General Eric Holder. She was narrowly defeated for reelection in 2012 by Chris Collins following redistricting. In the 2014 New York gubernatorial election, Governor Andrew Cuomo selected Hochul as his running mate. After they won the election, Hochul was inaugurated as lieutenant governor. Cuomo and Hochul were reelected in 2018. Hochul took office as governor of New York on August 24, 2021, after Cuomo resigned amid allegations of sexual harassment. She won a full term in the 2022 election against Republican U.S. Representative Lee Zeldin in the narrowest New York gubernatorial election since 1994.

name: JB Pritzker
education: Graduated from Duke University with a Bachelor of Arts in political science and earned a Juris Doctor from Northwestern University School of Law in 1993.
careerHistory: Served on legislative staffs for U.S. representatives and senators in the 1980s. Ran unsuccessfully for the U.S. House of Representatives in the 1998 Democratic primary. Chaired the Illinois Human Rights Commission from 2003 to 2006. Served as national co-chair for Hillary Clinton's 2008 presidential campaign. Elected as the 43rd Governor of Illinois in 2018, taking office in January 2019, and was reelected in 2022.
bio:
Jay Robert "JB" Pritzker (born January 19, 1965) is an American politician, lawyer, and businessman serving as the 43rd governor of Illinois since 2019. A member of the wealthy Pritzker family, which owns the Hyatt hotel chain, Pritzker graduated from Duke University and Northwestern University School of Law. Before entering electoral politics, he was a longtime active member and financial supporter of the Democratic Party. His early political involvement included serving on the legislative staffs of U.S. Representative Tom Lantos and U.S. Senators Terry Sanford and Alan J. Dixon in the 1980s, focusing on trade and transportation issues. He later founded Democratic Leadership for the 21st Century, an organization aimed at attracting younger voters to the Democratic Party.

Pritzker first sought elected office in 1998, running in the Democratic primary for Illinois's 9th congressional district. He finished third in a crowded and expensive primary. From 2003 to 2006, he chaired the Illinois Human Rights Commission under Governor Rod Blagojevich. In the 2008 presidential election, he served as national co-chair of Hillary Clinton's campaign and was a delegate to the 2008 and 2016 Democratic National Conventions.

Pritzker won the Democratic primary for governor of Illinois in the 2018 election and defeated Republican incumbent Bruce Rauner in the general election. He took office on January 14, 2019, and was reelected in 2022, defeating Republican Darren Bailey. During his governorship, Pritzker has focused on fiscal policy, education, healthcare, incentivizing clean energy, and criminal justice reform. Key policy achievements in his first term included the legalization of recreational cannabis, the expansion of abortion access, and managing the state's response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

In his business career, Pritzker co-founded Pritzker Group Private Capital, where he serves as managing partner. He also co-founded Chicago Ventures and funded the startups Techstars Chicago and Built in Chicago. He served as chairman of ChicagoNEXT, Mayor Rahm Emanuel's Council on Innovation and Technology, and founded 1871, a nonprofit digital startup incubator. According to Forbes, his estimated net worth is $3.9 billion as of August 2025.

name: Zohran Mamdani
education: Graduated from the Bronx High School of Science in 2010. Received a bachelor's degree in Africana studies from Bowdoin College in 2014.
careerHistory: Worked as a housing counselor and musician. Entered local politics as a campaign manager for Khader El-Yateem and Ross Barkan. Served as a member of the New York State Assembly for the 36th district from 2021 to 2025. Elected Mayor of New York City in November 2025, sworn in on January 1, 2026.
bio:
Zohran Kwame Mamdani (born October 18, 1991) is an American politician who has served as the 112th mayor of New York City since 2026. A member of the Democratic Party and the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), he is New York's first Muslim and Asian American mayor. Mamdani was born in Kampala, Uganda, to Indian parents, academic Mahmood Mamdani and filmmaker Mira Nair. He lived in Cape Town, South Africa, before moving to the United States at age seven, settling in New York City. He graduated from the Bronx High School of Science and earned a bachelor's degree in Africana studies from Bowdoin College in 2014, where he co-founded the school's chapter of Students for Justice in Palestine.

Before entering politics, Mamdani worked as a housing counselor and as a musician. Under the moniker Young Cardamom, he composed and performed rap music, often collaborating with Ugandan rapper HAB. He curated and produced the soundtrack for the 2016 film 'Queen of Katwe' and was nominated for a Guild of Music Supervisors Award.

Mamdani entered New York City politics as a volunteer in 2015 and joined the NYC-DSA in 2017. He worked as a campaign manager for Khader El-Yateem and Ross Barkan and was a field organizer for Tiffany Cabán's 2019 campaign. He was first elected to the New York State Assembly in 2020, defeating incumbent Aravella Simotas in the Democratic primary to represent the 36th district (Astoria and Long Island City, Queens). He was reelected without opposition in 2022 and 2024.

In October 2024, Mamdani announced his candidacy for mayor of New York City in the 2025 election, becoming the first mayoral candidate whose political career originated in Queens. A democratic socialist, he campaigned on a progressive platform supporting fare-free city buses, universal public child care, city-owned grocery stores, a rent freeze on rent-stabilized units, additional affordable housing, and a $30 minimum wage by 2030. He also expressed support for LGBTQ rights, comprehensive public safety reform, and tax increases on corporations and high earners. He won the Democratic primary in June 2025, defeating former governor Andrew Cuomo, and was elected mayor in the November general election. He was sworn in on January 1, 2026.

name: Karen Bass
education: Studied philosophy at San Diego State University (1971-1973), graduated from the physician assistant program at USC Keck School of Medicine (1982), earned a Bachelor of Science in health sciences from California State University, Dominguez Hills (1990), and received a Master of Social Work from USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work (2015).
careerHistory: Elected to California State Assembly (2004-2010), serving as Speaker from 2008. Served in U.S. House of Representatives (2011-2022), representing California's 33rd and later 37th congressional districts. Elected as 43rd Mayor of Los Angeles in 2022.
bio:
Karen Ruth Bass (born October 3, 1953) is an American politician serving as the 43rd mayor of Los Angeles since 2022, the first woman to hold the position. A member of the Democratic Party, her political career spans state and federal levels. Before entering politics, Bass worked as a physician assistant and clinical instructor at the USC Keck School of Medicine after graduating from its physician assistant program in 1982. She also earned a Bachelor of Science in health sciences from California State University, Dominguez Hills in 1990. In the late 1980s, she co-founded Community Coalition, a grassroots organization in South Los Angeles.

Bass began her political career in the California State Assembly, elected in 2004 to represent the 47th district. At her inauguration, she was the only African-American woman in the state legislature. She was re-elected in 2006 and 2008. During her tenure, Speaker Fabian Núñez appointed her as majority whip for the 2005–06 session and majority floor leader for the 2007–08 session. As vice chair of the Legislative Black Caucus, she commissioned the first "State of Black California" report.

In 2008, Bass was elected the 67th Speaker of the California State Assembly, becoming the first African-American woman in U.S. history to lead a state legislative body. Her speakership coincided with a severe budget crisis. She negotiated to address a multi-billion dollar shortfall, an effort for which she, along with three colleagues, received the 2010 Profile in Courage Award. As speaker, she promoted laws to improve the child welfare system, expanded Healthy Families Insurance Coverage for children, worked on tax code reform via the California Commission on the 21st-Century Economy, and secured funding for local projects including the Vision Theater and the Los Angeles Unified School District.

Bass was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2010, representing California's 33rd congressional district initially, then the 37th district after 2012 redistribution. She served until 2022. During her congressional tenure, she chaired the Congressional Black Caucus for the 116th Congress (2019–2021) and served as chair of the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime, Terrorism, Homeland Security and Investigations and the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Africa, Global Health, and Human Rights. She also founded and co-chaired the Congressional Caucus on Foster Youth. While in Congress, she earned a Master of Social Work from the USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work in 2015.

Bass won the 2022 Los Angeles mayoral election, making history as the city's first female mayor and first African-American woman to hold the office.

name: Brandon Johnson
education: Earned a bachelor's degree in youth development in 2004 and a master's degree in teaching in 2007, both from Aurora University.
careerHistory: 2007-2010: Social studies teacher at Jenner Academy Elementary in Chicago Public Schools. 2011: Became an organizer with the Chicago Teachers Union, helping organize the 2012 strike. 2018-2023: Served as Cook County Board of Commissioner for the 1st district. 2023–present: Serves as the 57th mayor of Chicago.
bio: Brandon Johnson (born March 27, 1976) is an American politician and former educator who has served as the 57th mayor of Chicago since 2023. A member of the Democratic Party, he began his political career on the Cook County Board of Commissioners, representing the 1st district from 2018 to 2023. Born and raised in Elgin, Illinois, Johnson earned a bachelor's degree in youth development and a master's degree in teaching from Aurora University. He started his professional career as a social studies teacher in the Chicago Public Schools system, working at Jenner Academy Elementary and later at George Westinghouse College Prep. During this time, he became an active member and organizer with the Chicago Teachers Union, helping to organize their 2012 strike. In his first run for public office in 2018, Johnson was elected to the Cook County Board of Commissioners, defeating the incumbent. He was reelected in 2022. As a commissioner, Johnson was the chief sponsor of the Just Housing Ordinance, which prohibited landlords from considering prospective tenants' criminal history. He also authored the "Justice for Black Lives" resolution in 2020, which called for reallocating funding from policing to public services. Johnson successfully ran for mayor of Chicago in 2023. In the first round of the election, he and Paul Vallas advanced to a runoff, unseating incumbent mayor Lori Lightfoot. Johnson subsequently defeated Vallas in the runoff. His campaign was supported by progressive groups and focused on funding for public schools, police reform, a real estate transfer tax to address homelessness, and raising new revenues through various taxes. Upon his election, he became the third black person to be elected mayor of Chicago and the first mayor to hail from the city's West Side since the 1930s. Throughout his political career, Johnson has been described as a political progressive. As mayor, his stated focuses include combating homelessness and enacting police and education reform.

name: Ron DeSantis
education: Graduated from Yale University with a B.A., magna cum laude, in 2001. Graduated from Harvard Law School with a J.D., cum laude, in 2005.
careerHistory: Commissioned as a U.S. Navy officer in 2004, serving as a legal advisor and special assistant U.S. attorney until his honorable discharge from active duty in 2010. Served as the U.S. Representative from Florida's 6th congressional district from 2013 to 2018. Elected as the 46th Governor of Florida in 2018, taking office in 2019. Announced candidacy for the 2024 Republican presidential nomination in May 2023, withdrawing in January 2024.
bio:
Ronald Dion DeSantis (born September 14, 1978) is an American politician, attorney, and former naval officer serving since 2019 as the 46th governor of Florida. A member of the Republican Party, he previously served as the U.S. representative from Florida's 6th congressional district from 2013 to 2018.

DeSantis was born in Jacksonville, Florida. He graduated magna cum laude from Yale University in 2001 with a Bachelor of Arts in history, where he captained the varsity baseball team. He then earned a Juris Doctor, cum laude, from Harvard Law School in 2005.

In 2004, DeSantis was commissioned as an officer in the U.S. Navy Judge Advocate General's Corps. His service included advising SEAL Team One, a deployment to Iraq in 2007 as part of the troop surge, and work at the Guantanamo Bay detention camp in 2006. He was appointed as a special assistant U.S. attorney in the Middle District of Florida before his honorable discharge from active duty in 2010. He continued in the Navy Reserve, achieving the rank of lieutenant commander. His military awards include the Bronze Star Medal and the Navy and Marine Corps Commendation Medal.

DeSantis was first elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2012, aligning with the Tea Party movement, and was reelected in 2014 and 2016. During his tenure, he became a founding member of the Freedom Caucus. He briefly ran for U.S. Senate in 2016 but withdrew when incumbent Marco Rubio sought reelection.

In 2018, DeSantis won the Republican nomination and was elected Governor of Florida, defeating Democrat Andrew Gillum by a narrow margin. His governorship has included the state's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and major hurricanes. He championed legislation such as the Parental Rights in Education Act and signed the Heartbeat Protection Act. In the 2022 gubernatorial election, he was reelected by a large margin, defeating former governor Charlie Crist.

During his second term, DeSantis established the Florida Department of Commerce and the Florida Department of Government Efficiency, and signed Florida Senate Bill 266. He announced his candidacy for the 2024 Republican presidential nomination on May 24, 2023, but withdrew from the race on January 21, 2024, and endorsed former President Donald Trump.

name: Greg Abbott
education: Graduated from the University of Texas at Austin with a Bachelor of Business Administration in finance in 1981. Earned a Juris Doctor from Vanderbilt University Law School in 1984.
careerHistory: 1996-2001: Justice of the Texas Supreme Court. 2002-2015: 50th Attorney General of Texas. 2015-present: 48th Governor of Texas.
bio:
Gregory Wayne Abbott (born November 13, 1957) is an American politician, attorney, and jurist who has served as the 48th governor of Texas since 2015. A member of the Republican Party, his political career includes serving as the 50th attorney general of Texas from 2002 to 2015 and as a justice of the Texas Supreme Court from 1996 to 2001. As of 2025, Abbott is the longest-serving incumbent governor in the United States.

Abbott was born in Wichita Falls, Texas. He earned a Bachelor of Business Administration in finance from the University of Texas at Austin in 1981 and a Juris Doctor from Vanderbilt University Law School in 1984. He then worked in private practice for the law firm Butler and Binion, LLP from 1984 to 1992. His judicial career began in Houston, where he served as a state trial judge on the 129th District Court for three years. In 1995, Governor George W. Bush appointed him to the Texas Supreme Court; he was subsequently elected to full terms in 1996 and 1998.

Abbott was elected Texas Attorney General in 2002 and was reelected in 2006 and 2010, becoming the longest-serving attorney general in state history. In this role, he notably advocated for the display of the Ten Commandments at the Texas State Capitol, a position upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court in the 2005 case Van Orden v. Perry. He also defended the state's ban on same-sex marriage and was involved in numerous lawsuits against the Obama administration, challenging the Affordable Care Act and various environmental regulations. He established a Fugitive Unit to track sex offenders and a unit to pursue voter-fraud prosecutions.

Elected governor in 2014, Abbott is the first Texas governor and third U.S. state governor to use a wheelchair. As governor, he has promoted a conservative agenda including maintaining Texas's abortion ban, supporting lenient gun laws, backing law enforcement funding, and pursuing election reform. During the COVID-19 pandemic, he opposed mask and vaccine mandates and blocked local entities from implementing their own. In response to the 2021 winter storm power crisis, he called for reforms to the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) and signed legislation requiring power plant weatherization. He has also prioritized border security, initiating Operation Lone Star in 2021 to combat illegal immigration.

name: Sarah Huckabee Sanders
education: Graduated from Ouachita Baptist University in 2004 with a Bachelor of Arts degree, majoring in political science and minoring in mass communications.
careerHistory: Regional liaison for congressional affairs at the U.S. Department of Education under President George W. Bush. Senior advisor on Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign. White House deputy press secretary (2017) and then White House press secretary (2017-2019). Elected 47th Governor of Arkansas in 2023.
bio:
Sarah Elizabeth Huckabee Sanders (born August 13, 1982) is an American politician serving as the 47th governor of Arkansas since 2023. A member of the Republican Party, she is the daughter of former Arkansas governor Mike Huckabee. Before becoming governor, she served as the 31st White House press secretary under President Donald Trump from 2017 to 2019, the third woman to hold that position. She also served as a senior advisor on Trump's 2016 presidential campaign.

Sanders was born in Little Rock, Arkansas, and graduated from Ouachita Baptist University in 2004 with a Bachelor of Arts in political science. Her early political career began with involvement in her father's campaigns, including his 1992 Senate bid and his 2002 gubernatorial reelection campaign. She worked as a regional liaison for congressional affairs at the U.S. Department of Education under President George W. Bush and as a field coordinator for Bush's 2004 reelection campaign in Ohio. She was a founding partner of the Republican consulting firm Second Street Strategies and served as national political director for her father's 2008 presidential campaign. Sanders also worked as a senior adviser to Tim Pawlenty's 2012 presidential run and was involved in the campaigns of Arkansas U.S. Senators John Boozman and Tom Cotton. In 2010, she was named one of Time magazine's "40 under 40" in politics.

In the Trump administration, Sanders initially served as deputy White House press secretary before being promoted to press secretary in July 2017. As press secretary, she was the spokesperson for the administration's policy decisions and had a confrontational relationship with the White House press corps. She hosted fewer press conferences than any of the 13 previous press secretaries. During the Mueller probe, she admitted to investigators that she had made false statements in her role. She left the position in June 2019.

In January 2021, Sanders announced her candidacy for governor of Arkansas, with Trump's endorsement. She secured the Republican nomination in May 2022 and won the general election, defeating Democratic nominee Chris Jones. Upon taking office in 2023, she became the first woman to serve as governor of Arkansas, the first woman to be governor of a state of which her father was also governor, and the youngest current governor in the United States. She is the author of the New York Times bestseller "Speaking for Myself," a former Fox News Channel contributor, and has served on the Fulbright board.

name: Brian Kemp
education: Graduated from the University of Georgia in 1987 with a major in agriculture.
careerHistory: Served as a member of the Georgia State Senate from 2003 to 2007. Appointed and served as Georgia's Secretary of State from 2010 to 2018. Elected as the 83rd Governor of Georgia in 2019 and reelected to a second term in 2022.
bio:
Brian Porter Kemp (born November 2, 1963) is an American politician serving as the 83rd governor of Georgia since 2019. A member of the Republican Party, Kemp is a graduate of the University of Georgia, where he majored in agriculture. Before entering politics, he operated several businesses in agriculture, financial services, and real estate, working as a home builder and developer and founding Kemp Properties, a property management and real estate investment business.

Kemp's political career began with his election to the Georgia State Senate in 2002, where he served from 2003 to 2007. In 2006, he ran unsuccessfully for commissioner of the Georgia Department of Agriculture, losing the Republican primary runoff. In 2010, Governor Sonny Perdue appointed him as Georgia's 27th Secretary of State. Kemp was elected to a full term later that year and was reelected in 2014. During his tenure as Secretary of State, he faced criticism after a data breach of over six million voters' personal information in 2015. During the 2016 election, he was the only state official to reject help from the Department of Homeland Security to guard against Russian interference, rejecting the U.S. Intelligence Community's conclusion on the matter.

Kemp ran for governor in 2018, refusing to resign as secretary of state while campaigning, which stirred controversy. He narrowly defeated Democratic nominee Stacey Abrams, who accused him of voter suppression, though news outlets and experts found no evidence it affected the result. Kemp resigned as secretary of state shortly after the election. As governor, he opposed face mask mandates and stay-at-home orders during the COVID-19 pandemic and prohibited localities from implementing stricter public health measures than the state. After the 2020 presidential election in Georgia, he faced criticism from President Donald Trump for certifying the state's results in accordance with the law.

In 2021, Kemp signed the Election Integrity Act of 2021 into law. During his 2022 reelection campaign, he defeated a primary challenge from former U.S. Senator David Perdue, who was endorsed by Trump, and then defeated Abrams again in the general election by a wider margin. Kemp was sworn in for a second term on January 12, 2023. He is the first Republican since Reconstruction to be elected governor of Georgia who was not a former Democrat.

name: Glenn Youngkin
education: Attended Rice University, graduating in 1990 with a Bachelor of Arts in managerial studies and a Bachelor of Science in mechanical engineering. Earned an MBA from Harvard Business School in 1994.
careerHistory: 1990-1992: Investment banker at First Boston (later Credit Suisse First Boston). 1994: Management consultant at McKinsey & Company. 1995-2020: Various roles at The Carlyle Group, including Partner and Managing Director (1999), interim CFO (2010-2011), COO (2011-2014), President and COO (2014-2017), and co-CEO (2018-2020). 2022-present: 74th Governor of Virginia.
bio:
Glenn Allen Youngkin (born December 9, 1966) is an American politician and businessman serving as the 74th governor of Virginia since 2022. A member of the Republican Party, he spent 25 years at the private-equity firm The Carlyle Group, where he rose to become co-CEO in 2018. He resigned from that position in 2020 to run for governor.

Youngkin was born in Richmond, Virginia. He attended Rice University on a basketball scholarship, graduating in 1990 with degrees in managerial studies and mechanical engineering. He later earned an MBA from Harvard Business School in 1994. After business school, he worked at McKinsey & Company before joining The Carlyle Group in 1995. His career there included roles as a partner, managing director, chief operating officer, and president, culminating in his appointment as co-CEO in 2018. He retired from Carlyle in September 2020.

In January 2021, Youngkin declared his candidacy for the Republican nomination for Governor of Virginia. He won the nomination at the state convention in May 2021 and defeated former Democratic governor Terry McAuliffe in the general election, becoming Virginia's first Republican governor since Bob McDonnell in 2009.

As governor, Youngkin supported COVID-19 vaccination efforts but opposed vaccine mandates and banned mask mandates in Virginia public schools, a ban later partially rescinded after legal challenges. During his first year, he signed a bipartisan state budget that increased education spending alongside tax cuts. His term has included signing a Democratic-passed bill to protect same-sex marriage, repealing protections for transgender students in schools, and unsuccessfully advocating for abortion restrictions following the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision. He has opposed liberalizing recreational marijuana laws while signing a bill to ease the medical marijuana registration process.

Due to Virginia's term limits, Youngkin cannot run for re-election in 2025. He is scheduled to leave office on January 17, 2026, and will be succeeded by Democrat Abigail Spanberger.

name: John Whitmire
education: Attended the University of Houston to study political science. Began law studies at the Bates College of Law (now University of Houston Law Center) but did not graduate, passing the bar in 1981.
careerHistory: Texas House of Representatives (1973–1983). Texas State Senate (1983–2023). Mayor of Houston (2024–present).
bio:
John Harris Whitmire (born August 13, 1949) is an American attorney and politician who has served as the 63rd mayor of Houston, Texas, since 2024. Whitmire was born in Hillsboro, Texas, and moved to North Houston as a teenager, attending Waltrip High School. He studied political science at the University of Houston, paying for his education by working for the Texas State Welfare Department.

Whitmire's political career began in 1973 when he was elected as a Democratic member of the Texas House of Representatives, serving until 1983. He was inspired to run by his political science professor, who showed him the newly drawn single-member district lines encompassing his neighborhood. During his tenure in the House, he finished his undergraduate degree and began law studies, passing the bar in 1981 while still serving.

In 1983, Whitmire was elected to the Texas State Senate, representing District 15, which included much of northern Houston. He served in the Senate until 2023, becoming its longest-serving member. In 1993, he was appointed Chair of the Senate Criminal Justice Committee by Lieutenant Governor Bob Bullock, overseeing reforms to the penal code and increased prison construction. He also served as acting governor of Texas for a single day in 1993 as part of a tradition. Notably, in 2011, he successfully pushed the Texas Department of Criminal Justice to end the practice of last meal requests for death row inmates after an incident involving a convicted murderer. In 2003, he was part of the "Texas Eleven," a group of Democrats who fled to New Mexico to prevent redistricting legislation, though he ultimately returned, allowing the Republican-favored maps to pass.

In November 2021, Whitmire announced his candidacy for mayor of Houston in the 2023 election. The race became a de facto contest between him and U.S. Representative Sheila Jackson Lee. Whitmire's campaign focused on public safety, pledging to bring state troopers to assist the Houston Police Department. After advancing to a runoff, he won by a wide margin on December 9, 2023. He resigned from the State Senate on December 31, 2023, and assumed the mayoral office in 2024.

As mayor, one of his first actions was to order the removal of recently installed safety improvements on Houston Avenue, a project that cost $100,000 to install and $730,000 to reverse. He has also spoken out against "anti-car activists" and directed the removal of specific bike safety infrastructure, including barriers on Heights Blvd, a raised crosswalk on Westheimer Rd, and a bi-directional bike lane on Austin St.

name: Francis Suarez
education: Graduated from Florida International University (FIU) with a bachelor's degree in finance, then earned a J.D. cum laude from the University of Florida Fredric G. Levin College of Law in 2004.
careerHistory: Served as a member of the Miami City Commission representing District 4 from 2009 to 2017. Elected as the 43rd mayor of Miami in 2017 and re-elected in 2021, serving until 2025. Worked as an attorney at Greenspoon Marder after law school, then joined Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan's Miami office in 2021. Was a candidate in the 2024 Republican Party presidential primaries but withdrew.
bio:
Francis Xavier Suarez (born October 6, 1977) is an American lawyer and politician who served as the 43rd mayor of Miami from 2017 to 2025. A member of the Republican Party, he is the son of former Miami mayor Xavier Suarez. Suarez earned a bachelor's degree in finance from Florida International University, graduating in the top 10% of his class, and received his J.D. degree cum laude from the University of Florida Fredric G. Levin College of Law in 2004.

His political career began when he was first elected to represent the 4th district on the Miami City Commission in a 2009 special election, winning a runoff. He was reelected unopposed in 2011 and 2015, serving until 2017. As a commissioner, his policy results were described as mixed. He successfully introduced a motion that decreased city employee salaries and advocated for zoning code changes aimed at easing affordable housing construction. However, he was unsuccessful in an effort to move the city from a weak mayor to a strong mayor form of government. He was an opponent of red light cameras in the city.

Suarez launched a campaign for mayor in the 2013 election against incumbent Tomás Regalado, focusing on increasing emergency financial reserves, helping small businesses, strengthening the police department, and elevating the city's national prominence. His campaign was impacted by scandals involving staffers who pleaded guilty to misdemeanors related to absentee ballot requests. He withdrew from the race in August 2013, citing mistakes made by his campaign team.

He was elected mayor in the 2017 election, becoming Miami's first local-born mayor and the first mayor not born in Cuba since 1996. He was re-elected in 2021, receiving over 78% of the vote. Miami's mayoralty is a part-time position with limited powers under a weak mayor system, including a veto over city commission legislation and the ability to hire and fire the city manager (subject to commission override). Despite the position's limited statutory power, Suarez positioned himself as a high-profile figure in city government.

During his mayoralty, he was noted for his advocacy for cryptocurrency. He also held leadership roles in the United States Conference of Mayors, serving as second vice president (2020), first vice president (2021), and president from June 2022 to June 2023. Suarez was a candidate in the 2024 Republican Party presidential primaries but withdrew after failing to qualify for the first primary debate.

In his private legal career, Suarez worked as an attorney specializing in corporate and real estate transactions at Greenspoon Marder and later at the Miami office of Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, taking unpaid leave in 2023 due to his presidential candidacy.

name: Mattie Parker
education: Graduated in 2006 with a Bachelor of Arts in Government from the University of Texas at Austin. Graduated in 2012 with a Juris Doctor from the Texas Wesleyan University School of Law.
careerHistory: Press assistant, then deputy press secretary and executive assistant for Texas House Speaker Tom Craddick (during college and after 2006). Legislative director and chief of staff for Texas Rep. Phil King (2007-2010). Campaign manager for U.S. Rep. Kay Granger while in law school, later her district director (2012-2014). Associate attorney at Harris, Finley & Bogle, P.C. (2014). Chief of Staff for the Mayor and Fort Worth City Council (2015-2020). Founding CEO of Fort Worth Cradle to Career/Tarrant To & Through Partnership (2020-July 2021). Elected 45th Mayor of Fort Worth (June 2021-present, re-elected 2023 and 2025).
bio:
Mattie Parker (born November 9, 1983) is an American politician, businesswoman, and attorney serving as the 45th Mayor of Fort Worth, Texas. She was elected in 2021 and re-elected in 2023 and 2025. Although Fort Worth's mayoral elections are nonpartisan, Parker is affiliated with the Republican Party. She succeeded Betsy Price, who served five consecutive terms and endorsed Parker, her former chief of staff.

Parker was born in Hico, Texas, and graduated from Hico High School in 2002. She earned a Bachelor of Arts in Government from the University of Texas at Austin in 2006 and a Juris Doctor from Texas Wesleyan University School of Law in 2012, later admitted to the State Bar of Texas in 2013.

Her political career began during her junior year at university as a press assistant in Texas House Speaker Tom Craddick's office, later becoming his deputy press secretary and executive assistant. Between 2007 and 2010, she served as legislative director and chief of staff to Texas Representative Phil King. While in law school, she was campaign manager for U.S. Representative Kay Granger. She later became Granger's district director before working as an associate attorney at Harris, Finley & Bogle, P.C.

From 2015 to April 2020, Parker served as Chief of Staff for the Mayor and the Fort Worth City Council. She then became the founding CEO of Fort Worth Cradle to Career and the Tarrant To & Through (T3) Partnership, nonprofits focused on postsecondary education, leaving the position after her mayoral victory but remaining on the board.

In the 2021 mayoral election, Parker placed second in the first round before winning a runoff against Deborah Peoples with 53.5% of the vote, becoming Fort Worth's first millennial mayor and the youngest mayor among the 25 largest U.S. cities. Her campaign raised and spent over $1.98 million, a record for Fort Worth mayoral races.

As mayor, Parker has prioritized education reform, aiming for equitable educational opportunities across Fort Worth's twelve school districts and aiding in hiring a new Fort Worth ISD Superintendent. She secured a federal allocation of $400 million for the Central City Flood Control Project. In association with the Texas Blockchain Council, she also helped Fort Worth become the first U.S. city to mine bitcoin.

Parker is married to David Parker, a registered lobbyist, and they have three children.
